records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me that the People of the Book say: 'Ḥaḍramawt ibn Qaḥṭān ibn ‘Ābir, who is Hūd, and they say: Sabā’ ibn Qaḥṭān ibn ‘Ābir, who is Hūd.'
records.text_ar: وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، قَالَ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ يَقُولُونَ: " حَضْرَمَوْتُ ⦗ص: 36⦘ بْنُ قَحْطَانَ بْنِ عَابِرٍ، وَهُوَ هُودٌ، وَيَقُولُونَ: سَبَأُ بْنُ قَحْطَانَ بْنِ عَابِرٍ، وَهُوَ هُودٌ "

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah said: Abū Hurayrah used to [the Arabic text is damaged here] a man and ask him where he was from. If he said, “From Judhām,” Abū Hurayrah would say: “Welcome, in-laws of Moses and people of Shuʿayb.”

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah said ‘Amr ibn Jābir al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to me that he heard Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sā‘idī, a companion of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Do not curse Tubba‘, for he had embraced Islam.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah said Abū al-Aswad narrated to me that he heard Abū Bakr ibn Sulaymān ibn Abī Ḥathmah say: 'We did not find in the knowledge of any scholar or the poetry of any poet anyone who knows what is beyond Ma‘d ibn ‘Adnān.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me that ‘Ā’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ, said 'We did not find anyone who knows what is beyond Ma‘d ibn ‘Adnān or what is beyond Qaḥṭān except as mere conjecture.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Hammad ibn al-Saʾib al-Kinani, who said that Humayd said: “Hud, Shuʿayb, Salih, Ishmael, and Muhammad the Prophet are prophets from among the Arabs.”

records.text_en: He said: Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from Bakr ibn Sawadah al-Judhami, who said: “A man from ʿAd came to ʿAli ibn Abi Talib. ʿAli asked him, ‘Where are you from?’ He replied, ‘Mahrah.’ ʿAli recited: ‘And remember the brother of ʿAd, when he warned his people among the sand dunes’ [Qurʾan 46:21].” Ibn Lahiʿah added: “Hud’s grave is in Mahrah.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ سَوَادَةَ الْجُذَامِيِّ، قَالَ: " أَتَى رَجُلٌ مِنْ عَادٍ إِلَى عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ فَقَالَ لَهُ: مِمَّنْ أَنْتَ؟ فَقَالَ: مِنْ مَهْرَةَ، فَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ: " {وَاذْكُرْ أَخَا عَادٍ إِذْ أَنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِالْأَحْقَافِ} [الأحقاف: 21] " قَالَ ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ: قَبْرُ هُودٍ فِي مَهْرَةَ

records.raw_text_en: Maslamah ibn ‘Alī reported to me from Zayd ibn Wāqid, who narrated to me from Busr ibn ‘Ubayd God, from Wāthilah ibn al-Asqa‘, who said 'I was among the People of the Bench, and I saw us when none of us had a complete garment. The sweat had made tracks on our skins from dust and dirt. One day, the Messenger of God, ﷺ, came out and said: Rejoice, O poor emigrants, three times. We said: We are as you see. Then a man with a handsome appearance came—I do not know when I have seen a man more impressive—until he recited to the Messenger of God, ﷺ. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, did not speak a word without the man feeling compelled to respond with something that surpassed the Messenger’s words. When he left, the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: God does not love this. Those who twist their tongues for people like cows twist their tongues in the pasture. Thus, God will twist their tongues and faces in Hell on the Day of Resurrection.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from ‘Uqayl ibn Khālid, from Ibn Shihāb, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭ‘im, that Jubayr ibn Muṭ‘im informed him that he heard ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb standing on the pulpit say: 'Learn your lineages and maintain your ties of kinship. By God, there may be something between a man and his brother, but if he knew the kinship between them, it would deter him from destruction.'
records.text_ar: وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنْ عُقَيْلِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ مُطْعِمٍ، أَنَّ جُبَيْرَ بْنَ مُطْعِمٍ، أَخْبَرَهُ، أَنَّهُ، سَمِعَ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ يَقُولُ: «تَعَلَّمُوا أَنْسَابَكُمْ، وَصِلُوا أَرْحَامَكُمْ، وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَيَكُونَ بَيْنَ الرَّجُلِ وَأَخِيهِ الشَّيْءُ وَلَوْ عَلِمَ الَّذِي بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهُ مِنْ دُخْلَةِ الرَّحِمِ ⦗ص: 47⦘ لَوَزِعَهُ ذَلِكَ عَنِ التَّهْلُكَةِ»

records.text_en: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd reported to me from ʿUqayl ibn Khalid, from Ibn Shihab, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Whoever disowns his child will come on the Day of Resurrection with his two ends bound together.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي اللَّيْثُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ عُقَيْلِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «مَنْ تَبَرَّأَ مِنْ وَلَدِهِ أَتَى يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مَعْقُودًا بَيْنَ طَرَفَيْهِ»

records.text_en: Al-Harith ibn Nabhan reported to me from 'Asim Al-Ahwal, from Abu 'Uthman, from Sa'd and Abu Bakrah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Whoever claims a lineage other than his father's, knowing that he is not his father, God will forbid Paradise for him.'

records.text_en: Someone who heard al-Awzaʿi say reported to me that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: “I wish my father were like Bilal’s father, my mother like Bilal’s mother, and I were like Bilal.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مَنْ، سَمِعَ الْأَوْزَاعِيَّ، يَقُولُ: قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ: «لَوَدِدْتُ أَنَّ أَبِي مِثْلُ أَبِي بِلَالٍ، وَأُمِّي مِثْلُ أُمِّ بِلَالٍ، وَأَنَا مِثْلُ بِلَالٍ، قَضَى كَذَلِكَ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مَنْ، سَمِعَ الْأَوْزَاعِيَّ، يَقُولُ: قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ: «لَوَدِدْتُ أَنَّ أَبِي مِثْلُ أَبِي بِلَالٍ، وَأُمِّي مِثْلُ أُمِّ بِلَالٍ، وَأَنَا مِثْلُ بِلَالٍ، قَضَى كَذَلِكَ»

records.text_en: Yahya ibn Ayyub reported to me from Zabban ibn Faʾid, from Sahl ibn Muʿadh, from his father, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Among God’s servants are people to whom He will not speak on the Day of Resurrection, whom He will not purify or cleanse, and upon whom He will not look.” They asked: “Who are they, Messenger of God?” He replied: “One who rejects his parents out of aversion to them; one who disowns his child; and a man whom people have favored, but who denies their favor and disowns them.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ زَبَّانَ بْنِ فَائِدٍ، عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «مِنَ الْعِبَادِ عِبَادٌ لَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ، وَلَا يُطَهِّرُهُمْ، وَلَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ» ، قَالُوا: مَنْ أُولَئِكِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟، قَالَ: «الْمُتَبَرِّئُ مِنْ وَالِدَيْهِ رَغْبَةً عَنْهُمَا، وَالْمُتَبَرِّئُ مِنْ وَلَدِهِ، وَرَجُلٌ أَنْعَمَ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ فَكَفَرَ نِعْمَتَهُمْ وَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُمْ»

records.raw_text_en: Yahya ibn Ayyub reported to me from Zabban ibn Fa'id, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh, from his father, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Among the servants are those whom God will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, nor look at them.' They asked: 'Who are they, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'The one who disowns his parents out of aversion to them, the one who disowns his children, and the man who was granted a favor by people but denied their favor and disowned them.'

records.text_en: Jarir ibn Hazim reported to me from Al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah, from Al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, from Mujahid, from 'Abdullah ibn Sakhbarah, from Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, that he said 'Whoever disowns a lineage, even if distant, has disbelieved in God, and whoever claims a lineage that is not known has disbelieved in God.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عُمَارَةَ، عَنِ الْحَكَمِ بْنِ عُتَيْبَةَ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَخْبَرَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مَنْ تَبَرَّأَ مِنْ نَسَبٍ وَإِنْ دَقَّ، وَكَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مَنِ ادَّعَى عَلَى نَسَبٍ لَا يُعْرَفُ»

records.text_en: Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from Ibn Hubayrah, from ʿAlqamah ibn …, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, was asked: “What is Sabaʾ—a place, a man, or a woman?” He replied: “Rather, it was a man who had ten children. Six settled in Yemen and four in Syria. The Yemenis are Madhhij, Kindah, al-Azd, the Ashʿariyyun, Anmar, and all of Himyar. The Syrian tribes are Lakhm, Judham, Ghassan, and ʿAmilah.”

records.text_en: Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from Tawbah …, who told him: “We were with ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman in Ifriqiyah. One day he said, ‘Whenever a people settle in a land, they are counted among its people.’ ʿAli ibn Rabah objected: ‘No. So-and-so told me that Farwah ibn Musayk al-Ghutayfi came to the Messenger of God, pledged allegiance to him upon Islam, and was given a banner. Farwah pledged to fight those who turned away. Later Farwah returned and said, “Prophet of God, Sabaʾ were a people of great standing in pre-Islamic times, and I fear they may turn away from Islam. Should I fight them?” He replied, “I have not yet received any instruction concerning them.” Then the verse was revealed: “There was indeed a sign for Sabaʾ in their homeland: two gardens…” [Qurʾan 34:15 and following]. A man asked, “Messenger of God, what is Sabaʾ?”’” The narrator then related a report like Ibn Hubayrah’s.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنْ تَوْبَةَ. . . . . .، أَخْبَرَهُ وَكُنَّا، عِنْدَ ⦗ص: 60⦘ عُبَيْدَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بِإِفْرِيقِيَةَ، فَقَالَ يَوْمًا: " مَا أَطَرَ قَوْمٌ بِأَرْضٍ إِلَّا وَهُمْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا، فَقَالَ عُلَيُّ بْنُ رَبَاحٍ: كَلَّا قَدْ حَدَّثَنِي فُلَانٌ، أَنَّ فَرْوَةَ بْنَ مُسَيْكٍ الْغُطَيْفِيَّ، " قَدِمَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَبَايَعَهُ عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ، وَعَقَدَ لَهُ رَايَةً، فَبَايَعَهُ فَرْوَةُ عَلَى أَنْ يُقَاتِلَ مَنْ أَدْبَرَ. ثُمَّ إِنَّ فَرْوَةَ رَجَعَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ سَبَأَ قَوْمٌ كَانَ لَهُمْ عِزٌّ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، وَإِنِّي أَخْشَى أَنْ يُدْبِرُوا عَن الْإِسْلَامِ، أَفَأُقَاتِلُهُمْ؟ فَقَالَ: " مَا أُمِرْتُ فِيهِمْ بِشَيْءٍ بَعْدُ، فَأُنْزِلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ: {لَقَدْ كَانَ لِسَبَإٍ فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ آيَةٌ جَنَّتَانِ} [سبأ: 15] الْآيَاتُ فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَا سَبَأٌ؟ " ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ مِثْلَ حَدِيثِ ابْنِ هُبَيْرَةَ

records.text_en: Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from Maʿruf ibn Suwayd al-Judhami, from Abu ʿUshshanah, a companion of Ibn Wahb, that he heard ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir say: “One day I was with the Messenger of God, ﷺ, when he said: ‘Whoever here is descended from Maʿadd, let him stand.’ I stood, and he said, ‘Sit down.’ He repeated this two or three times. I asked, ‘Then from whom are we, Messenger of God?’ He replied, ‘You are from Qudaʿah ibn Malik ibn Himyar.’”

records.text_en: Mu‘āwiyah ibn Sālih reported to me from Yahyā ibn Sa‘īd, from Sa‘īd ibn al-Musayyib, who said 'Noah had three sons: Sām, Hām, and Yāfith. Sām was the father of the Arabs, Persians, and Romans, and there is good in all of them. Hām was the father of the Sudanese, Berbers, and Copts. Yāfith was the father of the Turks, Slavs, Ya’jūj, and Ma’jūj.'

records.raw_text_en: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Yūnus reported to me from Ibn Shihāb who said Kathīr ibn ‘Abbās ibn ‘Abd al-Muṭṭalib told me that ‘Abbās said: I witnessed the Battle of Ḥunayn with the Messenger of God, ﷺ. I and Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ‘Abd al-Muṭṭalib stayed close to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and did not leave him. The Messenger of God was on a white mule that Farwah ibn Nufāthah al-Judhāmī had gifted to him. When the Muslims and the disbelievers met, the Muslims turned and fled. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, began urging his mule towards the disbelievers. ‘Abbās said: I was holding the reins of the Messenger of God’s mule, restraining it so it would not rush, and Abū Sufyān was holding the stirrup of the Messenger of God. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'O ‘Abbās, call the companions of the Samurah tree.' By God, when they heard my voice, they turned like cows turning to their calves. The leaders came to the Messenger of God, and he returned their women and children to them. He divided the camels and sheep among those with him. Then the Messenger of God, ﷺ, returned from there with an ‘Umrah, and that was in Dhū al-Qa‘dah. On that day, he reconciled some men from Quraysh with some men from the Arabs. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, gave Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah one hundred camels, then another hundred, then another hundred. Ibn Shihāb said: Sa‘īd ibn al-Musayyib told me that Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah said: By God, the Messenger of God, ﷺ, gave me what he gave me, and he was the most hateful of people to me. But he kept giving me until he became the most beloved of people to me. He also gave Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām one hundred camels, then another hundred, then another hundred. Then the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to Ḥakīm: 'This wealth is fresh and sweet. Whoever takes it rightfully will be blessed in it, but whoever takes it with arrogance will not be blessed in it. He is like one who eats and is not satisfied. The upper hand is better than the lower hand.'... The Messenger of God, ﷺ, gave Rahrān one hundred camels that day, and he gave al-Aqra‘ ibn Ḥābis one hundred camels... The Messenger of God said: 'You may go to Medina.' When we arrived, Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq was appointed to lead the Hajj.

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi said: Sufyan al-Thawri reported to me from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Aslam, who said that ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud said: “If you knew my sins, not two of you would follow behind me; you would throw dust on my head. I wish God would forgive me one of my sins and that I were called ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawthah.”

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb said: Hisham ibn Saʿd reported to me from Saʿid al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “God has removed from you the arrogance and boasting about forefathers of the pre-Islamic age. A person is either a God-fearing believer or a wretched sinner. You are the children of Adam, and Adam was created from earth. Let people stop boasting about their peoples, who are merely charcoal from Hell; otherwise they will be more insignificant to God than dung beetles that push filth with their noses.”

matched_source_translation.english_text: Ibn Wahb said Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Sa‘īd al-Maqburī, from his father, from Abī Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Allāh has removed from you the arrogance of the Jāhiliyyah and its boasting about ancestors. A believer is pious, and a wicked person is miserable. You are the children of Ādam, and Ādam was from dust. Let men cease boasting about people, for they are merely coals from the coals of Hell, or they will be more insignificant to Allāh than the dung beetles that push filth with their noses.'

records.text_en: Hisham ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Someone remarked in the presence of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, “How knowledgeable so-and-so is!” The Messenger asked, “In what?” They replied, “In people’s genealogies.” He said: “Knowledge that brings no benefit, and ignorance that causes no harm.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ قَالَ: قِيلِ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَا أَعْلَمَ فُلَانًا؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «بِمَ؟» قِيلَ: بَأَنْسَابِ النَّاسِ. قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «عِلْمٌ لَا يَنْفَعُ، وَجَهَالَةٌ لَا تَضُرُّ»

records.raw_text_en: I heard Mālik ibn Anas say: ‘Abd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr told me that Ibn Abī Mulaykah told him: While ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was circumambulating the Ka‘bah, he saw a leprous woman and said to her: 'Do not harm the people.' She stayed in her house. When ‘Umar died, the people came to her and said: 'The one who forbade you from going out has died, so go out.' She said: 'By God, I will obey him while he is alive and disobey him when he is dead.'

records.text_en: Haywah ibn Shurayh and Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from Abu al-Aswad, from a freedman of Ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, who said: “One who is ungrateful to his patron is like one who is ungrateful for God’s favor.”

records.text_en: Sufyān al-Thawrī reported to me from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash, from Mūsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Khaṭmī, who reported from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hilāl al-ʿAbsī, from Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'The Muhājirūn and the Anṣār are allies of one another in this world and the Hereafter. The freedmen of Quraysh and the freedmen of Thaqīf are allies of one another in this world and the Hereafter.'

records.text_en: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith reported to me that Bakr ibn Sawādah informed him that Abū Sālim al-Jayshānī informed him from Abī Dharr that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to him: 'What do you think of Juʿayl?' I said: 'A poor man, like others.' He said: 'What do you think of so-and-so?' I said: 'A leader among the people.' He said: 'Juʿayl is better than the earth full of, or thousands of, or the like of, so-and-so.' I said: 'O Messenger of God, but so-and-so is like this, or do you treat him as you do?' He said: 'He is the leader of his people, so I seek to win them over through him.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، أَنَّ بَكْرَ بْنَ سَوَادَةَ حَدَّثَهُ، أَنَّ أَبَا سَالِمٍ الْجَيْشَانِيَّ حَدَّثَهُ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ لَهُ: «كَيْفَ تَرَى جُعَيْلًا؟» قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ: مِسْكِينًا كَشَكْلِهِ مِنَ النَّاسِ. قَالَ: «فَكَيْفَ تَرَى فُلَانًا؟» قُلْتُ: سَيِّدًا مِنْ سَادَاتِ النَّاسِ. قَالَ: «فَجُعَيْلٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مِلْءِ الْأَرْضِ أَوْ آلَافٍ أَوْ نَحْوِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ فُلَانٍ» . قَالَ: قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، فَفُلَانٌ هَكَذَا أَوْ أَنْتَ تَصْنَعُ بِهِ مَا تَصْنَعُ؟ فَقَالَ: إِنَّهُ رَأْسُ قَوْمِهِ، فَأَنَا أَتَأَلَّفُهُمْ فِيهِ "

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah, who said 'The Anṣār flogged a son of Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām for saying to the people of Yemen: You are not from the descendants of Ismāʿīl.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ غَزِيَّةَ، قَالَ: " جَلَدَتِ الْأَنْصَارُ ابْنًا لِيُوسُفَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَلَامٍ الْحَدَّ لِأَنَّهُ قَالَ لِأَهْلِ الْيَمَنِ: إِنَّكُمْ لَسْتُمْ مِنْ وَلَدِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ "

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Ibn Anʿam, from the brother of Bakr ibn Sawādah al-Judhāmī, who informed him that he heard ʿUlayy ibn Rabāḥ say: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'All the Arabs are from the descendants of Ismāʿīl and Ibrāhīm... They are from Thamūd and tribes from Ḥimyar... They are from Tubbaʿ.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rāshid al-Zawfī, that he heard Rabīʿah ibn Qays al-Ḥimlalī say: 'I was sitting with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib one day when I heard him say: Three tribes: Jurhum are from the remnants of ʿĀd, and Thaqīf are from the remnants of Thamūd.' records.isnad_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rāshid al-Zawfī, that he heard Rabīʿah ibn Qays al-Ḥimlalī say: 'I was sitting with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib one day when I heard him say:
records.matn_en: Three tribes: Jurhum are from the remnants of ʿĀd, and Thaqīf are from the remnants of Thamūd.' A man from Thaqīf was beside me, so I said to him: 'Do you not hear what the Commander of the Faithful is saying about you?' He said: 'What do you want? Do you want me to respond to him with words I heard from the Messenger of God, ﷺ?' Then Abū Shimr ibn Abrahah approached, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: 'And the people of this one,' meaning Abū Shimr, 'are remnants of Tubbaʿ, and the clan of Abū Shimr ibn Abrahah, the people of Dhī Aṣbaḥ, are from Ḥimyar.'
records.boundary_review_note: Rabi‘ah narrates Ali; the Thaqafi interlocutor is dialogue, not chain.

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah that al-Mundhir ibn Ḥizām, the grandfather of Ḥassān ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī, said in the Age of Ignorance: 'We inherited from al-Bahlūl ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir... and Ḥārithah al-Ghaṭrīf a glorious, well-established legacy. Traces from the family of the daughter of the son of Mālik... and the daughter of the son of Ismāʿīl, which will not change.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ غَزِيَّةَ، قَالَ: إِنَّ الْمُنْذِرَ بْنَ حِزَامٍ، جَدُّ حَسَّانَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ قَالَ: " فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: [البحر الطويل] وَرِثْنَا مِنَ الْبَهْلُولِ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَامِرٍ … وَحَارِثَةَ الْغَطْرِيفِ مَجْدًا مُؤَثَّلَا مَآثِرَ مِنْ آلِ ابْنِ بِنْتِ ابْنِ مَالِكٍ … وَبِنْتِ ابْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ مَا إِنْ تَحَوَّلَا

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, that it reached him regarding the lineage of Ḥaḍramawt: 'Ḥaḍramawt ibn Ghurr ibn Nabīt ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from ʿUlayy ibn Rabah, from ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “These lineages of yours are no grounds for disparaging anyone. You are all children of Adam, like the scant remainder in a measure that has not been filled. No one is superior to another except through religion or righteous deeds. It is enough disgrace for a man to be obscene, foul-mouthed, miserly, and cowardly.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ عُلَيِّ بْنِ رَبَاحٍ، عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ عَامِرٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «إِنَّ أَنْسَابَكُمْ هَذِهِ لَيْسَتْ بِمَسَابٍّ عَلَى أَحَدٍ، وَإِنَّمَا أَنْتُمْ وَلَدُ آدَمَ، طَفُّ الصَّاعِ لَمْ تَمْلَؤُهُ، وَلَيْسَ لِأَحَدٍ عَلَى أَحَدٍ فَضْلٌ إِلَّا بِدِينٍ، أَوْ عَمِلٍ صَالِحٍ، حَسْبُ الرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَكُونَ فَاحِشًا بَذِيًّا بَخِيلًا جَبَانًا» .

It is sufficient for a man to be foul-mouthed, miserly, or cowardly.'

records.text_en: Hishām ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that some people said to the Messenger of God, ﷺ: 'Tell us who are the most honorable of people.' He said: '{Indeed, the most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous.} [Al-Ḥujurāt: 13]' They said: 'We know that, but in this world.' He said: 'The most honorable of you is Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm.' They said: 'We know that, but we...' He said: 'People are like mines; the best of them in the Age of Ignorance are the best of them in Islam if they gain understanding.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، " أَنَّ نَاسًا، قَالُوا ⦗ص: 85⦘ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أَخْبِرْنَا بِأَكْرَمِ النَّاسِ» ، قَالَ: " {إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ} [الحجرات: 13] " قَالُوا: قَدْ عَلِمْنَا ذَلِكَ، وَلَكِنْ فِي الدُّنْيَا، قَالَ: «أَكْرَمُكُمْ يُوسُفُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ» قَالُوا: قَدْ عَلِمْنَا ذَلِكَ وَلَكِنْ نَحْنُ. قَالَ: «النَّاسُ مَعَادِنُ، خِيَارُهُمْ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ خِيَارُهُمْ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ إِذَا فَقِهُوا»

records.text_en: Ibrāhīm ibn Nashīṭ reported to me: I heard ʿUmar, the freedman of Ghufrah, say: Ibn Masʿūd passed by two men from Quraysh who were mocking him about his lineage. He heard them without realizing it, then turned to them and said: I heard what you said . records.text_en: ʿUmar, the freedman of Ghufrah, said Ibn Masʿūd passed by a man from Banī Fazārah one day while he was boasting of nobility to another, saying: 'I am the son of Badr, the son of Ḥudhayfah, the son of Ḥiṣn, the son of the noble elders.' Ibn Masʿūd said: 'That is Yūsuf, a prophet, the son of a prophet, the son of a prophet, the son of the Friend of the Merciful. A man boasts of another, yet he may be from the people of Hell. If his deeds are slow, his lineage will not hasten him.'
records.text_ar: وَقَالَ عُمَرُ مَوْلَى غُفْرَةَ: أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، مَرَّ يَوْمًا عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْ بَنِي فَزَارَةَ، وَهُوَ يُنَافِرُ آخَرَ الْمَجْدَ، وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: أَنَا ابْنُ بَدْرٍ، أَنَا ابْنُ حُذَيْفَةَ، أَنَا ابْنُ حِصْنٍ، أَنَا ابْنُ الْأَشْايَخِ الْأَكَارِمِ. فَقَالَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ: «ذَلِكَ يُوسُفُ، نَبِيٌّ ابْنُ نَبِيٍّ ابْنِ نَبِيٍّ ابْنِ خَلِيلِ الرَّحْمَنِ، إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَتَفَاخَرُ بِالرَّجُلِ، وَإِنَّهُ لَمِنْ أَهْلِ جَهَنَّمَ، إِنْ أَبْطَأَ بِهِ عَمَلُهُ لَمْ يُسْرِعْ بِهِ نَسَبُهُ»

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Ibn Abī Ḥabīb that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, was brought a boy, and he asked: 'What have you named this one?' They said 'Al-Sāʾib.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Do not name him al-Sāʾib, but rather ʿAbd Allāh.' They insisted on naming him al-Sāʾib, and he did not die until he lost his mind.'

records.text_en: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl, from Anas ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, was in al-Baqīʿ when a man said 'O Abū al-Qāsim.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, turned to him, and the man said: 'O Messenger of God, I did not mean you; I meant so-and-so.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Name with my name, but do not adopt my kunyah.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ حُمَيْدٍ الطَّوِيلِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، " أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ بِالْبَقِيعِ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ: يَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ، فَالْتَفَتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام، فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنِّي لَمْ أَعْنِكَ إِنَّمَا عَنِيتُ فُلَانًا، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «تَسَمَّوْا بِاسْمِي، وَلَا تَكَنَّوْا بِكُنْيَتِي»

records.text_en: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd reported to me from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Hilal, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to al-Hubab ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, who was known by that name: “Give up the name al-Hubab, for it is the name of a devil.” He renamed him ʿAbd Allah. The Messenger also said to al-Hubab ibn Mundhir al-Sulami: “Give up al-Hubab, for it is the name of a devil.” He renamed him ʿAbd al-Rahman.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي اللَّيْثُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي هِلَالٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ لِلْحُبَابِ بْنِ عبد اللَّهِ بْنِ أُبَيٍّ ابْنِ سَلُولَ، وَكَانَ يُكْنَى بِهِ: «دَعِ اسْمَ الْحُبَابِ، فَإِنَّهُ اسْمُ شَيْطَانٍ» . فَسَمَّاهُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام لِلْحُبَابِ بْنِ مُنْذِرٍ السُّلَمِيِّ: «دَعِ الْحُبَابَ فَإِنَّهُ اسْمُ شَيْطَانٍ» فَسَمَّاهُ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ "

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿah, from Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir al-Yaḥṣibī, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said 'The best names are ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and the like. The most truthful names are al-Ḥārith and Hammām. Al-Ḥārith for his worldly and religious affairs, and Hammām for both. The worst names are Ḥarb and Murrah.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ رَبِيعَةَ، عَنْ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ الْيَحْصِبِيِّ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «خَيْرُ الْأَسْمَاءِ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ، وَعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ، وَنَحْوَ هَذَا، وَأَصْدَقُ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْحَارِثُ، وَهَمَّامٌ، حَارِثٌ لِدُنْيَاهُ وَلِدِينِهِ، وَهَمَّامٌ بِهِمَا. وَشَرٌّ الْأَسْمَاءِ حَرْبٌ، وَمُرَّةُ»

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «خَيْرُ الْأَسْمَاءِ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ، وَعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ، وَنَحْوَ هَذَا، وَأَصْدَقُ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْحَارِثُ، وَهَمَّامٌ، حَارِثٌ لِدُنْيَاهُ وَلِدِينِهِ، وَهَمَّامٌ بِهِمَا. وَشَرٌّ الْأَسْمَاءِ حَرْبٌ، وَمُرَّةُ»
records.isnad_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿah, from Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir al-Yaḥṣibī, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said '
records.matn_en: The best names are ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and the like. The most truthful names are al-Ḥārith and Hammām. Al-Ḥārith for his worldly and religious affairs, and Hammām for both. The worst names are Ḥarb and Murrah.'
records.boundary_review_note: The matn begins at the prophetic attribution. English supplies the saying as a quote following the attribution.

records.text_en: And he informed me from Abdullah ibn Yazid, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from al-Qasim ibn Abdur-Rahman: 'Do not say 'Qaws Quzah' (the bow of Quzah), for Quzah is a devil, but it is simply 'the bow.''

records.boundary_review_note: The chain ends at al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman, who transmits the saying without an explicit attribution to the Prophet in this source wording.

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Ayyash, from Umar, the freed slave of Ghufrah, and Hammad ibn Hilal, that Ibn al-Kawwa said to Ali ibn Abi Talib: 'What is Qaws Quzah?' He said: 'Do not say Qaws Quzah, for Quzah is the devil, but it is a sign of security from God for the people of the earth from drowning after the people of Noah.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَيَّاشٍ، عَنْ عُمَرَ مَوْلَى غُفْرَةَ، وَحَمَّادِ بْنِ هِلَالٍ، أَنَّ ابْنَ الْكَوَّاءِ، قَالَ لِعَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: مَا قَوْسُ قُزَحَ؟ قَالَ: «لَا تَقُولُوا قَوْسَ قُزَحَ، فَإِنَّ قُزَحَ الشَّيْطَانُ، وَلَكِنْ أَمَنَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِأَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْغَرَقِ بَعْدَ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ»

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Humayd al-Tawil, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah had a son called Abu Umayr, named by his father. He had a nughayr (a small bird), and whenever the Messenger of God, ﷺ, entered, he would say: 'O Abu Umayr, what did the nughayr do?'

records.text_en: Khalid ibn Humayd and others reported to me from ʿUqayl ibn Khalid, from Ibn Shihab, that ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had been named Hubab. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, renamed him ʿAbd Allah and said: “This is a devil.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي خَالِدُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، وَغَيْرُهُ عَنْ عُقَيْلِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ ⦗ص: 107⦘ شِهَابٍ، «أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أُبَيٍّ ابْنِ سَلُولَ، كَانَ اسْمُهُ حُبَابٌ» فَسَمَّاهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، وَقَالَ: «هَذَا شَيْطَانٌ»

records.text_en: And he informed me from Muawiyah ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Jabir, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Among the names, you should have Yazid, for there is no one except that he increases in good and evil; al-Harith, for there is no one except that he cultivates for his Hereafter or his worldly life; and Hammam, for there is no one except that he is concerned with his Hereafter or his worldly life. If these names escape you, then name them with names that denote servitude.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ جَابِرٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ بِيَزِيدَ، فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا وَهُوَ يَزِيدُ فِي الْخَيْرِ وَالشَّرِّ، وَالْحَارِثِ فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا وَهُوَ يَحْرُثُ لِآخِرَتِهِ أَوْ دُنْيَاهُ، وَهَمَّامٍ فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا وَهُوَ يَهْتَمُّ بِآخِرَتِهِ أَوْ دُنْيَاهُ. فَإِنْ أَخْطَأَكُمْ هَذِهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ فعَبِّدُوا»

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Nafi ibn Yazid, from... that he was a young boy known as Abu al-Qasim, and his name was Muhammad. Two boys followed him and called out: 'O Abu al-Qasim.' Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ, heard them from her chamber, called him, and asked him about it. He informed her that it was his kunyah (agnomen). She forbade him from that and said 'Do not use the kunyah of Abu al-Qasim.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي نَافِعُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ. . . أَنَّهُ كَانَ وَهُوَ غُلَامٌ يُكَنَّى أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ، واسْمُهُ مُحَمَّدٌ، وَاتَّبَعَهُ غُلَامَانِ مَعَهُ فَصَاحُوا: يَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ، فَسَمِعَتْهُمْ عَائِشَةُ زَوْجُ النَّبِيِّ عليه السلام مِنْ حُجْرَتِهَا فَدَعَتْهُ وَسَأَلَتْهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، فَأَخْبَرَهَا أَنَّهَا كُنْيَتُهُ، فَنَهَتْهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وَقَالَتْ: «لَا تَتَكَنَّ بِأَبِي الْقَاسِمِ»

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Abu Tahir, that his father, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm, told him that his grandfather, Amr ibn Hazm, had a son named Muhammad ibn Amr. He named him Muhammad and gave him the kunyah Abu al-Qasim. When this reached the Prophet, ﷺ, he said 'Whoever is named with my name should not use my kunyah.' He then gave him the kunyah Abu Abd al-Malik. He said: 'You will hardly find anyone in the family of Hazm named Muhammad except that he is given the kunyah Abu Abd al-Malik.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي أَبُو طَاهِرٍ، أَنَّ أَبَاهُ مُحَمَّدَ بْنَ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ حَزْمٍ، حَدَّثَهُ أَنَّ جَدَّهُ عَمْرَو بْنَ حَزْمٍ وُلِدَ لَهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو، فَسَمَّاهُ مُحَمَّدًا وَكَنَّاهُ أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ النَّبِيَّ عليه السلام، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «مَنْ تَسَمَّى بِاسْمِي فَلَا يُكَنَّى بِكُنْيَتِي» . قَالَ: فَكَنَّاهُ النَّبِيُّ عليه السلام بِأَبِي عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ " قَالَ: فَلَا يَكَادُ يَجِدُ فِي آلِ حَزْمٍ أَحَدًا يُسَمَّى مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا يُكْنَى بِأَبِي عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ

records.raw_text_en: And he narrated to me from Abu Tahir, that his father, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm, told him that his grandfather, Amr ibn Hazm, had a son named Muhammad ibn Amr. He named him Muhammad and gave him the kunyah Abu al-Qasim. When this reached the Prophet, ﷺ, he said 'Whoever is named with my name should not use my kunyah.' He then gave him the kunyah Abu Abd al-Malik. He said: 'You will hardly find anyone in the family of Hazm named Muhammad except that he is given the kunyah Abu Abd al-Malik.'

records.text_en: Hisham ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: “An umm walad (enslaved woman who had borne him a child) belonging to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab’s son came to ʿUmar and asked him for clothing. He said, ‘Who is your master that he does not clothe you?’ She replied, ‘Abu ʿIsa.’ He said, ‘Abu ʿIsa?’ Aslam said: I was told, ‘Go and summon him, but do not tell him why.’ ʿUmar used to tell us: ‘When I send you to summon someone, do not tell him why; Satan may teach him a lie and he will come to me with it.’ I went to summon him. He asked why, and I said I did not know. He came with me, continuing to ask, until we reached the door. I had found many chickens there; he gave me one in exchange for telling him, so I told him. I entered, and he followed behind me. ʿUmar asked him, ‘Did he tell you why I summoned you?’ He said yes. ʿUmar called me over, held both my hands in his left hand, and began striking me with his whip. I kept shrinking away. Aslam said: ʿUmar kept saying, ‘He is resolute!’ Then he let me go and said, ‘By God, you are making me do things to you that I dislike.’ He then went to his son and began striking him with the whip until he weakened. He said: ‘Do you know the names of the Arabs, you wretch? ʿAmir, ʿUwaymir, Malik, Sirm, Muwaylik, and Sararah—that is, Murrah.’ He repeated this two or three times. Then he said: ‘Give up ʿIsa, for by God, we know no father of ʿIsa.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ: جَاءَتْ أُمُّ وَلَدٍ لِابْنِ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ، إِلَى عُمَرَ، فَقَالَتِ: اكْسُنِي، فَقَالَ: مَنْ سَيِّدُكِ، لَا يَكْسُوكِ؟ قَالَتْ: أَبُو عِيسَى. قَالَ: أَبُو عِيسَى؟ قَالَ أَسْلَمَ: فَقِيلَ لِي: اذْهَبْ وادْعُهُ وَلَا تُخْبِرْهُ لِمَ تَدْعُوهُ. وَقَدْ كَانَ يَقُولُ لَنَا: إِذَا أَرْسَلْتُكُمْ إِلَى أَحَدٍ تَدْعُونَهُ فَلَا تُخْبِرُوهُ لِمَ أَدْعُوهُ فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يُعَلِّمُهُ كِذْبَةً فَيَأْتِينِي بِهَا. فَجِئْتُهُ فَدَعَوْتُهُ، فَقَالَ: لِمَ تَدْعُونِي؟ قَالَ: فَلَا أَدْرِي. قَالَ: فَأَقْبَلَ مَعِيَ وَجَعَلَ يَسْأَلُنِي، وَأَنَا أُخْبِرُهُ حَتَّى جِئْنَا الْبَابَ، وَقَدْ وَجَدْتُ لَهُ دَجَاجًا عَظِيمًا، قَالَ: وَأَعْطَانِي مِنْهُنَّ دَجَاجَةً عَلَى أَنْ أُخْبِرَهُ، فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ، قَالَ: وَدَخَلْتُ ودَخَلَ فِي أَثَرِي، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَكَ لِمَ أَرْسَلْتُ إِلَيْكَ، قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: وَدَعَانِي فَجَمَعَ يَدَيَّ فِي يَدِهِ الْيُسْرَى، ثُمَّ جَعَلَ يَضْرِبُنِي بِالدِّرَّةِ وَجَعَلْتُ أَنْزَوِي، قَالَ أَسْلَمُ: وَيَقُولُ إِنَّهُ لَحَدِيدٌ. قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي، وَقَالَ: " وَاللَّهِ إِنَّكُمْ تَحْمِلُونِي عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ وَأَنَا كَارِهٌ، ثُمَّ قَامَ إِلَى ابْنِهِ فَلَوْ أَرَادَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ، ثُمَّ جَعَلَ يَضْرِبُهُ بِالدِّرَّةِ حَتَّى فَتَرَ، فَقَالَ: هَلْ تَدْرِي مَا أَسْمَاءُ الْعَرَبِ لَا أُمَّ لَكَ؟ عَامِرٌ، وَعُوَيْمِرٌ، وَمَالِكٌ، وَصِرْمٌ، وَمُوَيْلِكٌ، وسَرَرَةُ، هُوَ مُرَّةُ، ثُمَّ جَعَلَ يَضْرِبُهُ وَيَقُولُ لَهُ ذَلِكَ: هَلْ تَدْرِي مَا أَسْمَاءُ الْعَرَبِ؟، ثُمَّ يُرَدِّدُ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ مِثْلَ مَقَالَتِهِ الْأُولَى مَرَّتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَاثًا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: دَعْ عَنْكَ عِيسَى، فَإِنَّا وَاللَّهِ مَا نَعْلَمُ لِعِيسَى أَبًا "

records.raw_text_en: And he informed me from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said A slave woman of Ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab came to Umar and said: 'Clothe me.' He said: 'Who is your master that he does not clothe you?' She said: 'Abu Isa.' He said: 'Abu Isa?' Aslam said: It was said to me: 'Go and call him, but do not tell him why you are calling him.' He used to tell us: 'When I send you to call someone, do not tell him why I am calling him, for Satan may teach him a lie, and he will come to me with it.' I went to him and called him, and he said: 'Why are you calling me?' I said: 'I do not know.' He came with me, and he kept asking me, and I kept informing him until we reached the door. I found a large rooster for him. He gave me one of them on the condition that I inform him, so I did. He said: 'You entered, and he followed me.' He said: 'Did he tell you why I sent for you?' I said: 'Yes.' He took my hands and gathered them in his left hand, then he began to strike me with a whip, and I kept shrinking back. Aslam said: He kept saying it was severe. Then he released me and said: 'By God, you make me do to you what I dislike.' Then he went to his son and grabbed him by the neck, striking him with the whip until he weakened. He said: 'Do you know the names of the Arabs? May you have no mother! Amir, Uwaymir, Malik, Sirm, Muwaylik, and Sararah—he is Murrah.' Then he kept striking him and saying: 'Do you know the names of the Arabs?' He repeated this to him like his first statement two or three times. Then he said: 'Leave Isa, for by God, we do not know of any father for Isa.'
records.display_text_en: Hisham ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: “An umm walad (enslaved woman who had borne him a child) belonging to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab’s son came to ʿUmar and asked him for clothing. He said, ‘Who is your master that he does not clothe you?’ She replied, ‘Abu ʿIsa.’ He said, ‘Abu ʿIsa?’ Aslam said: I was told, ‘Go and summon him, but do not tell him why.’ ʿUmar used to tell us: ‘When I send you to summon someone, do not tell him why; Satan may teach him a lie and he will come to me with it.’ I went to summon him. He asked why, and I said I did not know. He came with me, continuing to ask, until we reached the door. I had found many chickens there; he gave me one in exchange for telling him, so I told him. I entered, and he followed behind me. ʿUmar asked him, ‘Did he tell you why I summoned you?’ He said yes. ʿUmar called me over, held both my hands in his left hand, and began striking me with his whip. I kept shrinking away. Aslam said: ʿUmar kept saying, ‘He is resolute!’ Then he let me go and said, ‘By God, you are making me do things to you that I dislike.’ He then went to his son and began striking him with the whip until he weakened. He said: ‘Do you know the names of the Arabs, you wretch? ʿAmir, ʿUwaymir, Malik, Sirm, Muwaylik, and Sararah—that is, Murrah.’ He repeated this two or three times. Then he said: ‘Give up ʿIsa, for by God, we know no father of ʿIsa.’”

records.matn_en: Hisham ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: “An umm walad (enslaved woman who had borne him a child) belonging to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab’s son came to ʿUmar and asked him for clothing. He said, ‘Who is your master that he does not clothe you?’ She replied, ‘Abu ʿIsa.’ He said, ‘Abu ʿIsa?’ Aslam said: I was told, ‘Go and summon him, but do not tell him why.’ ʿUmar used to tell us: ‘When I send you to summon someone, do not tell him why; Satan may teach him a lie and he will come to me with it.’ I went to summon him. He asked why, and I said I did not know. He came with me, continuing to ask, until we reached the door. I had found many chickens there; he gave me one in exchange for telling him, so I told him. I entered, and he followed behind me. ʿUmar asked him, ‘Did he tell you why I summoned you?’ He said yes. ʿUmar called me over, held both my hands in his left hand, and began striking me with his whip. I kept shrinking away. Aslam said: ʿUmar kept saying, ‘He is resolute!’ Then he let me go and said, ‘By God, you are making me do things to you that I dislike.’ He then went to his son and began striking him with the whip until he weakened. He said: ‘Do you know the names of the Arabs, you wretch? ʿAmir, ʿUwaymir, Malik, Sirm, Muwaylik, and Sararah—that is, Murrah.’ He repeated this two or three times. Then he said: ‘Give up ʿIsa, for by God, we know no father of ʿIsa.’”
records.boundary_review_note: The report begins with Aslam’s first-person account of a slave woman approaching Umar; the full dialogue remains matn.

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Musa ibn Ulayy, from his father, who said Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata, who said: I had a daughter, and Zaynab, the daughter of Umm Salamah, asked me about her name. I said: 'Barrah.' She said: 'Do not do that, for I was named Barrah, and the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'God knows best who are the righteous among you.' She was then named Zaynab.'
records.text_ar: وَحَدَّثَنِي مُوسَى بْنُ عُلَيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ أَبِي حَبِيبٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَطَاءٍ، قَالَ وُلِدَتْ لِيَ ابْنَةٌ، فَسَأَلَتْنِي زَيْنَبُ ابْنَةُ أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ، عَنِ اسْمِهَا، فَقُلْتُ: بَرَّةُ، فَقَالَتْ: لَا تَفْعَلْ، فَإِنِّي سُمِّيتُ بَرَّةُ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِالْأَبْرَارِ مِنْكُمْ» سُمِّيَتْ زَيْنَبَ "

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Ibn Shihab, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, forbade the kunyah Abu Murrah and named him Abu Hulwah, but it did not stick. He named Abu al-As Muti, but it did not stick. He named Hazn Sahl, but it did not stick.

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from his father, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said 'The most despicable name with God on the Day of Resurrection is a man who is named Malik al-Amlak (King of Kings).'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from Ibn Abi Habib that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab would not allow anyone to adopt a prophet’s name as a kunyah or to be named after a prophet. Talhah ibn ʿUbayd God said: “I have the kunyah Abu Muhammad, and the Messenger of God did not object.” Another speaker [name missing in the Arabic] said: “I have the kunyah Abu Yahya, and the Messenger of God heard it without objecting.” ʿUmar said: “[The remainder of this sentence is corrupt/unclear in the Arabic.] But I will never give one of my children that name.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي حَبِيبٍ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، " كَانَ لَا يَدَعُ أَحَدًا يَتَكَنَّى بِاسْمِ نَبِيٍّ وَلَا يُسَمَّى بِهِ، فَقَالَ طَلْحَةُ بْنُ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ: لَقَدْ كُنِيتُ أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ فَمَا أَنْكَرَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام، وَقَالَ (. . . . . .) : لَقَدْ كُنِيتُ أَبَا يَحْيَى ورَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام يَسْمَعُهَا فَمَا أَنْكَرَهَا. قَالَ عُمَرُ: «أَمَا أَدَلُّ أَشَرُّ الَّذِي يَحْيَى، وَلَكِنْ لَا أُسَمِّي بِهَا وَلَدًا لِي أَبَدًا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي حَبِيبٍ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، " كَانَ لَا يَدَعُ أَحَدًا يَتَكَنَّى بِاسْمِ نَبِيٍّ وَلَا يُسَمَّى بِهِ، فَقَالَ طَلْحَةُ بْنُ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ: لَقَدْ كُنِيتُ أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ فَمَا أَنْكَرَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام، وَقَالَ (. . . . . .) : لَقَدْ كُنِيتُ أَبَا يَحْيَى ورَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام يَسْمَعُهَا فَمَا أَنْكَرَهَا. قَالَ عُمَرُ: «أَمَا أَدَلُّ أَشَرُّ الَّذِي يَحْيَى، وَلَكِنْ لَا أُسَمِّي بِهَا وَلَدًا لِي أَبَدًا»

records.raw_text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Ibn Abi Habib, that Umar ibn al-Khattab would not allow anyone to use the name of a prophet or to be named after him. Talhah ibn Ubaydullah said 'I have been known as Abu Muhammad, and the Messenger of God, ﷺ, did not object to it.' He said: 'I have been known as Abu Yahya, and the Messenger of God, ﷺ, heard it and did not object.' Umar said: 'As for the one named Yahya, it is the worst of names, but I will never name any of my children with it.'

records.text_en: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar reported to me from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, who said: “The most truthful names are al-Harith and Hammam; the names most hateful to God are Harb and Murrah; and the most false [in their implication] are Khalid and Malik—for there is no malik (sovereign) but God.”

The most deceitful are Khalid and Malik—there is no deity except God.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Yahya ibn Abdullah and Sa'id ibn Abdur-Rahman, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Abbad ibn Hamzah, from Hamzah, or he heard it from Aisha, that Aisha said to the Messenger of God: 'Will you not give me a kunyah?' records.text_en: Ubaydullah said It reached me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, changed the name of a man who was named al-As (the disobedient) and named him Muti (the obedient).
records.text_ar: قَالَ عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ وَبَلَغَنِيَ «أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام غَيَّرَ اسْمَ رَجُلٍ كَانَ اسْمُهُ الْعَاصِ، فَسَمَّاهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ مُطِيعًا»

records.text_en: Al-Qasim ibn ʿAbd Allah reported to me from ʿUmarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Muhammad ibn Habban, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said on the day of Badr: “Stand firm with me.” Al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir al-Ansari stood and said: “Messenger of God, you know Badr best.” The Prophet asked: “Who are you?” He replied: “I am al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir.” He said: “Your name is al-Hubab? Al-Hubab is a devil. You are ʿAbd Allah.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ غَزِيَّةَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَبَّانَ، " أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ: «اشْتَدُّوا عَلَيَّ» ، فَقَامَ الْحُبَابُ بْنُ الْمُنْذِرِ الْأَنْصَارِيُّ، فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَوْلَى بِبَدْرٍ عِلْمًا، قَالَ: «مَنْ أَنْتَ؟» قَالَ: أَنَا الْحُبَابُ بْنُ الْمُنْذِرِ، قَالَ: «اسْمُكَ الْحُبَابُ، إِنَّمَا الْحُبَابُ شَيْطَانٌ ، أَنْتَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ»

records.text_en: And I heard Malik ibn Anas narrate from Yahya ibn Sa'id, that Umar ibn al-Khattab asked a man: 'What is your name?' He said 'Jamrah (ember).' He said: 'Son of whom?' He said: 'Son of Shihab (flame).' He said: 'From whom?' He said: 'From al-Huraqah (the burned).' He said: 'Where are your people?' He said: 'In Hirrat al-Nar (the land of fire).' He said: 'Which one?' He said: 'Dhat al-Latha (the blazing).' Umar said: 'Go to your people, for they have burned.'

records.text_en: Sufyan narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah: “A man from the Ansar had a son and named him Abu al-Qasim. The Ansar said, ‘We will not give you the kunyah Abu al-Qasim, nor will we bring you joy.’ He went to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and told him what had happened. The Messenger said: ‘Name your son ʿAbd al-Rahman.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: وُلِدَ لِرَجُلٍ مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ غُلَامٌ فَسَمَّاهُ أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ، فَقَالَتِ الْأَنْصَارُ: لَا نُكَنِّيكَ بِأَبِي الْقَاسِمِ وَلَا نُنْعِمُكَ عَيْنًا، فَأَتَى رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام فَذَكَرَ ذَلِكَ لَهُ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: «سَمِّ ابْنَكَ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ»

records.text_en: And I heard Sufyan narrate from Amr ibn Kathir, who said: I heard a man in Medina say: My grandfather brought my father to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and said to him: 'I have been blessed with a boy, what should I name him?' He said: 'Name him with the name of the most beloved person to me: Hamzah.'

records.text_en: And I heard Sufyan narrate from Ibn Shihab, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'I have five names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the eraser) through whom disbelief is erased, I am al-Hashir (the gatherer) at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am al-Aqib (the last), and there is no one after al-Aqib.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from Abu Qabil, from a man of Banu Ghifar who told him: “His mother brought him to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, with an amulet on him. The Messenger cut it off and asked: ‘What is your son’s name?’ She said: ‘al-Saʾib.’ He replied: ‘Rather, his name is ʿAbd Allah.’” The man said: “I asked him, ‘Did you answer to both names?’ He said: ‘No, by God. I answered only to the name the Messenger of God gave me.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي قَبِيلٍ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، مِنْ بَنِي غِفَارٍ حَدَّثَهُ " أَنَّ أُمَّهُ جَاءَتْ بِهِ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام وَعَلَيْهِ تَمِيمَةٌ، فَقَطَعَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام تَمِيمَتَهُ وَقَالَ: «مَا اسْمُ ابْنُكِ؟» . فَقَالَتِ: اسْمُهُ السَّائِبُ، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «بَلِ اسْمُهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ» : فَقُلْتُ: أَتُجِيبُ بِكُلِّهِمَا؟ قَالَ: لَا وَاللَّهِ مَا كُنْتُ أُجِيبُ إِلَّا عَلَى اسْمِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام الَّذِي سَمَّانِي

records.raw_text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Abu Qabil, from a man of Banu Ghifar, who narrated to him: His mother brought him to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, while he had an amulet on him. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, cut it off and said 'What is your son's name?' She said: 'His name is al-Sa'ib.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Rather, his name is Abdullah.' I said: 'Should I answer to both?' He said: 'No, by God, I would only answer to the name the Messenger of God, ﷺ, gave me.'

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, who said I asked Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Qasim about the name of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. He said: 'They were three brothers, sons of Abu Quhafah: Atiq, Mu'taq, and Utayq.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talhah, from his uncle Ishaq ibn Talhah, who said I entered upon Aisha, ؓ, and she said: 'Abu Bakr entered upon the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and he said to him: 'You are Atiq (freed) from the Fire.' From that day, he was named Atiq.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, who said When the delegation of Banu al-Shaytan ibn al-Harith ibn Mu'awiyah came to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, he asked them: 'Who are you?' They said: 'We are the sons of Shaytan.' He said: 'Rather, you are the sons of Abdullah.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، قَالَ: لَمَّا وَفَدَ بَنَوُ الشَّيْطَانِ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام سَأَلَهُمْ: «مَنْ أَنْتُمْ؟» ، فَقَالُوا: نَحْنُ بَنُو الشَّيْطَانِ، قَالَ: «بَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَنُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ»

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, that when the delegation of Rashidah came to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, he said 'Who are you?' They were called Khalifah (successor). They said: 'From Khalifah?' The Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Rather, you are from Rashidah (rightly guided).'

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Abi Dhiʾb reported to me from Saʿid al-Maqburi, who heard al-Saluli tell Nawfal ibn Musahiq that he had asked Kaʿb al-Ahbar: “What does the Book of God say about disobedience to parents?” Kaʿb replied: “I will tell you: when a parent calls upon the child by oath and the child does not honor it; when the parent asks him for something and he does not give it; when the parent entrusts him with something and he does not return it; and when the parent complains to God about what he suffers from him—this is all disobedience.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ: أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي ذِئْبٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدٍ الْمَقْبُرِيِّ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ السَّلُولِيَّ، يُحَدِّثُ نَوْفَلَ بْنَ مُسَاحِقٍ، أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ كَعْبَ الْأَحْبَارِ: مَا تَجِدُونَ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ مِنْ عُقُوقِ الْوَالِدِ؟، فَقَالَ كَعْبٌ: «أَنَا أُخْبِرُكُ،» إِذَا أَقْسَمَ عَلَيْهِ فَلَمْ يَبِرَّهُ، وَسَأَلَهُ فَلَمْ يُعْطِهِ، وَائْتَمَنَهُ فَلَمْ يُؤدِّهْ عَلَيْهِ، وَاشْتَكَى إِلَى اللَّهِ مَا ⦗ص: 148⦘ يَلْقَى مِنْهُ، فَذَلِكَ الْعُقُوقُ كُلُّهُ "

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Zur'ah ibn Ibrahim, that a man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have a mother who has reached such old age that she cannot fulfill her needs except with my back as her mount. I carry her and turn my face away from her. Have I fulfilled her right?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, is it not enough that I carry her on my back and restrain myself for her?' He said: 'No, for she used to do that for you while hoping for your survival, and you do that for her while hoping for her departure.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ أَبِي هِلَالٍ، عَنْ زُرْعَةَ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا، أَتَى عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، فَقَالَ: يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، إِنَّ لِي أُمًّا بَلَغَهَا مِنَ الْكِبَرِ أَنَّهَا لَا تَقْضِي حَاجَةً إِلَّا وَظَهْرِي مَطِيَّةٌ لَهَا فَأُوطِيهَا وَأَصْرِفُ عَنْهَا وَجْهِي، فَهَلْ أَدَّيْتُ حَقَّهَا؟ قَالَ: لَا. قَالَ: يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، أَلَيْسَ بَعْدَ مَا حَمَلْتُهَا عَلَى ظَهْرِي، وَحَبَسْتُ عَلَيْهَا نَفْسِي؟ قَالَ: «لَا، لِأَنَّهَا كَانَتْ تَصْنَعُ ⦗ص: 150⦘ ذَلِكَ بِكَ وَهِيَ تَتَمَنَّى بَقَاءَكَ، وَأَنْتَ تَصْنَعُ ذَلِكَ بِهَا وَأَنْتَ تَتَمَنَّى فِرَاقَهَا»

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ رَجُلًا، أَتَى عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، فَقَالَ: يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، إِنَّ لِي أُمًّا بَلَغَهَا مِنَ الْكِبَرِ أَنَّهَا لَا تَقْضِي حَاجَةً إِلَّا وَظَهْرِي مَطِيَّةٌ لَهَا فَأُوطِيهَا وَأَصْرِفُ عَنْهَا وَجْهِي، فَهَلْ أَدَّيْتُ حَقَّهَا؟ قَالَ: لَا. قَالَ: يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، أَلَيْسَ بَعْدَ مَا حَمَلْتُهَا عَلَى ظَهْرِي، وَحَبَسْتُ عَلَيْهَا نَفْسِي؟ قَالَ: «لَا، لِأَنَّهَا كَانَتْ تَصْنَعُ ذَلِكَ بِكَ وَهِيَ تَتَمَنَّى بَقَاءَكَ، وَأَنْتَ تَصْنَعُ ذَلِكَ بِهَا وَأَنْتَ تَتَمَنَّى فِرَاقَهَا»
records.isnad_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Zur'ah ibn Ibrahim,
records.matn_en: that a man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have a mother who has reached such old age that she cannot fulfill her needs except with my back as her mount. I carry her and turn my face away from her. Have I fulfilled her right?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, is it not enough that I carry her on my back and restrain myself for her?' He said: 'No, for she used to do that for you while hoping for your survival, and you do that for her while hoping for her departure.'
records.boundary_review_note: The matn begins with an unnamed man’s visit to Umar; the man is not identified in the source.

records.text_en: And he informed me from Huyayy ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdur-Rahman al-Hubuli, who said I was sitting with Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab, and a man from Yemen was circumambulating the Kaaba while carrying his mother on his shoulders. When he completed his circumambulation, he put her down. Ibn Umar called him and said: 'Who is this woman to you?' He said: 'She is my mother.' Abdullah ibn Umar said: 'I wish I had reached my mother and circumambulated with her as you did with your mother, even if I had nothing in this world but these two sandals.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Sufyan ibn Sa'id, from Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ya'la ibn Ata, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said 'The pleasure of God is with the pleasure of the parent, and the wrath of God is with the wrath of the parent.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Shabib ibn Sa'id, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Ata al-Khurasani, that Ibn Abbas said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Whoever begins his day pleasing his parents will have two doors opened to Paradise for him, and if it is one parent, then one door. And whoever ends his day pleasing his parents, it is the same. But whoever begins his day displeasing his parents will have two doors opened to Hell for him, and if it is one parent, then one door. And whoever ends his day displeasing his parents, it is the same.' Then the Prophet, ﷺ, added: 'Even if they wrong him, even if they wrong him.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي شَبِيبُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ أَبَانَ بْنِ أَبِي عَيَّاشٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ الْخُرَاسَانِيِّ، أَنَّ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ: إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «مَنْ أَصْبَحَ مُرْضِيًّا لِوَالِدَيْهِ، أَصْبَحَ لَهُ بَابَانِ مَفْتُوحَانِ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَإِنْ كَانَ وَاحِدًا فَوَاحِدًا، وَإِنْ أَمْسَى مُرْضِيًّا لِوَالِدَيْهِ فَمِثْلُ ذَلِكَ. وَإِنْ أَصْبَحَ مُسْخِطًا لِوَالِدَيْهِ أَصْبَحَ لَهُ بَابَانِ مَفْتُوحَانِ إِلَى النَّارِ، وَإِنْ كَانَ وَاحِدًا فَوَاحِدًا، وَإِنْ أَمْسَى مُسْخِطًا لِوَالِدَيْهِ فَمِثْلُ ذَلِكَ» . قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ النَّبِيُّ عليه السلام: «وَإِنْ ظَلَمَاهُ، وَإِنْ ظَلَمَاهُ»

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ: إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «مَنْ أَصْبَحَ مُرْضِيًّا لِوَالِدَيْهِ، أَصْبَحَ لَهُ بَابَانِ مَفْتُوحَانِ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَإِنْ كَانَ وَاحِدًا فَوَاحِدًا، وَإِنْ أَمْسَى مُرْضِيًّا لِوَالِدَيْهِ فَمِثْلُ ذَلِكَ. وَإِنْ أَصْبَحَ مُسْخِطًا لِوَالِدَيْهِ أَصْبَحَ لَهُ بَابَانِ مَفْتُوحَانِ إِلَى النَّارِ، وَإِنْ كَانَ وَاحِدًا فَوَاحِدًا، وَإِنْ أَمْسَى مُسْخِطًا لِوَالِدَيْهِ فَمِثْلُ ذَلِكَ» . قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ النَّبِيُّ عليه السلام: «وَإِنْ ظَلَمَاهُ، وَإِنْ ظَلَمَاهُ»

records.text_en: Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from Bakr ibn Sawadah that a man came to the Prophet, ﷺ, and said: “Prophet of God, I have wealth that keeps me occupied. Tell me of a deed that will bring me nearer to Paradise.” The Prophet asked: “Is your mother alive?” He replied: “No.” The Prophet said: “Had your mother been alive, I would have told you [what to do]. But give food generously and speak gently.”

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Ka'b: 'In Hell, there are four bridges: The first is a bridge where every severer of kinship is detained. records.text_en: And he informed me from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Ubaydullah ibn Zahr, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu al-Darda, who said 'Among the acts of disobedience of a child to his parent is calling him by his name and walking ahead of him.'

records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ زَحْرٍ، عَنْ لَيْثِ بْنِ أَبِي سُلَيْمٍ، عَنْ شَهْرِ بْنِ حَوْشَبٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ، قَالَ: «
records.matn_ar: مِنْ عُقُوقِ الْوَلَدِ لِوَالِدِهِ أَنْ يَدْعُوَهُ بِاسْمِهِ، وَأَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَهُ فِي الْمَشْيِ»
records.isnad_en: And he informed me from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Ubaydullah ibn Zahr, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu al-Darda, who said '
records.matn_en: Among the acts of disobedience of a child to his parent is calling him by his name and walking ahead of him.'
records.boundary_review_note: The matn is Abu al-Darda’s statement about a child’s conduct toward a parent.

records.text_en: And he informed me from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from Ata ibn Dinar, that a man said 'O Messenger of God, which of the parents has the greatest right?' He said: 'The one who carried you between her sides, nursed you with her breasts, cradled you on her thighs, and sacrificed her parents for you.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ دِينَارٍ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا، قَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَيُّ الْوَالِدَيْنِ أَعْظَمُ حَقًّا؟ . قَالَ: «الَّتِي حَمَلَتْ بَيْنَ الْجَنْبَيْنِ، وَأَرْضَعَتْ بِالثَّدْيَينِ، وَحَضَنَتْ عَلَى الْفَخِذَيْنِ، وَفَدَتْهُ بِالْوَالِدَيْنِ»

records.text_en: And he informed me from al-Harith ibn Nabhan, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, that Abu Hurayrah saw a man with his father and asked the young man: 'Who is this?' He said 'This is my father.' He said: 'Do not walk ahead of him, do not sit before him, and do not call him by his name, for that is disobedience.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْحَارِثُ بْنُ نَبْهَانَ، عَنْ لَيْثِ بْنِ أَبِي سُلَيْمٍ، أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، رَأَى رَجُلًا مَعَهُ أَبُوهُ فَسَأَلَ الْفَتَى: مَنْ هَذَا؟ فَقَالَ: هَذَا أَبِي، قَالَ: «فَلَا تَمْشِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ، وَلَا تَجْلِسْ قَبْلَهُ، وَلَا تَدْعُهُ بِاسْمِهِ، فَإِنَّهُ مِنَ الْعُقُوقِ»

records.text_en: And he informed me from al-Qasim ibn Abdullah and Shimr ibn Numayr, from Husayn ibn Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Treat Abbas well, for he is my uncle and the twin of my father.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، وَشِمْرُ بْنُ نُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ جَدِّهِ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «اسْتَوْصُوا بِعَبَّاسٍ خَيْرًا؛ فَإِنَّهُ عَمِّي وَصِنْوُ أَبِي»

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ashhal ibn Hatim, from Abdullah ibn Awn, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said 'They used to say: Honor your child and teach him good manners.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي أَشْهَلُ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَوْنٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِيرِينَ، قَالَ: كَانُوا يَقُولُونَ: «أَكْرِمْ وَلَدَكَ وَأَحْسِنْ أَدَبَهُ»

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Harmalah ibn Imran, from Abu al-Hudaj al-Tujibi, who said I said to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: 'Every time God mentions in the Quran the duty of being good to parents, I understand it except for His saying: {And speak to them a generous word} [Al-Isra: 23]. What is this generous word?' Ibn al-Musayyib said: 'The word of a sinful servant to a harsh master.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي حَرْمَلَةُ بْنُ عِمْرَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْهُدَاجِ التُّجِيبِيِّ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِسَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ: " كُلَّمَا ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ بِرِّ الْوَالِدَيْنِ عَرَفْتُهُ ⦗ص: 173⦘ إِلَّا قَوْلَهُ: {وَقُلْ لَهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا} [الإسراء: 23] مَا هَذَا الْقَوْلُ الْكَرِيمُ؟، فَقَالَ ابْنُ الْمُسَيِّبِ: «قَوْلُ الْعَبْدِ الْمُذْنِبِ لِلسَّيِّدِ الْفَظِّ»

records.text_en: And he informed me from Haywah ibn Shurayh, from Ibn al-Had, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that a Bedouin met him on the road to Mecca. Abdullah ibn Umar greeted him, let him ride the donkey he was riding, and gave him the turban he was wearing on his head. Ibn Dinar said We said to him: 'May God rectify you, they are Bedouins, and they are content with little.' Abdullah said: 'This man's father was a close friend of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: 'Goodness is the child's maintaining the ties of his father's friends.''

records.text_en: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid reported to me from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUtbah, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: “Moses hastened to his Lord and saw a servant. He wished for a station like his near the Throne. He asked: ‘My Lord, who is this servant of Yours?’ He replied: ‘I will tell you three of his deeds: he does not envy people for what God has granted them from His bounty; he does not go about spreading malicious gossip; and he does not behave toward his parents in a way that causes them to be cursed.’ Moses asked: ‘Can a person cause his parents to be cursed?’ He replied: ‘He makes himself liable to their being insulted [by insulting another’s parents].’”

records.text_en: Someone who heard al-Awzaʿi reported to me that he said: “It reached me that whoever mistreated his parents while they were alive, then pays any debt they left, seeks forgiveness for them, and does not cause them to be cursed, will nevertheless be recorded as dutiful. And whoever treated his parents well while they were alive, but does not pay their debt or seek forgiveness for them, and causes them to be cursed, will be recorded as dutiful.”

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Ibn Ayyub, from Zabban ibn Fa'id, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh, from his father, that the Messenger of God said 'Whoever is dutiful to his parents, glad tidings for him. God will increase his lifespan.'

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb said: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih reported to me from al-ʿAlaʾ ibn al-Harith, who said: “As ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab was circumambulating the House, he saw a man circling while carrying his mother and reciting: ‘I am a mount that does not stumble; when men scatter, I do not flee. For a month I do not run away. After my mother, which person could I put before her?’ ʿUmar said to him: ‘You could not repay even one of her labor pains.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ: أَخْبَرَنِي مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، عَنِ الْعَلَاءِ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ، قَالَ: بَيْنَا عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ يَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ إِذْ رَأَى رَجُلًا يَطُوفُ يَحْمِلُ أُمَّهُ وَيَقُولُ: " إِنِّي مَطِيٌّ لَا أَعْثُرُ إِذِ انْتَفَرَ الرِّجَالُ لَا أَنْفِرُ لِي شَهْرًا فَبِأَيِّ شَخَصٍ مِنْهُمْ بَعْدَ أُمِّي. . فَقَالَ لَهُ عُمَرُ: «وَلَا طَلْقَةً مِنْ طَلَائِقِهَا»

records.text_en: And he informed me from Abdur-Rahman ibn Shurayh: 'A woman came to the Prophet, ﷺ, and said 'O Messenger of God, my mother has reached such an age with me that I have taken care of her as she took care of me. She has no life except through me, and I clean her as one cleans a child. Have I fulfilled what was required, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'No, you have taken care of her as you mentioned while wishing for rest from her, and she took care of you while wishing for your survival.' Abu Shurayh said: I heard Ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab say to some who said something similar: 'Not even a single favor from her.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ شُرَيْحٍ: " أَنَّ امْرَأَةً أَتَتِ النَّبِيَّ عليه السلام فَقَالَتْ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ أُمِّي بَلَغَتِ في السِّنَّ عِنْدِي حَتَّى وَلِيتُ مِنْهَا الَّذِي كَانَتْ وَلِيَتْهُ مِنِّي، وَحَتَّى لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهَا عَيْشٌ إِلَّا دَرِى، وَكُنْتُ أُنَظِّفُهَا مَا يُنَظَّفُ مِنْهُ الصَّبِيُّ، فَهَلْ بَلَغْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِذًا مَا كَانَ؟ قَالَ: «لَا، إِنَّكَ وَلِيتِ مِنْهَا الَّذِي ذَكَرْتِ وَأَنْتِ تُحِبِّينَ الرَّاحَةَ مِنْهَا، وَوَلِيَتْ ذَلِكَ مِنْكِ وَهِيَ تُحِبُّ بَقَاءَكِ» قَالَ أَبُو شُرَيْحٍ: وَسَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ قَالَ لِبَعْضِ مَنْ يَقُولُ فِي نَحْوِ ذَلِكَ: وَلَا طَلْقَةً مِنْ طَلَائِقِهَا "

records.text_en: And he informed me from Shabib ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Alqamah, from Abu Salamah ibn Abdur-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said 'The Messenger of God, ﷺ, passed by Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul while he was in the shade of a thicket. He said: 'The son of Abu Kabshah has wearied us.' His son, Abdullah ibn Abdullah, said: 'By the One who honored you and revealed the Book to you, if you wish, I will bring you his head.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'No, but be dutiful to your father.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي شَبِيبُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: " مَرَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام عَلَى عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أُبَيٍّ ابْنِ سَلُولَ وَهُوَ فِي ظِلِّ أَجَمَةٍ، فَقَالَ: قَدْ غَبَّرَ عَلَيْنَا ابْنُ أَبِي كَبْشَةَ، فَقَالَ ابْنُهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: وَالَّذِي هُوَ أَكْرَمَكَ وَأَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ، لَوْ شِئْتَ لَآتِيَنَّكَ بِرَأْسِهِ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «لَا، وَلَكِنْ بِرَّ أَبَاكَ»

records.text_en: And he informed me from Abdur-Rahman ibn Salman al-Hajri, from Ibn al-Had, from Tha'labah ibn Abi Malik, who said Umar ibn al-Khattab called the rabbis one day and called Abu Malik with them. Umar said to them: 'Speak.' Abu Malik said: 'Is there any deed you know of that, if a person does it, their lifespan will be increased?' They said: 'No.' Abu Malik called for a book, opened it, placed his hand on some of its letters, and said: 'Do you recognize what is above my hand?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you recognize what is below my hand?' They said: 'Yes.' He lifted his hand and said: 'Read.' It said: 'Whoever is dutiful to his parent, his lifespan will be increased.' He said: 'Do you recognize this?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'We testify that this is from God, and by God, we did not know this before today.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ سَلْمَانَ الْحَجْرِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْهَادِ، عَنْ ⦗ص: 184⦘ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ أَبِي مَالِكٍ، قَالَ: دَعَا عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ الْأَحْبَارَ يَوْمًا ودَعَا أَبَا مَالِكٍ مَعَهُمْ، فَقَالَ لَهُمْ عُمَرُ: تَحَدَّثُوا، فَقَالَ أَبُو مَالِكٍ: هَلْ مِنْ عَمِلٍ تَعْلَمُونَهُ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِهِ زِيدَ فِي عُمُرِهِ؟، قَالُوا: لَا، فَدَعَا أَبُو مَالِكٍ بِسِفْرٍ فَفَتَحَهُ، ثُمَّ وَضَعَ يَدَهُ عَلَى أَحْرُفٍ مِنْهُ فَقَالَ: أَتَعْرِفُونَ مَا فَوْقَ يَدِي؟، قَالُوا: نَعَمْ. قَالَ: أَتَعْرِفُونَ مَا تَحْتَ يَدِي؟ قَالُوا: نَعَمْ، فَرَفَعَ يَدَهُ قَالَ: اقْرَأُوا، فَإِذَا فِيهِ: «مَنْ بَرَّ وَالِدَهُ زِيدَ فِي عُمُرِهِ» قَالَ: تَعْرِفُونَ هَذَا؟ قَالُوا: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: «نَشْهَدُ أَنَّ هَذَا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ، وَاللَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا هَذَا قَطُّ قَبْلَ الْيَوْمِ»

records.text_en: Ibn al-Had said: It reached me that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: “May a man be disgraced who lives to see both his parents, or even one of them, yet fails to treat them dutifully and thereby enter Paradise through them.”

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Mahdi, from al-Thawri, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, regarding the verse: {And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy} [Al-Isra: 24], who said 'Do not refuse anything they love.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Mujahid, that a man asked him: 'My father calls me while the prayer has been established.' He said 'Obey your father.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنِ الْعَوَّامِ بْنِ حَوْشَبٍ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، أَنَّهُ سَأَلَهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ: " يَدْعُونِي أَبِي وَقَدْ أُقِيمَتِ الصَّلَاةُ، قَالَ: أَطِعْ أَبَاكَ "

records.text_en: It reached me that al-Hasan was asked about being dutiful to parents. He said 'Give them what you possess and obey them in what they command you, as long as it is not disobedience to God.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِي عَنِ الْحَسَنِ أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ بِرِّ الْوَالِدَيْنِ قَالَ: «أَنْ تَبْذُلَ لَهُمَا مَا مَلَكْتَ وَتُطِيعَهُمَا فِيمَا أَمَرَاكَ مَا لَمْ تَكُنْ مَعْصِيَةٌ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِي عَنِ الْحَسَنِ أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ بِرِّ الْوَالِدَيْنِ قَالَ: «أَنْ تَبْذُلَ لَهُمَا مَا مَلَكْتَ وَتُطِيعَهُمَا فِيمَا أَمَرَاكَ مَا لَمْ تَكُنْ مَعْصِيَةٌ»

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Mahdi, from al-Thawri, from Mu'awiyah ibn Ishaq, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said 'Whoever glares at his parent has not been dutiful to him.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Abu Bakr ibn Hafs, who said A man came to the Prophet, ﷺ, and said: 'O Messenger of God, I have committed a great sin.' He said: 'Do you have a mother?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Do you have a maternal aunt?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then be dutiful to her.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ مَهْدِيٍّ، عَنْ سُفْيَانَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُوقَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ حَفْصٍ، قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ عليه السلام فَقَالَ: " يَا ⦗ص: 194⦘ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنِّي أَذْنَبْتُ ذَنْبًا عَظِيمًا، فَقَالَ: «هَلْ لَكَ مِنْ وَالِدَةٍ؟» قَالَ: لَا. قَالَ: «هَلْ لَكَ مِنْ خَالَةٍ؟» قَالَ: نَعَمْ قَالَ: «فَبِرَّهَا»

records.boundary_review_note: Abu Bakr ibn Hafs’s report begins with the unnamed man’s visit; the source gives no further transmitter identity.

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Ibn Mahdi, from Umarah ibn Zadhan, who said I said to al-Hasan: 'O Abu Sa'id, to what extent does disobedience to parents go?' He said: 'You abandon them and desert them.' An elder said: 'No.' Abdullah ibn Sa'id said: I heard al-Hasan, and a man asked him: 'O Abu Sa'id, what about a parent's supplication for their child?' He said: 'It is salvation.' He said: 'And their supplication against him?' He said: 'It is destruction.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ مَهْدِيٍّ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ زَاذَانَ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِلْحَسَنِ: يَا أَبَا سَعِيدٍ إِلَى مَا يَنْتَهِي عُقُوقُ الْوَالِدَيْنِ؟ قَالَ: «تُحَرِّمُهُمَا وَتَهْجُرُهُمَا» قَالَ شَيْخٌ: لَا. فَقَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ الْحَسَنَ وَسَأَلَهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ: يَا أَبَا سَعِيدٍ، دُعَاءُ الْوَالِدِ لِوَلَدِهِ، قَالَ: نَجَاةٌ. قَالَ: دُعَاؤُهُ عَلَيْهِ اسْتِئْصَالُهُ

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Ibn Mahdi, from Muhammad ibn Sulaym, from Muwarriq al-Ijli, from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, who said 'Do you know of any expenditure better than spending in the way of God?' They said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Yes, spending on one's parents, for their supplication for good nurtures the root and the branch, and their supplication for evil dries up the root.'

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb said: Maslamah ibn ʿUlayy reported to me from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan, attributing it to the Prophet: “Two-thirds of dutifulness belongs to the mother.”

records.text_en: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmir al-Aslami reported to me that Abu Hurayrah used to say: “Any Muslim who has both parents alive and treats them dutifully will have two gates of Paradise opened for him. If one parent dies, one gate closes; if both die, both gates close.”

records.text_en: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith reported to me from Saʿid ibn Abi Hilal, who said that Kaʿb said: “By the One in whose hand is my soul, God hastens punishment for a servant who is undutiful to his parents; and God extends the life of a servant who is dutiful to them so that he may grow in righteousness and good. Kaʿb also said: ‘I find in God’s Book that if a parent calls to him and he does not answer, he has been undutiful. If he drives a parent to pray against him and complain to God about him, he has committed the fullest disobedience. If a parent entrusts him with something and he betrays that trust, he has been undutiful; and if a parent asks him for something he can afford and he refuses, he has been undutiful.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ أَبِي هِلَالٍ، قَالَ: إِنَّ كَعْبًا قَالَ: " وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَيُعَجِّلُ حِينَ الْعَبْدِ إِذَا كَانَ الْعَبْدُ ⦗ص: 203⦘ عَاقًّا لِوَالِدَيْهِ لِيُعَجِّلَ لَهُ الْعَذَابَ، وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لِيَزِيدُ فِي عُمُرِ الْعَبْدِ إِذَا كَانَ بَارًّا بِوَالِدَيْهِ لِيَزْدَادَ بِرًّا وَخَيْرًا. وَقَالَ كَعْبٌ: أَجِدُ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ أَنَّهُ إِذَا دَعَاهُ فَلَمْ يُجِبْهُ فَقَدْ عَقَّهُ، وَإِذَا أَلْجَأَهُ إِلَى أَنْ يَدْعُوَ عَلَيْهِ وَيَبْكِيَ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهُ فِيمَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهُ فَقَدْ عَقَّهُ كُلَّ الْعُقُوقِ، وَإِذَا ائْتَمَنَهُ فَخَانَهُ فَقَدْ عَقَّهُ، وَإِذَا سَأَلَهُ مِمَّا يَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهِ فَمَنَعَهُ فَقَدْ عَقَّهُ "

records.raw_text_en: 130 - And he informed me from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, that Ka'b said 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, God hastens the punishment for the servant who is disobedient to his parents, and God increases the lifespan of the servant who is dutiful to his parents so that he may increase in goodness. Ka'b said: I find in the Book of God that if he calls him and he does not answer, he has disobeyed him. If he drives him to curse him and cry to God about him, he has fully disobeyed him. records.text_en: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith reported to me from Saʿid ibn Abi Hilal, who said: “It reached him that the first thing God revealed to Moses was: ‘In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. This is God’s Book on the Tablets, in His hand, for His servant Moses: My servant, do not associate anything with Me, and do not swear falsely by My name, for I neither purify nor show mercy to one who swears falsely by My name.’ Moses said: ‘My Lord, counsel me.’ He replied: ‘I counsel you concerning your mother.’ Moses asked again, and He repeated the counsel about his mother twice more. Moses asked again; He said: ‘I counsel you concerning your father.’ Moses asked again; He said: ‘I counsel you concerning all your fellow human beings.’ Moses asked: ‘How can I care for all my fellow human beings?’ He replied: ‘Wish for them what you wish for yourself, and dislike for them what you dislike for yourself.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ أَبِي هِلَالٍ، أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ " أَنَّ أَوَّلَ، شَيْءٍ نَزَلَ مِنَ اللَّهِ عَلَى مُوسَى: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ، هَذَا كِتَابُ اللَّهِ فِي الْأَلْوَاحِ بِيَدِهِ لِعَبْدِهِ مُوسَى، عَبْدِي لَا تُشْرِكْ بِي شَيْئًا، وَلَا تَحْلِفْ بِاسْمِي كَاذِبًا فَإِنِّي لَا أُزَكِّي وَلَا أَرْحَمُ مَنْ يَحْلِفُ بِاسْمِي كَاذِبًا. قَالَ: يَا رَبِّ أَوْصِنِي قَالَ: أُوصِيكَ بِأُمِّكَ، قَالَ: يَا رَبِّ أَوْصِنِي. قَالَ: أُوصِيكَ بِأُمِّكَ، قَالَ: يَا رَبِّ أَوْصِنِي، قَالَ: أُوصِيكَ بِأُمِّكَ، قَالَ: يَا رَبِّ أَوْصِنِي، قَالَ ⦗ص: 205⦘ : أُوصِيكَ بِأَبِيكَ، قَالَ: يَا رَبِّ أَوْصِنِي قَالَ: أُوصِيكَ بِبَنِي جِنْسِكَ كُلِّهِمْ، قَالَ: وَكَيْفَ أَسْتَوْصِي بِبَنِي جِنْسِي كُلِّهِمْ؟ قَالَ: تُحِبُّ لَهُمْ مَا تُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِكَ، وَتَكْرَهُ لَهُمْ مَا تَكْرَهُ لِنَفْسِكَ "

records.text_en: Yunus ibn Yazid reported to me from Ibn Shihab, who said: ʿAmrah bint ʿAbd al-Rahman told me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “While I was asleep, I saw myself in Paradise and heard someone reciting. I asked, ‘Who is that?’ It was said: ‘That is Harithah ibn al-Nuʿman.’ Such is dutifulness; such is dutifulness; such is dutifulness. Harithah was the most dutiful of this community to his mother.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يُونُسُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَتْنِي عَمْرَةُ ⦗ص: 206⦘ ابْنَةُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: " بَيْنَمَا أَنَا نَائِمٌ رَأَيْتُنِي فِي الْجَنَّةِ، فَسَمِعْتُ صَوْتَ قَارِئٍ يَقْرَأُ، فَقُلْتُ: مَنْ هَذَا؟ فَقَالَ: هَذَا حَارِثَةُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ، كَذَلِكَ الْبِرُّ، كَذَلِكَ الْبِرُّ، كَذَلِكَ الْبِرُّ، وَكَانَ حَارِثَةُ أَبَرَّ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ بِأُمِّهِ "

He said: I advise you regarding your mother. He said: O Lord, give me advice. He said: I advise you regarding your father. He said: O Lord, give me advice. records.text_en: Makhramah ibn Bukayr reported to me from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that a man from Iraq came to him seeking a legal ruling. He had killed a daughter of his paternal aunt. Ibn ʿAbbas asked: “Do you have a mother?” He said: “No.” Ibn ʿAbbas asked: “Do you have a sister?” He said: “No.” Ibn ʿAbbas said: “Among the deeds dearest to God—or nearest to God—is dutifulness to one’s mother.” He then mentioned the sister and said to the man: “Repent to God.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مَخْرَمَةُ بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، أَنَّهُ أَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ قَتَلَ ابْنَةَ عَمَّةٍ لَهُ يَسْتَفْتِيهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ: أَلَكَ أُمٌّ؟ قَالَ: لَا. قَالَ: أَلَكَ أُخْتٌ؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: " إِنَّ أَقْرَبَ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ، أَوْ أَحَبُّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللَّهِ بِرُّ الْوَالِدَةِ، ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ الْأُخْتَ، فَقَالَ لَهُ: تُبْ إِلَى اللَّهِ "

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb said It reached me from Ata ibn Abi Rabah that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'May God have mercy on a parent who helps his child to be dutiful to him.' They said: 'How, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'He accepts his good deeds, overlooks his mistakes.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ، بَلَغَنِي عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ أَبِي رَبَاحٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «رَحِمَ اللَّهُ وَالِدًا أَعَانَ وَلَدَهُ عَلَى بِرِّهِ» ، قَالُوا: كَيْفَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ: «يَقْبَلُ إِحْسَانَهُ، وَيَتَجَاوَزُ عَنْ إِسَاءَتِهِ»
