records.boundary_review_note: Ibn Wahb’s بلغني leaves an intermediary unspecified before Ata ibn Abi Rabah; the matn begins with the Prophetic supplication.

records.text_en: Ibn Abi al-Zinad reported to me from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from someone who told him, from Abu Hurayrah, who said to a man while advising him to be dutiful to his father: “Do not walk ahead of your father, do not sit before him, do not call him by his name, and do not make yourself a cause of his being insulted.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ لِرَجُلٍ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ فِي بِرِّ أَبِيهِ: «لَا تَمْشِ أَمَامَ أَبِيكَ، وَلَا تَجْلِسْ قَبْلَهُ، وَلَا تَدَعُوهُ بِاسْمِهِ، وَلَا تَسْتَسِبَّ لَهُ»

records.raw_text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from someone who narrated to him, from Abu Hurayrah, who said to a man while advising him about being dutiful to his father: 'Do not walk ahead of your father, do not sit before him, do not call him by his name, and do not curse him.'

records.boundary_review_note: Hisham’s source is explicitly anonymous; Abu Hurayrah’s advice to a man begins the matn.

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from a trustworthy person, that a man entered upon Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz while walking ahead of his father. Umar said to him: 'Go back, do not walk ahead of your master.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، عَنِ الثِّقَةِ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا، دَخَلَ عَلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ وَهُوَ يَمْشِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْ أَبِيهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عُمَرُ: «ارْجِعْ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، لَا تَمْشِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ سَيِّدِكَ»

records.boundary_review_note: The source calls the intermediary al-thiqah (“the trustworthy”) but does not name him; the man’s visit to Umar begins the matn.

records.text_en: Bakkar ibn ʿAbd Allah reported to me from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, from Ayyub ibn Khalid al-Ansari, from Ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab: “Among the worst people are three: a man who stirs up corruption among people until they become corrupt; a man who behaves arrogantly toward his parents and despises them; and a man who works to corrupt a man’s relationship with his wife until he separates them, then marries her after him.”

records.raw_text_en: And he informed me from Bakkar ibn Abdullah, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Ayyub ibn Khalid al-Ansari, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar ibn al-Khattab: 'Among the people, there are three who are the worst: a man who strives to cause corruption among people until they become corrupt, a man who is arrogant towards his parents so that he becomes arrogant and belittles them, and a man who strives to cause corruption between a man and his wife until he separates them and then marries her after him.'

records.text_en: Al-Qasim ibn ʿAbd Allah reported to me from Ibrahim ibn Ismaʿil ibn Mujammaʿ al-Ansari, from Muhammad ibn al-Harith ibn Sufyan, from Ibn ʿIyad, who heard ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs say: “Among the major sins is for a man to make himself a cause of his parents being insulted.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مُجَمِّعٍ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ سُفْيَانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عِيَاضٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، يَقُولُ: «مِنَ الْكَبَائِرِ أَنْ يَسْتَسِبَّ، الرَّجُلُ لِوَالِدَيْهِ»

records.text_en: And Usamah ibn Zayd narrated to me that Abu Hazim narrated to him that a man came to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and said 'O Messenger of God, I have done such and such—evil deeds he mentioned. Is there any repentance, or what do you command me?' He said: 'Are your parents alive?' He said: 'One of them, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'Make it your mother.' He said: 'She is my mother, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'Go and be dutiful to her.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، أَنَّ أَبَا حَازِمٍ، حَدَّثَهُ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا جَاءَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام فَقَالَ: " يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، عَمِلْتُ كَذَا وَكَذَا، لِأَعْمَالٍ قَبِيحَةٍ ذَكَرَهَا، فَهَلْ مِنْ تَوْبَةٍ، أَوْ مَا تَأْمُرُنِي؟ قَالَ: «أَبَوَاكَ حَيَّانِ؟» قَالَ: أَحَدُهُمَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: «اجْعَلْهَا أُمَّكَ» ، قَالَ: هِيَ أُمِّي يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: «فَاذْهَبْ فَبِرَّهَا»

records.text_en: I heard Malik ibn Anas when he was asked about someone who did not live to see his parents, or one of them. He said: “There is no harm in saying: ‘My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small’ [Qurʾan 17:24].” Malik added: “A man may live with his father without caring for him, and may be away from him for a long time.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ مَالِكَ بْنَ أَنَسٍ، وَسُئِلَ، عَنِ الَّذِي لَمْ يُدْرِكْ أَبَوَيْهِ أَوْ أَحَدَهُمَا، أَنَّهُ لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَقُولَ: " اللَّهُمَّ {ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا} [الإسراء: 24] " قَالَ مَالِكٌ: «وَقَدْ يَكُونُ الرَّجُلُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ لَا يُرَبِّيهِ وَيَغِيبُ عَنْهُ لِلزَّمَانِ الطَّوِيلِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ مَالِكَ بْنَ أَنَسٍ، وَسُئِلَ، عَنِ الَّذِي لَمْ يُدْرِكْ أَبَوَيْهِ أَوْ أَحَدَهُمَا، أَنَّهُ لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَقُولَ: " اللَّهُمَّ {ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا} [الإسراء: 24] " قَالَ مَالِكٌ: «وَقَدْ يَكُونُ الرَّجُلُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ لَا يُرَبِّيهِ وَيَغِيبُ عَنْهُ لِلزَّمَانِ الطَّوِيلِ»

records.raw_text_en: And I heard Malik ibn Anas being asked about someone who did not reach his parents or one of them, and he said 'There is no harm in saying: O God, {have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small} [Al-Isra: 24].' Malik said: 'A man may be with his father but not raise him, and he may be absent from him for a long time.'

records.text_en: I heard Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah narrate from Salim ibn Abi Hafsah, from Mundhir al-Thawri, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, that he used to comb and groom his mother’s hair with a midra (a long comb or hair pick).
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ سُفْيَانَ بْنَ عُيَيْنَةَ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ سَالِمِ بْنِ أَبِي حَفْصَةَ ⦗ص: 220⦘ ، عَنْ مُنْذِرٍ الثَّوْرِيِّ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ ابْنِ الْحَنَفِيَّةِ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ يُمَشِّطُ أُمَّهُ وَيُدَرِّيهَا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ سُفْيَانَ بْنَ عُيَيْنَةَ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ سَالِمِ بْنِ أَبِي حَفْصَةَ ⦗ص: 220⦘ ، عَنْ مُنْذِرٍ الثَّوْرِيِّ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ ابْنِ الْحَنَفِيَّةِ، «أَنَّهُ كَانَ يُمَشِّطُ أُمَّهُ وَيُدَرِّيهَا»

records.text_en: And I heard Sufyan narrate from Amr ibn Dinar, from Abu Qabus, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, that he used to say: 'The merciful will be shown mercy by God. Show mercy to the people of the earth, and the people of the heavens will show mercy to you. Kinship is a branch from the Merciful. Whoever severs it, God will sever him, and whoever maintains it, God will maintain him.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Jabir ibn Ismail, from Uqayl ibn Khalid, from Ibn Shihab, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi when the Quraysh sent him during the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah: 'O Urwah, do these people have kinship with you that I do not have?' records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, who said 'Abu Hurayrah used to visit his mother every day and say: May God reward you with good, O mother, as you raised me when I was small. She would say: May God reward you with good, my son, as you were dutiful to me when I was old.'

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'No servant forms a brotherhood for the sake of God except that God raises him a degree because of it.' A man from the hypocrites said to himself: What is a degree that a man is raised or lowered? The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'It is not the step of your mother's house, but it is a degree as between the heaven and the earth.'

records.text_en: Al-Awzaʿi reported to me from ʿAbdah ibn Abi Lubabah, from Mujahid, who said: “When two people who love one another for God’s sake meet, and one walks to the other, takes his hand, and smiles at him, their sins fall away like leaves falling from a tree.” I said: “That seems easy.” He replied: “Do not say that: God says, ‘Had you spent all that is on earth, you could not have united their hearts; but God united them. He is Almighty, All-Wise’ [Qurʾan 8:63].”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْأَوْزَاعِيُّ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ عَبْدَةَ بْنِ أَبِي لُبَابَةَ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: " إِذَا تَرَاءَا الْمُتَحَابَّانِ فِي اللَّهِ فَمَشَى أَحَدُهُمَا إِلَى صَاحِبِهِ فَأَخَذَ بِيَدِهِ، ثُمَّ ضَحِكَ إِلَيْهِ تَحَاتَّتْ خَطَايَاهُمَا كَمَا تَحَاتُّ وَرَقُ الشَّجَرِ. قَالَ: قُلْتُ: إِنَّ هَذَا لَيَسِيرٌ. قَالَ: لَا تَقُلْ ذَلِكَ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ: {لَوْ أَنْفَقْتَ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا مَا أَلَّفْتَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ، وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ أَلَّفَ بَيْنَهُمْ، إِنَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ} [الأنفال: 63] "

records.text_en: Al-Awzaʿi reported to me from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “The people of the higher ranks in Paradise visit those below them. Those below do not visit those above them, except for one who used to visit others for God’s sake in this world; that person may visit wherever he wishes in Paradise.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْأَوْزَاعِيُّ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يَزُورُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ الْأَسْفَلِينَ، وَلَا يَزُورُ الْأَسْفَلُونَ الْأَعْلَيِينَ إِلَّا مَنْ كَانَ يَزُورُ فِي اللَّهِ فِي الدُّنْيَا، فَذَلِكَ يَزُورُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ حَيْثُ يَشَاءُ»

records.text_en: Someone who had heard Yazid ibn Muhammad reported to me from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Halhalah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: “I used to enter the mosque of Hims and see a group of middle-aged men and a youth with dark, kohl-lined eyes and gleaming front teeth. They would discuss jurisprudence without disputing. Whenever something puzzled them, they looked to the youth; whatever he said, they accepted. I admired their conduct and grew attached to them. I asked about the youth and learned that he was Muʿadh ibn Jabal. When his companions left, I sat with him and said: ‘Muʿadh ibn Jabal, I love you for God’s sake.’ He replied: ‘If you are sincere, I have heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: “Those who love one another for God’s sake—or for His majesty—will be on pulpits of light in the shade of the Throne, to the right of the All-Merciful, on the Day of Resurrection.”’” [The source text breaks off after this report.]

records.text_en: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAyyash reported to me from Yazid ibn Qawthar, from Kaʿb, who said: “Many a person who stands [in prayer] is thanked, and many a sleeper is forgiven. Two men love one another for God’s sake. One rises to pray, and God accepts his prayer, but grants him none of what he asks. During the night he remembers his brother in his supplication and says, ‘My Lord, forgive my brother so-and-so,’ and God forgives his brother while he sleeps.” Kaʿb said: “Those who love one another for God’s sake will be on columns of red ruby, with a thousand dwellings at the top of each column, overlooking the people of Paradise. Written on their foreheads will be: ‘These are those who love one another for God’s sake.’ When one appears, his beauty will fill the people of Paradise as the sun fills the people of the earth. They will say, ‘One of those who love for God’s sake has appeared,’ and look at his face as they look at the full moon.”

records.raw_text_en: 163 - And he informed me from someone who heard Yazid ibn Muhammad narrate from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Halhalah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, that he used to enter the mosque of Homs and see the people of a gathering—elders and a bright-eyed, gleaming-toothed young man—debating the pursuit of knowledge without contention. When something was unclear to them, they looked at the young man, and whatever he said , they accepted. I was amazed by this and grew fond of them. I asked about the young man and found out he was Mu'adh ibn Jabal. His companions rose, and I sat next to him. I said: 'Mu'adh ibn Jabal, I love you for the sake of God.' He said: 'If you are truthful, I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: The ones who love each other for the majesty of God will be on pulpits of light in the shade of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection.'

records.text_en: Yaʿqub ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman reported to me from Abu Hazim, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “A believer’s place among the faithful is like the head’s place in the body. A believer feels pain at what befalls the faithful just as the body feels pain at what befalls the head.”

records.raw_text_en: 166 - And he narrated to me from Quraysh ibn Hayyan, from Thabit al-Bunani, who said 'When we came to Anas ibn Malik, if he saw us, he would call for perfume and apply it to his hands for shaking hands with his brothers.'
records.display_text_en: Yaʿqub ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman reported to me from Abu Hazim, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “A believer’s place among the faithful is like the head’s place in the body. A believer feels pain at what befalls the faithful just as the body feels pain at what befalls the head.”

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Sa'd ibn Habib, that al-Hasan said 'Whoever escorts his brother for the sake of God, God will send angels from beneath His Throne on the Day of Resurrection to escort him to Paradise.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ حَبِيبٍ، قَالَ الْحَسَنَ: «مَنْ شَيَّعَ أَخًا لَهُ فِي اللَّهِ بَعَثَ اللَّهُ لَهُ مَلَائِكَةً مِنْ تَحْتِ عَرْشِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يُشَيِّعُونَهُ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ»

records.text_en: And it reached me from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Whoever visits a sick person or visits his brother for the sake of God, God will send a caller from the heavens saying: You are good, and your walking is good. You have taken a dwelling in Paradise.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَبَلَغَنِي عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «مَنْ عَادَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ زَارَ أَخًا لَهُ بَعَثَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ مُنَادِيًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ أَنْ طِبْتَ وَطَابَ مَمْشَاكَ، قَدْ تَبَوَّأْتَ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ مَنْزِلًا»

records.text_en: Abu Qilabah said: “When a servant goes out to meet his brother and renew their acquaintance, God sends a caller from the lowest heaven to proclaim: ‘You are good, your journey is good, and Paradise is yours.’ God says: ‘By My mercy, this is for Me, and I will provide his hospitality.’”
records.text_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو قِلَابَةَ: " إِذَا خَرَجَ الْعَبْدُ لِيَلْقَى أَخَاهُ يُحْدِثُ بِهِ عَهْدًا، بَعَثَ اللَّهُ مُنَادِيًا يُنَادِي مِنَ السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا أَنْ طِبْتَ وَطَابَ مَمْشَاكَ، لَكَ الْجَنَّةُ. يَقُولُ اللَّهُ: بِرَوْحِي هَذَا، وَعَلَيَّ قِرَاؤُهُ "
records.raw_text_ar: وَقَالَ أَبُو قِلَابَةَ: " إِذَا خَرَجَ الْعَبْدُ لِيَلْقَى أَخَاهُ يُحْدِثُ بِهِ عَهْدًا، بَعَثَ اللَّهُ مُنَادِيًا يُنَادِي مِنَ السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا أَنْ طِبْتَ وَطَابَ مَمْشَاكَ، لَكَ الْجَنَّةُ. يَقُولُ اللَّهُ: بِرَوْحِي هَذَا، وَعَلَيَّ قِرَاؤُهُ "

records.raw_text_en: Abu Qilabah said 'When a servant goes out to meet his brother with whom he has an appointment, God sends a caller from the heavens of the world saying: You are good, and your walking is good. Paradise is yours. God says: By My glory, this is for him, and I am responsible for his reward.'

records.text_en: And it reached me from al-Hasan, who said 'It is said: A man does not fully advise someone until he commands him to do what he cannot.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَبَلَغَنِي عَنِ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ: يُقَالُ: «لَا يُبَلِّغُ الرَّجُلُ النَّصِيحَةَ كُلَّ النَّصِيحَةِ لِأَحَدٍ حَتَّى يَأْمُرَهُ بِمَا عَجَزَ عَنْهُ»

records.text_en: And he informed me from Maslamah ibn Ali, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, raising it to the Prophet, ﷺ, who said 'When one of you has his brother visit, let him offer him what he has, even if it is just a drink of water.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Abdur-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from al-Thawri, from Ziyad ibn al-Fayyad al-Khuza'i, from Tamim ibn Salamah, who said 'Umar ibn al-Khattab returned from a journey, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah kissed his hand. Then they secluded themselves and conversed until they both wept.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ مَهْدِيٍّ، عَنِ الثَّوْرِيِّ، عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ الْفَيَّاضِ الْخُزَاعِيِّ، عَنْ تَمِيمِ بْنِ سَلَمَةَ، قَالَ: قَدِمَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ مِنْ سَفَرٍ فَقَبَّلَ يَدَهُ أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ بْنُ الْجَرَّاحِ، ثُمَّ خَلَوَا يَتَنَاجَيَانِ حَتَّى بَكَيَا جَمِيعًا "

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Ibn Mahdi, from al-Hasan ibn al-Khalil, that Umar ibn al-Khattab said 'If one of you knew what is in saying to his brother, 'May God reward you with good,' he would say it often.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Maslamah ibn Ali, from Zayd ibn Waqid and Hisham ibn al-Ghazi, from Makhul, who said 'Walk a mile to visit a sick person, walk two miles to reconcile between two people, and walk three miles to visit for the sake of God.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ 175 - وَأَخْبَرَنِي مَسْلَمَةُ بْنُ عُلَيٍّ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ وَاقِدٍ، وَهِشَامِ بْنِ الْغَازِي، عَنْ مَكْحُولٍ، قَالَ: «امْشِ مِيلًا عُدْ مَرِيضًا، امْشِ مِيلَيْنِ أَصْلِحْ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ، امْشِ ثَلَاثَةً زُرْ فِي اللَّهِ» ⦗ص: 262⦘

records.text_en: Someone who heard Saʿid ibn Abi Ayyub reported to me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Shall I tell you which of your men are among the people of Paradise?” They said: “Yes, Messenger of God.” He replied: “The prophets, the truthful, and a man who visits his brother for God’s sake.” He then asked: “Shall I tell you which of your women are among the people of Paradise?” They said: “Yes, Messenger of God.” He replied: “The affectionate, childbearing woman who returns to her husband: if she does wrong or is wronged, she takes his hand and says, ‘I will not sleep until you are pleased.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي مَنْ، سَمِعَ سَعِيدَ بْنَ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ، يَقُولُ: إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «أَلَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِرِجَالِكُمْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ؟» ، قَالُوا: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ: «النَّبِيِّينَ، وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ، وَرَجُلٍ زَارَ أَخَاهُ فِي اللَّهِ» . قَالَ: «أَلَا أُخْبِرُكُمْ بِنِسَائِكُمْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ؟» ، قَالُوا: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ: " الْوَدُودُ، وَالْوَلُودُ، الْعَؤُودُ الَّتِي إِذَا أَسَاءَتْ أَوْ أُسِيءَ إِلَيْهَا وَضَعَتْ يَدَهَا فِي يَدِهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَتِ: اعْمَلْ وَافْعَلْ مَا بَدَا لَكَ "

records.text_en: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr reported to me from al-Thawri, from a man, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: “When Jaʿfar returned from Abyssinia, the Messenger of God, ﷺ, welcomed him, kissed him between the eyes, and fell silent.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ الثَّوْرِيِّ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، قَالَ: «لَمَّا قَدِمَ جَعْفَرٌ مِنَ الْحَبَشَةِ اسْتَقْبَلَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَبَّلَ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ وَصَمَتَ»

records.raw_text_en: 177 - And he narrated to me from someone who heard Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub say that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Shall I inform you about your men from the people of Paradise?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'The prophets, the truthful, and a man who visits his brother for the sake of God.' He said: 'Shall I inform you about your women from the people of Paradise?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'The loving, the fertile, the repentant who, if she does wrong or is wronged, places her hand in his and says: Do as you wish.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Haywah ibn Shurayh, from Bakr ibn Amr, from someone he trusted: 'When a man visits his brother for the sake of God, no angel remains in the heavens except that he greets him with a new greeting, unlike any greeting from another angel. Each angel greets him with a unique greeting. No tree among all the trees of Paradise remains except that it informs its companion: So-and-so, the son of so-and-so, has visited so-and-so for the sake of God.'

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Diraj, from Isa ibn Hilal, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, who said 'The souls of two believers meet even if they are a day's journey apart and have never seen each other.'

narrator_path.source_form: عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ

records.boundary_review_note: The matn begins with the report about the souls of two believers meeting.

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Sam'an, who said: I heard men of knowledge narrate from our predecessors, the companions of the Messenger of God, ﷺ: 'For one of them, the night would become long until morning so he could look at his brother's face. On their journeys, a tree would separate two men, and they would go around it, intertwining with each other out of intense longing for their brother and the purity of their hearts towards him.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ سَمْعَانَ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رِجَالًا، مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ يُحَدِّثُونَ عَنْ سَلَفِنَا، مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ مِنْهُمْ كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ تَطُولُ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ فَيَنْظُرَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيهِ، وَأَنَّهُمْ فِي أَسْفَارِهِمْ كَانَتِ الشَّجَرَةُ تُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ الرَّجُلَيْنِ، فَيَلْتَفُّونَ مِنْ وَرَائِهَا فَيُشَابِكُ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا مِنْ شِدَّةِ تَشَوُّقِهِ إِلَى أَخِيهِ، وَسَلَامَةِ صَدْرِهِ لَهُ»

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ مِنْهُمْ كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ تَطُولُ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ فَيَنْظُرَ فِي وَجْهِ أَخِيهِ، وَأَنَّهُمْ فِي أَسْفَارِهِمْ كَانَتِ الشَّجَرَةُ تُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ الرَّجُلَيْنِ، فَيَلْتَفُّونَ مِنْ وَرَائِهَا فَيُشَابِكُ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا مِنْ شِدَّةِ تَشَوُّقِهِ إِلَى أَخِيهِ، وَسَلَامَةِ صَدْرِهِ لَهُ»
records.isnad_en: And he informed me from Ibn Sam'an, who said: I heard men of knowledge narrate from our predecessors, the companions of the Messenger of God, ﷺ: '
records.matn_en: For one of them, the night would become long until morning so he could look at his brother's face. On their journeys, a tree would separate two men, and they would go around it, intertwining with each other out of intense longing for their brother and the purity of their hearts towards him.'

records.text_en: Hisham ibn Saʿd reported to me from Ghalib ibn ʿUbayd God, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “God continues to help a servant as long as the servant is helping his brother.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ غَالِبِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ الْهَمْدَانِيِّ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «لَا يَزَالُ اللَّهُ فِي حَاجَةِ الْعَبْدِ مَا كَانَ فِي حَاجَةِ أَخِيهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ غَالِبِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ الْهَمْدَانِيِّ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «لَا يَزَالُ اللَّهُ فِي حَاجَةِ الْعَبْدِ مَا كَانَ فِي حَاجَةِ أَخِيهِ»

records.raw_text_en: And he narrated to me from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Ghalib ibn Ubaydullah, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'God remains in the need of the servant as long as he is in the need of his brother.'

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb said al-Harith ibn Nabhan informed me from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash that Salman entered upon Umar ibn al-Khattab, who placed a cushion for him. He sat on it and said: 'Allahu Akbar.' Umar said: 'One of your wonders, O Abu Abdullah.' He said: 'I heard the Messenger of God say: When one of you, a Muslim, places something for his brother to honor him and he sits on it... they are both forgiven.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ: أَخْبَرَنِي الْحَارِثُ بْنُ نَبْهَانَ، عَنْ أَبَانَ بْنِ أَبِي عَيَّاشٍ أَنَّ سَلْمَانَ دَخَلَ عَلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ فَأَلْقَى لَهُ وِسَادَةً، فَجَلَسَ عَلَيْهَا، فَقَالَ: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، قَالَ عُمَرُ: بَعْضُ أَعَاجِيبِكَ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ يَقُولُ: «إِذَا أَلْقَى أَحَدُكُمُ الْمُسْلِمُ لِأَخِيهِ شَيْئًا يُكْرِمُهُ بِهِ فَجَلَسَ عَلَيْهِ. . . غُفِرَ لَهُمَا»

records.text_en: And he informed me from Ashhal ibn Hatim, from a man who narrated to him from al-Hakam, from al-Bara ibn Azib, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'When two Muslims meet, shake hands, praise God, and seek His forgiveness, they are forgiven.'

records.text_en: And he informed me... from Abdullah ibn Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, who said I said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal: 'By God, I love you for the sake of God.' He said: 'Why?' I said: 'For the majesty of God...' until he placed his knees against mine. Then he said: 'Rejoice, for I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: Those who love each other for the majesty of God are in the shade of God on the Day when there is no shade but His.' Then he mentioned Ubadah ibn al-Samit, and I said: 'Will you not listen? I am telling you good news, shall I not tell you?' I said: 'Tell me.' He said: '... My love is due for those who love each other in Me, My love is due for those who give to each other in Me, My love is due for those who... My love is due for those who visit each other in Me.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي. . . عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي حُسَيْنٍ، عَنْ شَهْرِ بْنِ حَوْشَبٍ، عَنْ أَبِي إِدْرِيسَ الْخَوْلَانِيِّ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِمُعَاذِ بْنِ جَبَلٍ ⦗ص: 280⦘ : وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّكَ لِلَّهِ قَالَ: لِمَ؟ قَالَ: مِنْ جَلَالِ اللَّهِ. . . حَتَّى أَلْصَقَ رُكْبَتَيَّ بِرُكْبَتِهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَبْشِرْ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام يَقُولُ: «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَتَحَابُّونَ مِنْ جَلَالِ اللَّهِ فِي ظِلِّ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ» قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَلْقَى عُبَادَةَ بْنَ الصَّامِتِ، فَقُلْتُ: أَلَا تَسْمَعُ، أُخْبِرُكَ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ، أَلَا أُحَدِّثُكَ؟ فَقُلْتُ: حَدِّثْنِي قَالَ:. . . حَقَّتْ مَحَبَّتِي لِلَّذِينَ يَتَحَابُّونَ فِيَّ، حَقَّتْ مَحَبَّتِي لِلَّذِينَ يَتَبَاذَلُونَ فِيَّ، حَقَّتْ مَحَبَّتِي لِلَّذِينَ. . .، حَقَّتْ مَحَبَّتِي لِلَّذِينَ يَتَزَاوَرُونَ فِيَّ "

records.text_en: And he narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Nashit... from Abdur-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Abu Malik and Abu Amir, that while they were with the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and this verse was revealed: {O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you} [Al-Ma'idah: 101], the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Peace is the attribute of a people who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whom the prophets and martyrs envy for their closeness and position with God on the Day of Resurrection.' They fell silent and did not ask about anything. A Bedouin knelt and said: 'O Messenger of God, tell us about them so we may know them.' I saw the Bedouin say: 'They are servants of God from various lands and tribes, with no kinship ties to connect them, nor worldly possessions to exchange. They love each other with the spirit of God. God will place for them pulpits of red ruby before the Most Merciful. People will be terrified, but they will not be terrified. People will fear, but they will not fear.'

records.raw_text_en: And he narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Nashit... from Abdur-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Abu Malik and Abu Amir, that while they were with the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and this verse was revealed: {O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you} [Al-Ma'idah: 101], the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Peace is the attribute of a people who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whom the prophets and martyrs envy for their closeness and position with God on the Day of Resurrection.' They fell silent and did not ask about anything. A Bedouin knelt and said: 'O Messenger of God, tell us about them so we may know them.' I saw the Bedouin say: 'They are servants of God from various lands and tribes, with no kinship ties to connect them, nor worldly possessions to exchange. They love each other with the spirit of God. God will place for them pulpits of red ruby before the Most Merciful. People will be terrified, but they will not be terrified. People will fear, but they will not fear.'

records.text_en: Al-Harith ibn Nabhan reported to me from Muhammad ibn Saʿid, from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: “Deceit, betrayal, and treachery lead to the Fire. Betrayal includes a man concealing from his brother something that, if he knew it, might help him attain good or escape harm.” It was asked: “Messenger of God, should each of us reveal to his brother what is in his heart?” He replied: “Yes, except what would neither harm nor benefit him.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْحَارِثُ بْنُ نَبْهَانَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ عُبَادَةَ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ، يَقُولُ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام يَقُولُ: «الْمَكْرُ وَالْخِيَانَةُ وَالْخَدِيعَةُ فِي النَّارِ، وَمِنَ الْخِيَانَةِ أَنْ يَكْتُمَ الرَّجُلُ أَخَاهُ مَا لَوْ عَلِمَهُ كَانَ عَسَى أَنْ يُدْرِكَ بِهِ خَيْرًا، أَوْ يَنْجُوَ بِهِ مِنْ سُوءٍ» . قِيلَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَيُظْهِرُ أَحَدُنَا لِأَخِيهِ مَا فِي نَفْسِهِ؟ قَالَ: «نَعَمْ، إِلَّا مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُ وَلَا يَنْفَعُهُ»

records.text_en: Someone also reported to me: “A man from an earlier people set out to visit a brother of his for God’s sake in another village. God sent an angel along his route. When the angel met him, he asked: ‘Where are you going?’ The man replied: ‘To visit a brother of mine.’ The angel asked: ‘Are you related to him?’ He said: ‘No; I love him only for God’s sake.’ The angel said: ‘I am a messenger from your Lord to tell you that He loves you as you love that man for His sake.’”

" أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ خَرَجَ يَزُورُ أَخًا لَهُ فِي اللَّهِ فِي قَرْيَةٍ أُخْرَى فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَدْرَجَتِهِ مَلَكًا، فَلَمَّا أَتَى عَلَيْهِ قَالَ: أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ؟ قَالَ: أَزُورُ أَخًا لِي، قَالَ: أَبَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ رَحِمٌ؟ قَالَ: لَا، غَيْرَ أَنِّي أَحْبَبْتُهُ لِلَّهِ. قَالَ: فَإِنِّي رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ إِلَيْكَ أَنَّهُ يُحِبُّكَ كَمَا أَحْبَبْتَهُ فِيهِ " ⦗ص: 293⦘ ،

records.raw_text_en: 194 - And he informed me from Shabib ibn Sa'id, from Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Ishaq... 'A man is with those he accompanies, so he only accompanies his like.'
records.display_text_en: Someone also reported to me: “A man from an earlier people set out to visit a brother of his for God’s sake in another village. God sent an angel along his route. When the angel met him, he asked: ‘Where are you going?’ The man replied: ‘To visit a brother of mine.’ The angel asked: ‘Are you related to him?’ He said: ‘No; I love him only for God’s sake.’ The angel said: ‘I am a messenger from your Lord to tell you that He loves you as you love that man for His sake.’”

records.matn_en: Someone also reported to me: “A man from an earlier people set out to visit a brother of his for God’s sake in another village. God sent an angel along his route. When the angel met him, he asked: ‘Where are you going?’ The man replied: ‘To visit a brother of mine.’ The angel asked: ‘Are you related to him?’ He said: ‘No; I love him only for God’s sake.’ The angel said: ‘I am a messenger from your Lord to tell you that He loves you as you love that man for His sake.’”
records.boundary_review_note: The source omits the isnad; the parable begins with a man setting out to visit his brother.

records.text_en: Muʿadh ibn Fadalah reported to me from Hisham ibn Abi ʿAbd Allah, from Qatadah, who said: “… his brother returned from a journey. Should he take him by the hand?” He replied: “It was customary …” [The Arabic fragment is incomplete.]
records.text_ar: 197 - قَالَ: وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُعَاذُ بْنُ فَضَالَةَ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، قَالَ:. . . أَخَاهُ جَاءَ مِنْ سَفَرٍ أَيَأْخُذُ بِيَدِهِ قَالَ: قَدْ كَانَ. . .
records.source_number_note_en: The export ran this report into the end of report 196 and dropped its number; it is separated here, as the edition prints it. Its English is given with report 196.

records.boundary_review_note: The Arabic and English are fragmentary at both ends; missing wording is not supplied. The attribution reaches Qatadah.

records.text_en: Al-Khalil ibn Murrah reported to me from Aban ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Whenever two people form a bond of brotherhood, the one most beloved to God is the one who loves his companion more.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْخَلِيلُ بْنُ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ أَبَانَ بْنِ أَبِي عَيَّاشٍ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «مَا تَواخَى اثْنَانِ قَطُّ إِلَّا كَانَ أَحَبُّهُمَا إِلَى اللَّهِ أَشَدَّهُمَا حُبًّا لِصَاحِبِهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْخَلِيلُ بْنُ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ أَبَانَ بْنِ أَبِي عَيَّاشٍ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «مَا تَواخَى اثْنَانِ قَطُّ إِلَّا كَانَ أَحَبُّهُمَا إِلَى اللَّهِ أَشَدَّهُمَا حُبًّا لِصَاحِبِهِ»
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْخَلِيلُ بْنُ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ أَبَانَ بْنِ أَبِي عَيَّاشٍ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «مَا تَواخَى اثْنَانِ قَطُّ إِلَّا كَانَ أَحَبُّهُمَا إِلَى اللَّهِ أَشَدَّهُمَا حُبًّا لِصَاحِبِهِ»
records.raw_text_en: 195 - And he informed me... that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Do not spy, and be servants of God as brothers, as God has commanded you.'
records.display_text_en: Al-Khalil ibn Murrah reported to me from Aban ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Whenever two people form a bond of brotherhood, the one most beloved to God is the one who loves his companion more.”
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي الْخَلِيلُ بْنُ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ أَبَانَ بْنِ أَبِي عَيَّاشٍ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «
records.matn_ar: مَا تَواخَى اثْنَانِ قَطُّ إِلَّا كَانَ أَحَبُّهُمَا إِلَى اللَّهِ أَشَدَّهُمَا حُبًّا لِصَاحِبِهِ»
records.isnad_en: And he informed me from al-Khalil ibn Murrah, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said '
records.matn_en: Al-Khalil ibn Murrah reported to me from Aban ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Whenever two people form a bond of brotherhood, the one most beloved to God is the one who loves his companion more.”
records.boundary_review_note: The matn begins with the Messenger’s statement about two people forming brotherhood.

records.text_en: 196 - And he also informed me... 'A man from before you set out to visit his brother for the sake of God in another village. God sent an angel in his path. When he came upon him, he said Where are you going? He said: I am visiting my brother. He said: Is there any kinship between you and him? He said: No, except that I love him for the sake of God. He said: I am the messenger of your Lord to you, that He loves you as you have loved him for His sake.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ أَبِي عِيسَى، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ الشَّعْبِيَّ، يَقُولُ: «مَا تَحَابَّ اثْنَانِ فِي اللَّهِ فَفَرَّقَ بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا حَدَثٌ أَحْدَثَهُ أَحَدُهُمَا، وَالْمُحْدِثُ شَرُّهُمَا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ أَبِي عِيسَى، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ الشَّعْبِيَّ، يَقُولُ: «مَا تَحَابَّ اثْنَانِ فِي اللَّهِ فَفَرَّقَ بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا حَدَثٌ أَحْدَثَهُ أَحَدُهُمَا، وَالْمُحْدِثُ شَرُّهُمَا»
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ أَبِي عِيسَى، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ الشَّعْبِيَّ، يَقُولُ: «مَا تَحَابَّ اثْنَانِ فِي اللَّهِ فَفَرَّقَ بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا حَدَثٌ أَحْدَثَهُ أَحَدُهُمَا، وَالْمُحْدِثُ شَرُّهُمَا»
records.raw_text_en: 196 - And he also informed me... 'A man from before you set out to visit his brother for the sake of God in another village. God sent an angel in his path. When he came upon him, he said Where are you going? He said: I am visiting my brother. He said: Is there any kinship between you and him? He said: No, except that I love him for the sake of God. He said: I am the messenger of your Lord to you, that He loves you as you have loved him for His sake.'
records.display_text_en: And he informed me from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Isa ibn Abi Isa, that he heard al-Sha'bi say: 'No two have loved each other for the sake of God and then separated except that one of them committed a sin, and the one who committed the sin is the worse of the two.'
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ أَبِي عِيسَى، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ الشَّعْبِيَّ، يَقُولُ: «
records.matn_ar: مَا تَحَابَّ اثْنَانِ فِي اللَّهِ فَفَرَّقَ بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا حَدَثٌ أَحْدَثَهُ أَحَدُهُمَا، وَالْمُحْدِثُ شَرُّهُمَا»
records.isnad_en: And he informed me from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Isa ibn Abi Isa, that he heard al-Sha'bi say: '
records.matn_en: No two have loved each other for the sake of God and then separated except that one of them committed a sin, and the one who committed the sin is the worse of the two.'
records.boundary_review_note: The matn is the statement attributed to al-Shabi about two people who love each other for Allah.

records.text_en: 197 - And he informed me from Mu'adh ibn Fadalah, from Hisham ibn Abi Abdullah, from Qatadah, who said '... his brother returns from a journey, does he take his hand? It used to be...'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي أَشْهَلُ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ، عَنْ مَنْ، حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، قَالَ: «لَمَّا قَدِمَ جَعْفَرٌ مِنَ الْحَبَشَةِ قَبَّلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام جِلْدَهُ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي أَشْهَلُ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ، عَنْ مَنْ، حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، قَالَ: «لَمَّا قَدِمَ جَعْفَرٌ مِنَ الْحَبَشَةِ قَبَّلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام جِلْدَهُ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ»
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي أَشْهَلُ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ، عَنْ مَنْ، حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، قَالَ: «لَمَّا قَدِمَ جَعْفَرٌ مِنَ الْحَبَشَةِ قَبَّلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام جِلْدَهُ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_en: 197 - And he informed me from Mu'adh ibn Fadalah, from Hisham ibn Abi Abdullah, from Qatadah, who said '... his brother returns from a journey, does he take his hand? It used to be...'
records.display_text_en: And he informed me from Ashhal ibn Hatim, from someone who narrated to him from al-Sha'bi, who said 'When Ja'far returned from Abyssinia, the Messenger of God, ﷺ, kissed the skin between his eyes.'
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي أَشْهَلُ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ، عَنْ مَنْ، حَدَّثَهُ عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، قَالَ: «
records.matn_ar: لَمَّا قَدِمَ جَعْفَرٌ مِنَ الْحَبَشَةِ قَبَّلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام جِلْدَهُ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ»
records.isnad_en: And he informed me from Ashhal ibn Hatim, from someone who narrated to him from al-Sha'bi, who said '
records.matn_en: When Ja'far returned from Abyssinia, the Messenger of God, ﷺ, kissed the skin between his eyes.'
records.boundary_review_note: The transmitter between Ashhal and al-Shabi is anonymous. The account of Jaafar’s return from Abyssinia begins the matn.

records.text_en: 198 - And he informed me from al-Khalil ibn Murrah, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'No two have ever formed a brotherhood except that the more beloved of them to God is the one who loves his companion more.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ الْأَعْمَشِ، قَالَ: قَالَ سَلْمَانُ: «مَثَلُ الْمُسْلِمِ وَأَخِيهِ كَمَثَلِ الْكَفَّيْنِ تُنَقِّي إِحْدَاهُمَا الْأُخْرَى»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ الْأَعْمَشِ، قَالَ: قَالَ سَلْمَانُ: «مَثَلُ الْمُسْلِمِ وَأَخِيهِ كَمَثَلِ الْكَفَّيْنِ تُنَقِّي إِحْدَاهُمَا الْأُخْرَى»
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ الْأَعْمَشِ، قَالَ: قَالَ سَلْمَانُ: «مَثَلُ الْمُسْلِمِ وَأَخِيهِ كَمَثَلِ الْكَفَّيْنِ تُنَقِّي إِحْدَاهُمَا الْأُخْرَى»
records.raw_text_en: 198 - And he informed me from al-Khalil ibn Murrah, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'No two have ever formed a brotherhood except that the more beloved of them to God is the one who loves his companion more.'
records.display_text_en: And he informed me from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Sulayman al-A'mash, who said Salman said: 'The example of a Muslim and his brother is like two hands, each cleansing the other.'
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ الْأَعْمَشِ، قَالَ: قَالَ سَلْمَانُ: «
records.matn_ar: مَثَلُ الْمُسْلِمِ وَأَخِيهِ كَمَثَلِ الْكَفَّيْنِ تُنَقِّي إِحْدَاهُمَا الْأُخْرَى»
records.isnad_en: And he informed me from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Sulayman al-A'mash, who said Salman said: '
records.matn_en: The example of a Muslim and his brother is like two hands, each cleansing the other.'
records.boundary_review_note: The matn is Salman’s parable about a Muslim and his brother.

records.text_en: Sulayman ibn Bilal and Jarir ibn Hazim reported to me that the Prophet, ﷺ, said: “A Muslim is a mirror for his brother.”

records.text_en: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih reported to me from Abu Zahiriyyah, from Abu al-Dardaʾ, who used to say: “Make your brother a true brother, and be gentle with him. Do not reproach him for a mistaken word, lest you become like him. When death comes to him, it will have spared you until after him. When he dies, you will speak of him often—yet while he lived, you did not sever your bond with him.” [The Arabic poem is difficult and may be corrupt.]

records.text_en: Ibn Anʿam reported to me from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “If a man loves another for God’s sake and tells him, ‘I love you for God’s sake,’ they will both enter Paradise. The one who loved for God’s sake will have the higher rank, and his companion will be brought up to join him.”

records.text_en: Ibn Anʿam said: “It reached me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: ‘On the Day of Resurrection, those who love one another for God’s sake will be brought forward and pulpits of pearls will be set out for them in the shade of the Throne, until judgment is passed among the first and the last.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ أَنْعَمَ: وَبَلَغَنِي أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «يُؤْتَى بِالْمُتَحَابِّينَ فِي اللَّهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، فَيُوضَعُ لَهُمْ مَنَابِرُ مِنْ دُرٍّ فِي ظِلِّ الْعَرْشِ، حَتَّى يُقْضَى بَيْنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ»

records.text_en: 206 - Ibn An'am said It reached me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'The ones who love each other for the sake of God will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and pulpits of pearls will be placed for them in the shade of the Throne until the judgment is passed between the first and the last.'

records.display_text_en: Ibn Wahb said Ibn Lahi'ah and Khalid ibn Humayd informed me from Uqayl ibn Khalid, from Ibn Shihab: 'The companions, when they traveled and a tree came between one of them and his companion, they would meet and ask: How are you, my brother, as a right of Islamic brotherhood?'

records.matn_en: The companions, when they traveled and a tree came between one of them and his companion, they would meet and ask: How are you, my brother, as a right of Islamic brotherhood?'
records.boundary_review_note: Ibn Lahiah and Khalid ibn Humayd are parallel transmitters from Uqayl ibn Khalid; the matn reports the Companions’ practice.

records.display_text_en: And he informed me from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Abu Rafi', from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'It is a right upon the believers to feel pain for each other as the body feels pain from the head.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “A believer’s relationship to his fellow believer is like two hands; neither can do without the other.”

records.text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah, Dawud ibn Qays, and Hisham ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said to him: “Let your love not become excessive attachment, and let your hatred not become destructive.” Hisham’s version adds that ʿUmar said this to Aslam while reproving him: “Let your hatred not become enmity.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، وَدَاوُدُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ، وَهِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، قَالَ لَهُ: «لَا يَكُونَنَّ حُبُّكَ كَلَفًا وَلَا يَكُونَنَّ بُغْضُكَ تَلَفًا» إِلَّا أَنَّ هِشَامًا قَالَ فِي الْحَدِيثِ: قَالَ يَوْمًا لَأَسْلَمَ وَهُوَ يُعَاتِبَهُ: وَلَا يَكُونَنَّ بُغْضُكَ عَدَاوَةً
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، وَدَاوُدُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ، وَهِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، قَالَ لَهُ: «لَا يَكُونَنَّ حُبُّكَ كَلَفًا وَلَا يَكُونَنَّ بُغْضُكَ تَلَفًا» إِلَّا أَنَّ هِشَامًا قَالَ فِي الْحَدِيثِ: قَالَ يَوْمًا لَأَسْلَمَ وَهُوَ يُعَاتِبَهُ: وَلَا يَكُونَنَّ بُغْضُكَ عَدَاوَةً

records.raw_text_en: 210 - And he informed me from Khalid ibn Humayd, from Yahya ibn Abi Usayd, that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said 'When we missed a brother, we would visit him. If he was sick, it was a visit. If he was busy, it was assistance. If it was otherwise, it was a social call.'

records.text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “A believer’s blood, property, and honor are inviolable to another believer. A believer is his brother: he must not abandon him or wrong him. God-consciousness is here”—and he pointed to his chest. “It is enough evil for a person to despise his Muslim brother.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «الْمُؤْمِنُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِ حَرَامٌ، دَمُهُ، وَمَالُهُ، وَعِرْضُهُ، الْمُؤْمِنُ أَخُو الْمُؤْمِنِ، لَا يَخْذُلْهُ، وَلَا يَظْلِمْهُ، التَّقْوَى هَاهُنَا، وَأَشَارَ إِلَى صَدْرِهِ، حَسْبُ امْرِئٍ مِنَ الشَّرِّ أَنْ يَحْقِرَ أَخَاهُ الْمُؤْمِنَ»

records.text_en: Uthman ibn Atā’ narrated from his father, from Al-Barā’ ibn ‘Āzib, that he heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: 'When a Muslim meets his brother and greets him with peace and shakes his hand, neither of them removes his hand from the other’s hand until they are forgiven.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ بْنِ عَازِبٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام يَقُولُ: «إِذَا لَقِيَ الْمُسْلِمُ أَخَاهُ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَصَافَحَهُ لَمْ يَنْزِعْ أَحَدُهُمَا يَدَهُ مِنْ يَدِ صَاحِبِهِ حَتَّى يُغْفَرَ لَهُمَا»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ بْنِ عَازِبٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام يَقُولُ: «إِذَا لَقِيَ الْمُسْلِمُ أَخَاهُ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَصَافَحَهُ لَمْ يَنْزِعْ أَحَدُهُمَا يَدَهُ مِنْ يَدِ صَاحِبِهِ حَتَّى يُغْفَرَ لَهُمَا»
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ بْنِ عَازِبٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام يَقُولُ: «إِذَا لَقِيَ الْمُسْلِمُ أَخَاهُ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ وَصَافَحَهُ لَمْ يَنْزِعْ أَحَدُهُمَا يَدَهُ مِنْ يَدِ صَاحِبِهِ حَتَّى يُغْفَرَ لَهُمَا»

records.text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah reported to me from Mūsā ibn ‘Uqbah, from ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Utbah, that ‘Abd Allāh ibn Mas‘ūd used to say: 'Among the things that purify your love for your brother is to greet him when you meet him, to call him by the name he loves most, and to make space for him in your gathering.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ عُقْبَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُتْبَةَ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ مَسْعُودِ، كَانَ يَقُولُ: «مِمَّا يُصَفِّي لَكَ وُدَّ أَخِيكَ أَنْ تُسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ إِذَا لَقِيتَهُ، وَتَدَعُوَهُ بِأَحَبِّ الْأَسْمَاءِ ⦗ص: 316⦘ إِلَيْهِ، وَتَوَسِّعَ لَهُ الْمَجْلِسَ إِلَيْكَ»

narrator_path.name_en: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah
narrator_path.source_form: عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُتْبَةَ

records.boundary_review_note: The matn is Abdullah ibn Masud’s counsel on strengthening brotherly affection.

records.text_en: Hisham ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: “It has reached us that eight people who had accompanied one another and formed brotherhood for God’s sake will be brought forth—among them a poor person and a rich person. The rich person will be found to have extra good deeds from his use of wealth, and so will be raised above his companion. The poor person will ask: ‘My Lord, why have You raised him above me when we accompanied one another for Your sake and worked for You?’ God will reply: ‘Do you not see the extra good in his deeds?’ The poor person will say: ‘My Lord, You know that if You had given me wealth as You gave him, I would have done the same for You.’ God will say: ‘He has spoken the truth; join him with his companion.’ A sick person and a healthy one will then be brought; the healthy one will be raised for his extra deeds. The sick one will say: ‘Why have You raised him above me?’ God will reply: ‘I found extra good in his deeds.’ The sick one will say: ‘My Lord, You know that had You restored me to health, I would have done what he did.’ God will say: ‘He has spoken the truth; join him with his companion.’ Then a free person and an enslaved person will be brought, and the same will happen. Then a person of good character and one of bad character will be brought. The one of good character will be raised above the other. The latter will ask: ‘My Lord, why have You raised him above me when we accompanied one another for Your sake and did the same deeds?’ God will reply: ‘Because of his good character.’ The other will have no answer.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، قَالَ: بَلَغَنَا " أَنَّهُ يُؤْتَى بِثَمَانِيَةِ نَفَرٍ اصْطُحَبُوا فِي اللَّهِ وَتَآخَوْا فِيهِ، فَقِيرٌ وَغَنِيٌّ، فَيُوجَدُ لِلْغَنِيِّ فَضْلُ عَمِلٍ فِي مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِي مَالِهِ، فَرُفِعَ عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ، فَيَقُولُ الْفَقِيرُ: يَا رَبِّ لِمَ رَفَعْتَهُ عَلَيَّ، وَإِنَّمَا اصْطَحَبْنَا فِيكَ وَعَمِلْنَا لَكَ؟، فَيَقُولُ: أَلَا تَجِدُ لَهُ فِي عَمَلِهِ فَضْلًا؟، فَيَقُولُ: يَا رَبِّ، لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ لَوْ أَعْطَيْتَنِي مَالًا مِثْلَ مَا أَعْطَيْتَهُ لَعَمِلْتُ لَكَ فِيهِ مِثْلَ مَا عَمِلَ لَكَ، فَيَقُولُ: " صَدَقَ، أَلْحِقُوهُ بِصَاحِبِهِ، وَيُؤْتَى بِمَرِيضٍ وَصَحِيحٍ، فَيُرْفَعُ الصَّحِيحُ بِفَضْلِ عَمَلِهِ، فَيَقُولُ الْمَرِيضُ: لِمَ رَفَعْتَهُ عَلَيَّ؟ . فَيَقُولُ: وَجَدْتُ لَهُ فَضْلًا فِي عَمَلِهِ، فَيَقُولُ: يَا رَبِّ، لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ لَوْ أَصَحَحْتَنِي لَعَمِلْتُ لَكَ كَمَا عَمِلَ، فَيَقُولُ: صَدَقَ، أَلْحِقُوهُ بِصَاحِبِهِ. فَيُؤْتَى بِحُرٍّ وَمَمْلُوكٍ، فَيَكُونُ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ، وَيُؤْتَى بِحَسَنِ الْخُلُقِ وَسَيِّئِ الْخُلُقِ، فَيُرْفَعُ الْحَسَنُ الْخُلُقِ عَلَى السَّيِّئِ الْخُلُقِ، فَيَقُولُ: يَا رَبِّ لِمَ رَفَعْتَهُ عَلَيَّ وَإِنَّمَا اصْطَحَبْنَا فِيكَ، وَعَمِلْنَا لَكَ عَمَلًا وَاحِدًا؟، فَيَقُولُ: لِحُسْنِ خُلُقِهِ، فَلَا يَجِدُ لَهُ جَوَابًا "

records.raw_text_en: Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, saying: It reached us that eight men who had companionship and brotherhood in God—one poor and one rich—will be brought forth. The rich one will be found to have an excess of deeds from what he used to do with his wealth, so he will be raised above his companion. The poor one will say: 'O Lord, why have You raised him above me when we were companions in You and worked for You?' God will say: 'Do you not find that he has an excess in his deeds?' The poor one will say: 'O Lord, You know that if You had given me wealth like his, I would have done for You as he did.' God will say: 'He has spoken the truth. Join him with his companion.' Then a sick person and a healthy one will be brought forth, and the healthy one will be raised due to the excess of his deeds. The sick one will say: 'Why have You raised him above me?' God will say: 'I found an excess in his deeds.' The sick one will say: 'O Lord, You know that if You had made me healthy, I would have done for You as he did.' God will say: 'He has spoken the truth. Join him with his companion.' Then a free man and a slave will be brought forth, and the same will happen. Then a man of good character and one of bad character will be brought forth, and the one of good character will be raised above the one of bad character. The latter will say: 'O Lord, why have You raised him above me when we were companions in You and did the same deeds?' God will say: 'Because of his good character.' He will have no answer.

records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ يُؤْتَى بِثَمَانِيَةِ نَفَرٍ اصْطُحَبُوا فِي اللَّهِ وَتَآخَوْا فِيهِ، فَقِيرٌ وَغَنِيٌّ، فَيُوجَدُ لِلْغَنِيِّ فَضْلُ عَمِلٍ فِي مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِي مَالِهِ، فَرُفِعَ عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ، فَيَقُولُ الْفَقِيرُ: يَا رَبِّ لِمَ رَفَعْتَهُ عَلَيَّ، وَإِنَّمَا اصْطَحَبْنَا فِيكَ وَعَمِلْنَا لَكَ؟، فَيَقُولُ: أَلَا تَجِدُ لَهُ فِي عَمَلِهِ فَضْلًا؟، فَيَقُولُ: يَا رَبِّ، لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ لَوْ أَعْطَيْتَنِي مَالًا مِثْلَ مَا أَعْطَيْتَهُ لَعَمِلْتُ لَكَ فِيهِ مِثْلَ مَا عَمِلَ لَكَ، فَيَقُولُ: " صَدَقَ، أَلْحِقُوهُ بِصَاحِبِهِ، وَيُؤْتَى بِمَرِيضٍ وَصَحِيحٍ، فَيُرْفَعُ الصَّحِيحُ بِفَضْلِ عَمَلِهِ، فَيَقُولُ الْمَرِيضُ: لِمَ رَفَعْتَهُ عَلَيَّ؟ . فَيَقُولُ: وَجَدْتُ لَهُ فَضْلًا فِي عَمَلِهِ، فَيَقُولُ: يَا رَبِّ، لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ لَوْ أَصَحَحْتَنِي لَعَمِلْتُ لَكَ كَمَا عَمِلَ، فَيَقُولُ: صَدَقَ، أَلْحِقُوهُ بِصَاحِبِهِ. فَيُؤْتَى بِحُرٍّ وَمَمْلُوكٍ، فَيَكُونُ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ، وَيُؤْتَى بِحَسَنِ الْخُلُقِ وَسَيِّئِ الْخُلُقِ، فَيُرْفَعُ الْحَسَنُ الْخُلُقِ عَلَى السَّيِّئِ الْخُلُقِ، فَيَقُولُ: يَا رَبِّ لِمَ رَفَعْتَهُ عَلَيَّ وَإِنَّمَا اصْطَحَبْنَا فِيكَ، وَعَمِلْنَا لَكَ عَمَلًا وَاحِدًا؟، فَيَقُولُ: لِحُسْنِ خُلُقِهِ، فَلَا يَجِدُ لَهُ جَوَابًا "
records.isnad_en: Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, saying: It reached us that
records.matn_en: Hisham ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: “It has reached us that eight people who had accompanied one another and formed brotherhood for God’s sake will be brought forth—among them a poor person and a rich person. The rich person will be found to have extra good deeds from his use of wealth, and so will be raised above his companion. The poor person will ask: ‘My Lord, why have You raised him above me when we accompanied one another for Your sake and worked for You?’ God will reply: ‘Do you not see the extra good in his deeds?’ The poor person will say: ‘My Lord, You know that if You had given me wealth as You gave him, I would have done the same for You.’ God will say: ‘He has spoken the truth; join him with his companion.’ A sick person and a healthy one will then be brought; the healthy one will be raised for his extra deeds. The sick one will say: ‘Why have You raised him above me?’ God will reply: ‘I found extra good in his deeds.’ The sick one will say: ‘My Lord, You know that had You restored me to health, I would have done what he did.’ God will say: ‘He has spoken the truth; join him with his companion.’ Then a free person and an enslaved person will be brought, and the same will happen. Then a person of good character and one of bad character will be brought. The one of good character will be raised above the other. The latter will ask: ‘My Lord, why have You raised him above me when we accompanied one another for Your sake and did the same deeds?’ God will reply: ‘Because of his good character.’ The other will have no answer.”
records.boundary_review_note: The source is unspecified in the pluralبلغنا (“it reached us”); the extended account about paired people begins the matn.

records.text_en: Dāwūd ibn Qays reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Spread the greeting of peace among yourselves so that you may love one another. None of you will truly believe until his neighbor is safe from his harm.'

records.text_en: They said 'O Messenger of God, what is Islam?' He said: 'That Muslims are safe from your tongue and your hand.' They said: 'What is faith?' He said: 'That the people of Islam are secure in their blood and their wealth from you.'

records.text_en: Sufyān al-Thawrī reported to me from al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Furāfiṣah, from Abī al-‘Alā’, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said 'To feed a brother for the sake of God with a single morsel is more beloved to me than giving a dirham in charity. To give a brother for the sake of God a dirham is more beloved to me than giving ten dirhams in charity. To give a brother for the sake of God ten dirhams is more beloved to me than freeing a slave.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from ‘Abd Allāh ibn Hubayrah, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn al-Ḥajjāj, that he heard Ka‘b narrating to ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘Āṣ: 'On the Day of Resurrection, it will be called out: Where are those who loved one another for My Majesty? They will be brought forth. Then it will be said Call for Me those who praised Me. They will be brought forth. Then it will be said: Call for Me My neighbors. narrator_path.source_form: عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ

records.boundary_review_note: The report says Kaab narrated to Abdullah ibn Amr; the matn begins with the call on the Day of Resurrection.

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from Ibn Hubayrah, that ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘Āṣ said 'In the scripture that God revealed to Moses, God detests three types of people: one who causes division between those who love one another, one who walks with slander, and one who seeks to harm the innocent.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ هُبَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، قَالَ: " إِنَّهُ لَفِي النَّامُوسِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مُوسَى أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُبْغِضُ مِنَ الْخَلْقِ ثَلَاثَةً: الَّذِي يُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ الْمُتَحَابِّينِ، وَالَّذِي يَمْشِي بِالنَّمِيمَةِ، وَالَّذِي يَلْمِسُ لِلْبُرَآءِ الْعَنَتَ "

records.text_en: ‘Abd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥajrī al-Miṣrī reported to me that ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb used to say: 'Three things purify your love for your brother: greeting him first with peace, calling him by the name he loves most, and making space for him in your gathering. records.boundary_review_note: The matn is attributed to Umar ibn al-Khattab and includes further advice beyond the three items.

records.text_en: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl, from Anas ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'A people with softer hearts than yours will come to you.' Then the Ash‘arīs arrived, among them Abū Mūsā, and they were the first to introduce handshaking in Islam. When they neared Medina, they chanted: 'Tomorrow we meet the beloved, Muḥammad and his party.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ حُمَيْدٍ الطَّوِيلِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «يَقْدِمُ عَلَيْكُمْ قَوْمٌ أَرْفَقُ مِنْكُمْ قُلُوبًا» ، فَقَدِمَ عَلَيْنَا الْأَشْعَرِيُّونَ وَفِيهِمْ أَبُو مُوسَى، وَكَانُوا أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَظْهَرَ الْمُصَافَحَةَ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ، فَجَعَلُوا حِينَ دَنَوْا مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ يَرْجُزُونَ وَيَقُولُونَ: [البحر الرجز] غَدًا نَلْقَى الْأَحِبَّةْ … مُحَمَّدًا وَحِزْبَهْ "

records.text_en: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from ‘Ubayd God ibn Zaḥr, from al-Layth ibn Sulaym, from Sa‘īd ibn Jubayr or another, that he entered the Ka‘bah with ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Abbās. records.text_en: Al-Layth ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Khālid ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī Hilāl, that a man came to the Prophet, ﷺ, and said 'O Messenger of God, there is no one after you whom I love more than so-and-so, yet I feel something in my heart about him that only God knows.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Go and tell him.' The man went to him and told him, and the other said: 'By Him in Whose hand is my soul, I feel the same about you.' He returned to the Prophet, ﷺ, and told him. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'One thing matches another. I do not hear any lingering resentment from you.'

records.text_en: Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said 'A Muslim is the brother of another Muslim; he does not wrong him, nor forsake him, nor betray him. Piety is here—pointing to his chest. It is enough evil for a man to despise his Muslim brother.'

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Samʿan reported to us from Zayd ibn Aslam and others that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Love the person you love with moderation, for one day he may be someone you dislike; and dislike the person you dislike with moderation, for one day he may be someone you love.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ سَمْعَانَ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، وَغَيْرِهِ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ: «أَحْبِبْ حَبِيبَكَ هَوْنًا مَا، عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ بَغِيضَكَ يَوْمًا مَا، وَأَبْغَضْ بَغِيضَكَ هَوْنًا مَا، عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ حَبِيبَكَ يَوْمًا مَا»

records.text_en: Ibn Sam‘ān said: I heard some of our scholars narrating from ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he said to Aslam, his freedman: 'O Aslam, let not your love be infatuation, nor your hatred be destruction.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ سَمْعَانَ: وَسَمِعْتُ رِجَالًا، مِنْ عُلَمَائِنَا يُحَدِّثُونَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ لَأَسْلَمَ مَوْلَاهُ: «يَا أَسْلَمُ، لَا يَكُونَنَّ حُبُّكَ كَلَفًا، وَلَا يَكُونَنَّ بُغْضَكَ تَلَفًا»

records.text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me from ‘Aṭā’ al-Khurāsānī that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to Abū Razīn: 'O Abū Razīn, when a Muslim visits his brother for the sake of God, seventy thousand angels accompany him, praying for him and saying: O God, he has visited him for Your sake, so grant him Your favor. If you can, let your body work for this, then do so.' It is also said: 'Walk a mile to visit a sick person, two miles to reconcile between two people, and three miles to visit for the sake of God.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يُونُسُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ الْخُرَاسَانِيِّ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ لِأَبِي رَزِينٍ: " يَا أَبَا رَزِينٍ، إِنَّ الْمُسْلِمَ إِذَا زَارَ أَخَاهُ فِي اللَّهِ شَيَّعَهُ سَبْعُونَ أَلْفَ مَلَكٍ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَيْهِ يَقُولُونَ: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّهُ وَصَلَهُ فِيكَ فَصِلْهُ. فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ يَعْمَلَ جَسَدُكَ فِي ذَلِكَ فَافْعَلْ " قَالَ: وَيُقَالُ: امْشِ مِيلًا عُدْ ⦗ص: 334⦘ مَرِيضًا، امْشِ مِيلَيْنِ أَصْلِحْ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ، امْشِ ثَلَاثَةً زُرْ فِي اللَّهِ "

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from Ibn Abī Ḥabīb that Abū Sālim al-Jayshānī came to Abū Umayyah in his home and said: 'I heard Abū Dharr say that he heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: When one of you loves his companion, let him go to him in his home and inform him that he loves him for the sake of God.' He said 'I have come to you in your home.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي حَبِيبٍ، أَنَّ أَبَا سَالِمٍ الْجَيْشَانِيَّ، أَتَى إِلَى أَبِي أُمَيَّةَ فِي مَنْزِلِهِ، فَقَالَ: إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ أَبَا ذَرٍّ، يَقُولُ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام يَقُولُ: «إِذَا أَحَبَّ أَحَدُكُمْ صَاحِبَهُ فَلْيَأْتِهِ فِي مَنْزِلِهِ فَيُخْبِرُهُ أَنَّهُ يُحِبُّهُ لِلَّهِ» ، وَقَدْ جِئْتُكَ فِي مَنْزِلِكَ "

records.boundary_review_note: The nested transmission is preserved: Abu Salim reports to Abu Umayyah what he heard from Abu Dharr, who heard the Messenger.

records.text_en: I heard Mālik ibn Anas narrate from ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Ma‘mar, from Abī al-Ḥubāb, from Abī Hurayrah, that he said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'God will say on the Day of Resurrection: Where are those who loved one another for My Majesty? Today I will shade them in My shade on a day when there is no shade but Mine.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ مَالِكَ بْنَ أَنَسٍ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ مَعْمَرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الْحُبَابِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: " إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: أَيْنَ الْمُتَحَابُّونَ لِجَلَالِي؟ الْيَوْمَ أُظِلُّهُمْ فِي ظِلِّي يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلِّي "

records.matn_ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: أَيْنَ الْمُتَحَابُّونَ لِجَلَالِي؟ الْيَوْمَ أُظِلُّهُمْ فِي ظِلِّي يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلِّي "
records.isnad_en: I heard Mālik ibn Anas narrate from ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Ma‘mar, from Abī al-Ḥubāb, from Abī Hurayrah, that he said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: '
records.matn_en: God will say on the Day of Resurrection: Where are those who loved one another for My Majesty? Today I will shade them in My shade on a day when there is no shade but Mine.'

records.boundary_review_note: The matn begins with the report of what Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection, transmitted through Abu Hurayrah.

records.text_en: Mālik ibn Anas reported to me from Abū Ḥāzim, from Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī, who said: I entered the mosque of Damascus and saw a circle of people, with a young man among them who had bright, white incisors and was very quiet. The people were debating, and whenever they disagreed about something, they asked him and then accepted his judgment. I asked, “Who is this?” They said, “Muʿādh ibn Jabal.” The next day I came early to get close to him, but found that he had arrived before me and was praying. I waited until he had finished, then approached him from the front, greeted him, and said, “By God, I love you for God’s sake.” He asked, “By God?” I said, “By God.” He asked me this three times, then took hold of the gathered fold of my cloak, pulled me toward him, and said, “Rejoice, for I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: ‘God says: My love is due for those who love one another for My sake, sit together for My sake, give generously to one another for My sake, and visit one another for My sake.’”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مَالِكُ بْنُ أَنَسٍ، عَنْ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي إِدْرِيسَ الْخَوْلَانِيِّ، قَالَ: دَخَلْتُ مَسْجِدَ دِمَشْقَ فَإِذَا حَلْقَةٌ فِيهَا نَاسٌ بَيْنَ ظَهْرَانَيْهِمْ فَتًى شَابٌّ بَرَّاقُ الثَّنَايَا كَثِيرُ الصَّمْتِ، وَالْقَوْمُ يَتَنَازَعُونَ، فَإِذَا اخْتَلَفُوا فِي شَيْءٍ سَأَلُوا عَنْهُ، ثُمَّ صَدَرُوا عَنْ قَوْلِهِ، قَالَ: فَسَأَلْتُ: مَنْ هَذَا؟ فَقَالُوا: مُعَاذُ بْنُ جَبَلٍ، قَالَ: فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْغَدُ هَجَرْتُ لِأَدْنُوَ مِنْهُ قَالَ: فَوَجَدْتُهُ قَدْ سَبَقَنِي بِالتَّهْجِيرِ وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي، قَالَ: فَانْتَظَرْتُهُ حَتَّى إِذَا قَضَى صَلَاتَهُ جِئْتُهُ مِنْ جِهَةِ وَجْهِهِ فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَقُلْتُ لَهُ: وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأُحِبُّكَ لِلَّهِ قَالَ: آللَّهِ؟، قُلْتُ: وَاللَّهِ، قَالَ: رَدَّهَا ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ، فَأَخَذَ بِحُبْوَةِ رِدَائِي فَجَبَذَنِي إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَ: أَبْشِرْ، فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام يَقُولُ: " قَالَ اللَّهُ: وَجَبَتْ مَحَبَّتِي لِلْمُتَحَابِّينَ فِيَّ، وَالْمُتَجَالِسِينَ فِيَّ، وَالْمُتَبَاذِلِينَ فِيَّ، وَالْمُتَزَاوِرِينَ فِيَّ "

records.raw_text_en: Mālik ibn Anas reported to me from Abī Ḥāzim, from Abī Idrīs al-Khawlānī, who said I entered the mosque of Damascus and saw a circle of people with a young man among them, bright of teeth and mostly silent, while the people were discussing. Whenever they disagreed on something, they would ask him, and then follow his opinion. I asked: Who is this? They said: Mu‘ādh ibn Jabal. The next day, I arrived early to get closer to him, but found that he had already arrived before me and was praying. I waited for him until he finished his prayer, then approached him from the front, greeted him with peace, and said: By God, I love you for the sake of God. He said: By God? I said: By God. He repeated this three times, then took hold of the waistband of my garment, pulled me toward him, and said: Rejoice, for I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: God has decreed: My love is obligatory for those who love one another for My sake, those who sit together for My sake, those who give to one another for My sake, and those who visit one another for My sake.'

records.text_en: ‘Amr ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us from Bukayr ibn ‘Abd Allāh, from a man, from ‘Aṭā’ ibn Yasār: 'Two men were brothers during the time of the Messenger of God, ﷺ. One of them died, and the other returned from a journey he had been on. He came to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and said What happened to so-and-so? The Prophet said: He has died. I wish I had died with him, so I sought guidance. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: Did you fast Ramadan after him? He said: Yes. The Prophet said: It is as if he meant: You have its reward for that.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، عَنْ بُكَيْرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ: " أَنَّ رَجُلَيْنِ كَانَا مُتَوَاخِيَيْنِ عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام فَمَاتَ أَحَدُهُمَا، وَقَدِمَ الْآخَرُ مِنْ غِيبَةٍ كَانَ فِيهَا، فَجَاءَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ: «مَا فَعَلَ فُلَانٌ؟» قَالَ: هُوَ مَاتَ، وَلَوَدِدْتُ لَوْ أَنِّي مُتُّ مَعَهُ فَاسْتَخَرْتُ. فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لَمْ تَصُمْ رَمَضَانَ بَعْدَهُ؟» قَالَ: بَلَى، قَالَ: " فَكَأَنَّهُ يَقُولُ: إِنَّ لَكَ بِذَلِكَ فَضْلَهَا "

One of them died, and the other returned from a journey he had been on. He came to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and said What happened to so-and-so? The Prophet said: He has died. I wish I had died with him, so I sought guidance. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: Did you fast Ramadan after him? He said: Yes. The Prophet said: It is as if he meant: You have its reward for that.'

records.text_en: ‘Abd al-‘Azīz ibn Muḥammad reported to me from the nephew of Ibn Shihāb, from Hishām ibn ‘Urwah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'When one of you loves his companion, let him inform him, for God will only increase him in goodness by that.'
records.text_ar: وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَخِي ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ «إِذَا كَانَ أَحَدُكُمْ يَوَدُّ صَاحِبَهُ فَلْيُخْبِرْهُ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَزِيدُهُ بِذَلِكَ إِلَّا خَيْرًا»

records.boundary_review_note: The source identifies the transmitter only as Ibn Shihab’s nephew; no name is inferred.

records.text_en: Sulaymān ibn Bilāl reported to me from Kathīr ibn Zayd, from Walīd ibn Rabāḥ, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “A believer is a mirror to another believer, and a believer is a brother to another believer: wherever he encounters him, he looks after his affairs and protects him in his absence.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ بِلَالٍ، عَنْ كَثِيرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ وَلِيدِ بْنِ رَبَاحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «الْمُؤْمِنُ مِرْآةُ الْمُؤْمِنِ، وَالْمُؤْمِنُ أَخُو الْمُؤْمِنِ، مِنْ حَيْثُ لَقِيَهُ يَكُفُّ ضَيْعَتَهُ، وَيَحُوطُهُ مِنْ وَرَائِهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ بِلَالٍ، عَنْ كَثِيرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ وَلِيدِ بْنِ رَبَاحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «الْمُؤْمِنُ مِرْآةُ الْمُؤْمِنِ، وَالْمُؤْمِنُ أَخُو الْمُؤْمِنِ، مِنْ حَيْثُ لَقِيَهُ يَكُفُّ ضَيْعَتَهُ، وَيَحُوطُهُ مِنْ وَرَائِهِ»

records.raw_text_en: Sulaymān ibn Bilāl reported to me from Kathīr ibn Zayd, from Walīd ibn Rabāḥ, from Abī Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'The believer is the mirror of the believer, and the believer is the brother of the believer. Wherever he meets him, he safeguards his trust and protects him from behind.'

records.boundary_review_note: The matn begins with the Prophetic parable about the believer as a mirror and brother.

records.text_en: Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd reported to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Whenever a servant prays for his believing brother in his absence, his prayer is answered. An angel at his right and at his left says, ‘And the same for you,’ as long as he continues praying.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: " مَا مِنْ عَبْدٍ يَدْعُو لِأَخِيهِ الْمُؤْمِنِ عَنْ ظَهْرِ غَيَّبٍ إِلَّا اسْتُجِيبَ لَهُ، فَقَالَ لَهُ مَلَكٌ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَعَنْ شِمَالِهِ: وَلَكَ مَثْلَاهُ، حَتَّى يَسْكُتَ مِنْ دَاعِيهِ "

records.raw_text_en: Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd reported to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'There is no servant who supplicates for his believing brother in his absence except that it is answered for him. An angel says to him from his right and left: And for you is the same, until he stops supplicating.'
records.display_text_en: Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd reported to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Whenever a servant prays for his believing brother in his absence, his prayer is answered. An angel at his right and at his left says, ‘And the same for you,’ as long as he continues praying.”
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: "

records.boundary_review_note: The matn begins with the Messenger’s statement about supplication for an absent believing brother.

records.text_en: Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd reported to me, saying: I heard Mūsā ibn Wardān say: I heard from Abī Hurayrah, who said that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'In Paradise, there are columns of ruby upon which are rooms of emerald with open doors that shine as the shining star. We said: O Messenger of God, who will live in them? He said: Those who love one another for the sake of God, those who sit together for the sake of God, and those who meet for the sake of God.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ مُوسَى بْنَ وَرْدَانَ، يَقُولُ: سَمِعْتُ مِنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إِنَّ فِي الْجَنَّةِ لَعُمُدًا مِنْ يَاقُوتٍ عَلَيْهَا غُرَفٌ مِنْ زَبَرْجَدٍ لَهَا أَبْوَابٌ مُفَتَّحَةٌ تُضِيءُ كَمَا يُضِيءُ الْكَوْكَبُ الدُّرِّيُّ» قَالَ: قُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَنْ يَسْكُنُهَا؟ قَالَ ⦗ص: 346⦘ : «الْمُتَحَابُّونَ فِي اللَّهِ، وَالْمُتَجَالِسُونَ فِي اللَّهِ، وَالْمُتَلَاقُونَ فِي اللَّهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ مُوسَى بْنَ وَرْدَانَ، يَقُولُ: سَمِعْتُ مِنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إِنَّ فِي الْجَنَّةِ لَعُمُدًا مِنْ يَاقُوتٍ عَلَيْهَا غُرَفٌ مِنْ زَبَرْجَدٍ لَهَا أَبْوَابٌ مُفَتَّحَةٌ تُضِيءُ كَمَا يُضِيءُ الْكَوْكَبُ الدُّرِّيُّ» قَالَ: قُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَنْ يَسْكُنُهَا؟ قَالَ ⦗ص: 346⦘ : «الْمُتَحَابُّونَ فِي اللَّهِ، وَالْمُتَجَالِسُونَ فِي اللَّهِ، وَالْمُتَلَاقُونَ فِي اللَّهِ»

records.raw_text_en: Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥumayd reported to me, saying: I heard Mūsā ibn Wardān say: I heard from Abī Hurayrah, who said that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'In Paradise, there are columns of ruby upon which are rooms of emerald with open doors that shine as the shining star. We said: O Messenger of God, who will live in them? He said: Those who love one another for the sake of God, those who sit together for the sake of God, and those who meet for the sake of God.'

records.text_en: Ibn Abī Ḥumayd narrated to me from Ibn al-Munkadir that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Call your believing brother by the name he loves most, and address your believing brother by the kunyah he loves most.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ⦗ص: 347⦘ عليه السلام قَالَ: «سَمِّ أَخَاكَ الْمُؤْمِنَ بِأَحَبِّ أَسْمَائِهِ إِلَيْهِ، وَكَنِّ أَخَاكَ الْمُؤْمِنَ بِأَحَبِّ كُنَاهُ إِلَيْهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ⦗ص: 347⦘ عليه السلام قَالَ: «سَمِّ أَخَاكَ الْمُؤْمِنَ بِأَحَبِّ أَسْمَائِهِ إِلَيْهِ، وَكَنِّ أَخَاكَ الْمُؤْمِنَ بِأَحَبِّ كُنَاهُ إِلَيْهِ»

records.text_en: Ibn Abī Ḥumayd narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Qays that ‘Īsā ibn Maryam said 'A person’s faith is not complete until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ، أَنَّ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ، قَالَ: «لَا يَكْمُلُ إِيمَانُ الْمَرْءِ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ، أَنَّ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ، قَالَ: «لَا يَكْمُلُ إِيمَانُ الْمَرْءِ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ»

records.text_en: Ibn Abī Ḥumayd reported to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Whoever attends to his brother’s need, God will attend to his need.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «مَنْ يَكُونُ فِي حَاجَةِ أَخِيهِ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ فِي حَاجَتِهِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «مَنْ يَكُونُ فِي حَاجَةِ أَخِيهِ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ فِي حَاجَتِهِ»
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ أَبِي حُمَيْدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ: «مَنْ يَكُونُ فِي حَاجَةِ أَخِيهِ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ فِي حَاجَتِهِ»
records.raw_text_en: Ibn Abī Ḥumayd reported to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Whoever is in the need of his brother, God is in his need.'
records.display_text_en: Ibn Abī Ḥumayd reported to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Whoever attends to his brother’s need, God will attend to his need.”

records.boundary_review_note: The matn is the Prophetic statement about helping a brother and Allah meeting one’s need.

records.text_en: Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated to me from Ḥafṣ ibn ‘Ubayd God, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said It reached me that a man turns on his bed while sleeping and is forgiven due to the supplication of his brother for him in his absence.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ: بَلَغَنِي «أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ، يَتَقَلَّبُ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ نَائِمًا وَهُوَ مَغْفُورٌ لَهُ بِدُعَاءِ أَخِيهِ لَهُ، عَنْ ظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ: بَلَغَنِي «أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ، يَتَقَلَّبُ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ نَائِمًا وَهُوَ مَغْفُورٌ لَهُ بِدُعَاءِ أَخِيهِ لَهُ، عَنْ ظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ»

records.boundary_review_note: Anas reports that the source reached him without naming an intermediary; the matn begins with the sleeping man forgiven through his brother’s supplication.
