records.boundary_review_note: Bukayr ibn Abdullah is the source of an anecdote about the people of Badr and funeral processions; the quotation is attributed to them collectively. Matn begins قَالَ فِي أَهْلِ بَدْرٍ.

records.text_en: Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub reported to me from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Al-Hasan, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'A companion of truth is better than seclusion, and seclusion is better than a bad companion.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ شَهْرِ بْنِ حَوْشَبٍ، عَنِ ⦗ص: 602⦘ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «صَاحِبُ الصِّدْقِ خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْوَحْدَةِ، وَالْوَحْدَةُ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَاحِبِ السُّوءِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ شَهْرِ بْنِ حَوْشَبٍ، عَنِ ⦗ص: 602⦘ الْحَسَنِ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «صَاحِبُ الصِّدْقِ خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْوَحْدَةِ، وَالْوَحْدَةُ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَاحِبِ السُّوءِ»

records.text_en: Ibn An'am reported to me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'The best of you is the one who believes in God, establishes prayer, gives zakat, and secludes himself from people.' It was said to him: 'What does his seclusion from people mean?' He said: 'He avoids what they have fallen into of evil.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ أَنْعَمَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، قَالَ: «إِنَّ أَفْضَلَكُمْ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ ، وَأَقَامَ الصَّلَاةَ ، وَآتَى الزَّكَاةَ ، وَاعْتَزَلَ النَّاسَ» ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ: مَا اعْتِزَالُهُ النَّاسَ؟ قَالَ: «يَعْتَزِلُ مَا دَخَلُوا فِيهِ مِنَ الشَّرِّ»

records.boundary_review_note: Ibn Anam reports the saying directly from the Messenger without a named intermediary. The reported clarification exchange follows in the matn. Matn begins إِنَّ أَفْضَلَكُمْ.

records.text_en: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Al-Rahman reported to me from 'Amr, the freed slave of Al-Muttalib, from Al-Muttalib, from 'Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'A believer attains through good character the rank of one who fasts and stands in prayer.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَعْقُوبُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو مَوْلَى الْمُطَّلِبِ، عَنِ الْمُطَّلِبِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ عليه السلام ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: «إِنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ لَيُدْرِكُ بِحُسْنِ خُلُقِهِ دَرَجَةَ الصَّائِمِ الْقَانِتِ الْمُخْبِتِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَعْقُوبُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو مَوْلَى الْمُطَّلِبِ، عَنِ الْمُطَّلِبِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ عليه السلام ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: «إِنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ لَيُدْرِكُ بِحُسْنِ خُلُقِهِ دَرَجَةَ الصَّائِمِ الْقَانِتِ الْمُخْبِتِ»

records.text_en: Yaḥqā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from ʿUmar ibn Shaybah, from Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym, who said: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “By his good character, a man can attain the rank of one who fasts, devoutly worships, and humbly submits to God.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ 507 - وَحَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ شَيْبَةَ، عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ سُلَيْمٍ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ، صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيُدْرِكُ بِحُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ دَرَجَةَ الصَّائِمِ الْقَانِتِ الْمُخْبِتِ» ⦗ص: 605⦘
records.source_number_note_en: The export ran report 508 into the end of this one; it is separated here, as the edition prints it. The English given here also covers that report.

records.raw_text_en: Yahya ibn Ayyub reported to me from 'Umar ibn Shaybah, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'A man attains through good character the rank of one who fasts and stands in prayer.' Yahya ibn Ayyub also reported to me from Yahya ibn Sa'id Al-Ansari similarly, but he did not attribute it to the Prophet.

records.matn_en: “By his good character, a man can attain the rank of one who fasts, devoutly worships, and humbly submits to God.”
records.boundary_review_note: This is the first of two reports in a formerly combined English block. The separated following report from Yahya ibn Said al-Ansari is not raised to the Prophet. Matn begins إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ.

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb reported to me: Jarir ibn Hazim reported to me from Shu'bah ibn Al-Hajjaj that Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said 'A believer is molded on every character except treachery and lying.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ: أَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، عَنْ شُعْبَةَ بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ، أَنَّ سَعْدَ بْنَ أَبِي وَقَّاصٍ، قَالَ: «إِنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ يُطْبَعُ عَلَى كُلِّ طَبْعٍ غَيْرَ الْخِيَانَةِ وَالْكَذِبِ»

records.text_en: Jarir ibn Hazim reported to me that he heard Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan say: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Three traits, if found in a person, make him a hypocrite, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a believer: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ الْحَسَنَ بْنَ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ، يَقُولُ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ثَلَاثٌ مَنْ كُنَّ فِيهِ فَهُوَ مُنَافِقٌ ، وَإِنْ صَلَّى وَصَامَ وَزَعَمَ أَنَّهُ مُؤْمِنٌ: إِذَا حَدَّثَ كَذَبَ، وَإِذَا وَعَدَ أَخْلَفَ، وَإِذَا ائْتُمِنَ خَانَ "

records.text_en: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih reported to me from Bahir ibn Sa'd or 'Amir ibn Jushayb, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, who attributed it to the Prophet, ﷺ: 'No man lies intentionally except that God burdens him with the sin of everyone who lies after him.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ صَالِحٍ، عَنْ بَحِيرِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ، أَوْ عَامِرِ بْنِ جَشِيبٍ، عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ مَعْدَانَ، يَرْفَعُهُ، قَالَ: «مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ يَكْذِبُ كِذْبَةً مُتَعَمِّدًا إِلَّا حَمَّلَهُ اللَّهُ إِثْمَ مَنْ كَذَبَ بَعْدَ مَا بَعْدَهُ»

records.text_en: Yahya ibn Salam reported to me from 'Uthman ibn Miqsam, from Nu'aym ibn Al-Mujammir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'The most lying of people are the craftsmen.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ سَلَامٍ، عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ مِقْسَمٍ، عَنْ نُعَيْمِ بْنِ الْمُجَمِّرِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «إِنَّ أَكْذَبَ النَّاسِ الصُّنَّاعُ»

records.text_en: Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub reported to me from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, from Ibn Shihab, who said 'One is not considered a liar if he wards off harm from himself.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ رَبِيعَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ ⦗ص: 610⦘ شِهَابٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لَيْسَ بِكَاذِبٍ مَنْ دَرَأَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ»

records.text_en: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd reported to me from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said 'Whoever says to a child, 'Come, take this,' and then does not give him anything, it is a lie.'

records.text_en: Maslamah ibn ʿAlī reported to me that Yazīd ibn Maysarah said: “Lying opens the door to every evil, just as water nourishes the roots of trees.”
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مَسْلَمَةُ بْنُ عُلَيٍّ، قَالَ: قَالَ يَزِيدُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ: «إِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَسْقِي بَابَ كُلِّ شَرٍّ، كَمَا يَسْقِي الْمَاءُ أُصُولَ الشَّجَرِ»

records.text_en: Maslamah reported to me from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, who attributed it to the Prophet, ﷺ: 'A man may speak the truth until he is recorded as truthful, and a man may lie and be arrogant until he is recorded as a tyrant and faces what tyrants face of God’s punishment and wrath.'

records.text_en: Maslamah reported... Abu Al-Aswad Al-Du'ali said 'If you wish your companion to lie to you, then lie.'

records.text_en: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd reported to me from Ibn Al-'Ajlan, from 'Awn ibn 'Abdullah, from Ibn Shihab, who said 'No form of lying is ever permissible, whether serious or in jest. A servant may speak the truth until his heart is filled with righteousness, leaving no room for an iota of wickedness. A servant may lie until his heart is filled with wickedness, leaving no room for an iota of righteousness. Truth leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. Lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. The sign of this is that it is said: He spoke the truth and was righteous, or he lied and was wicked.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي اللَّيْثُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْعَجْلَانِ، عَنْ عَوْنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: " مَا حَلَّ مِنَ الْكَذِبِ شَيْءٌ قَطُّ لَا جَادًّا وَلَا هَازِلًا، وَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَيَصْدُقُ حَتَّى يَمْتَلِئَ قَلْبُهُ بِرًّا، وَمَا يَبْقَى مِنْهُ مَوْضِعُ إِبْرَةٍ مِنْ فُجُورٍ، وَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَيَكْذِبُ حَتَّى يَمْتَلِئَ قَلْبُهُ فُجُورًا ، فَمَا يَبْقَى فِي قَلْبِهِ مَوْضِعَ إِبْرَةٍ ⦗ص: 615⦘ مَنْ بِرٍّ، الصِّدْقُ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ، وَالْبِرُّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَالْكَذِبُ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ، وَالْفُجُورُ يَهْدِي إِلَى النَّارِ، وَآيَةُ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ يُقَالُ: صَدَقَ وَبَرَّ وَكَذَبَ وَفَجَرَ "

records.matn_ar: مَا حَلَّ مِنَ الْكَذِبِ شَيْءٌ قَطُّ لَا جَادًّا وَلَا هَازِلًا، وَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَيَصْدُقُ حَتَّى يَمْتَلِئَ قَلْبُهُ بِرًّا، وَمَا يَبْقَى مِنْهُ مَوْضِعُ إِبْرَةٍ مِنْ فُجُورٍ، وَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَيَكْذِبُ حَتَّى يَمْتَلِئَ قَلْبُهُ فُجُورًا ، فَمَا يَبْقَى فِي قَلْبِهِ مَوْضِعَ إِبْرَةٍ مَنْ بِرٍّ، الصِّدْقُ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ، وَالْبِرُّ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، وَالْكَذِبُ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ، وَالْفُجُورُ يَهْدِي إِلَى النَّارِ، وَآيَةُ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ يُقَالُ: صَدَقَ وَبَرَّ وَكَذَبَ وَفَجَرَ "
records.isnad_en: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd reported to me from Ibn Al-'Ajlan, from 'Awn ibn 'Abdullah, from Ibn Shihab, who said '
records.matn_en: No form of lying is ever permissible, whether serious or in jest. A servant may speak the truth until his heart is filled with righteousness, leaving no room for an iota of wickedness. A servant may lie until his heart is filled with wickedness, leaving no room for an iota of righteousness. Truth leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. Lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. The sign of this is that it is said: He spoke the truth and was righteous, or he lied and was wicked.'
records.boundary_review_note: This is a statement attributed to Ibn Shihab; the text begins with his maxim and includes its explanatory sequence. Matn begins مَا حَلَّ مِنَ الْكَذِبِ.

records.text_en: Ibn Sam'an reported to us: Ibn Shihab, Abu Al-Huwayrith, and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm reported to him that it reached them from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, that he was asked: 'O Messenger of God, can a believer be miserly?' He said 'Yes.' It was said: 'O Messenger of God, can a believer have bad character?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'O Messenger of God, can a believer be cowardly?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'O Messenger of God, can a believer be a liar?' He said: 'No.'

records.text_en: Malik ibn Anas reported to me from Safwan ibn Sulaym that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, was asked: 'O Messenger of God, can a believer be cowardly?' He said 'Yes.' It was said: 'Can a believer be miserly?' He said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'Can a believer be a liar?' He said: 'No.'

records.text_en: Hisham ibn Sa'd reported to me from 'Abd Al-Wahhab ibn Bukht, from Sulayman ibn Habib, that they visited Abu Umamah Al-Bahili to check on him. They found him with some of his companions, and he was advising them. Most of what he said to them was: 'Hold fast to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. Three types of people are under God’s protection: the pilgrim, the warrior, and the one who enters his home with peace.' Ibn Wahb said: I thought the third was Hajj.

records.text_en: I heard Sufyan Al-Thawri narrate from Abu Ishaq Al-Hamdani, from Abu Al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said 'It is enough lying for a person to narrate everything he hears.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ سُفْيَانَ الثَّوْرِيَّ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ الْهَمْدَانِيِّ ⦗ص: 620⦘ ، عَنْ أَبِي الْأَحْوَصِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «بِحَسْبِ الْمَرْءِ كَذِبًا أَنْ يُحَدِّثَ بِكُلِّ مَا سَمِعَ»

records.text_en: I heard Malik narrate that it reached him that Ibn Mas'ud said 'A servant continues to lie, and a black spot is marked in his heart until his heart becomes completely black, and he is recorded among the liars with God.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ مَالِكًا، يُحَدِّثُ قَالَ: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ: «لَا يَزَالُ الْعَبْدُ يَكْذِبُ وَتُنْكَتُ فِي قَلْبِهِ نُكْتَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ حَتَّى يَسْوَدَّ قَلْبُهُ فَيُكْتَبَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ»

records.text_en: Ibn 'Ajlan reported to me from a man among the freed slaves of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah Al-'Adawi, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, who said My mother called me one day while the Messenger of God, ﷺ, was sitting in our house. She said: 'Come, I will give you something.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to her: 'What did you intend to give him?' She said: 'I intended to give him some dates.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to her: 'If you had not given him anything, a lie would have been recorded against you.'

records.text_en: Malik ibn Anas reported to us from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he said 'Hold fast to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. Do you not see that it is said: He spoke the truth and was righteous, or he lied and was wicked?'

records.text_en: Anas ibn Mālik reported to me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: “Whoever gives up lying, though he could lie, will have a house built for him on the outskirts of Paradise; whoever gives up disputation, though he is in the right, will have a house built for him in the middle of Paradise; and whoever has good character will have a house built for him in its highest part.”

records.text_en: Al-Qasim ibn 'Abdullah reported to me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays.' This is in the Book of God: 'When the hypocrites come to you, they say: We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of God. God knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and God testifies that the hypocrites are indeed liars.' (Al-Munafiqun: 1) And He said: 'Among them are those who made a covenant with God: If He gives us from His bounty, we will surely give charity and be among the righteous. But when He gave them from His bounty, they became stingy with it and turned away, averse. So He penalized them with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they failed God in what they promised Him and because they were lying.' (At-Tawbah: 75-77)

records.text_en: Usamah ibn Zayd reported to us from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd Al-Rahman, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'A reformer is not a liar.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، قَالَ: «لَيْسَ الْمُصْلِحُ بِالْكَذَّابِ»

records.boundary_review_note: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman is the final named authority before the Prophetic attribution. Matn begins لَيْسَ الْمُصْلِحُ.

records.text_en: Dawud ibn 'Abd Al-Rahman reported to me from Ibn Khuthaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid Al-Ansariyyah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, address the people and say: 'O people, what makes you follow lies as moths follow a flame? Every lie is recorded against the son of Adam except three: a man lying to his wife to please her, a man lying between two people to reconcile them, and a man lying in the deception of war.'

records.isnad_en: Dawud ibn 'Abd Al-Rahman reported to me from Ibn Khuthaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid Al-Ansariyyah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, address the people and say: '
records.matn_en: O people, what makes you follow lies as moths follow a flame? Every lie is recorded against the son of Adam except three: a man lying to his wife to please her, a man lying between two people to reconcile them, and a man lying in the deception of war.'
records.boundary_review_note: Asma bint Yazid explicitly says she heard the Messenger address the people. Matn begins with the public address يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ.

records.text_en: Muhammad ibn Muslim reported to me from Ayyub Al-Sakhtiyani, from Ibn Sirin, from 'Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ, who said 'Nothing was more detested by the companions of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, than lying... from anyone, even if it was little, until it led him to repent.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ السَّخْتِيَانِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ سِيرِينَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ عليه السلام ، قَالَتْ: «مَا كَانَ شَيْءٌ أَبْغَضَ عِنْدَ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ، صلى الله عليه وسلم ، مِنَ الْكَذِبِ (. . . . . . . . .) مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنْ شَيْءٍ، وَإِنْ قَلَّ فَيُخْرِجُ لَهُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ حَتَّى تُحْدِثَ لَهُ تَوْبَةً»

records.text_en: Malik reported to me from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, that a man said to the Messenger of God, ﷺ: 'O Messenger of God, should I lie to my wife?' He said: 'There is no good in lying.' The man said: 'O Messenger of God, should I promise her and tell her?' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'There is no sin on you.' I also heard Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrate similarly from them.
records.text_ar: قَالَ 534 - وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ سُلَيْمٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا، قَالَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَكْذِبُ امْرَأَتِي؟ قَالَ: «لَا خَيْرَ فِي الْكَذِبِ» ، فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَعِدُهَا وَأَقُولُ لَهَا؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ، صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكَ» ⦗ص: 632⦘

records.text_en: Sulayman ibn Bilal reported to me from Kathir ibn Zayd, from the freed slave woman of Muhriz ibn Zuhayr, a man from Aslam and a companion of the Prophet, ﷺ, that she used to hear Muhriz say: 'O God, I seek refuge in You from the era of liars.' She said I asked him: 'What is the era of liars?' He said: 'An era in which lying becomes widespread, and the one who does not intend to lie speaks with their words, so he becomes involved in their lies.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ بِلَالٍ، عَنْ كَثِيرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ أُمِّ وَلَدِ مُحْرِزِ بْنِ زُهَيْرٍ، رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَسْلَمَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ عليه السلام، أَنَّهَا كَانَتْ تَسْمَعُ مُحْرِزًا يَقُولُ: «اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ زَمَانِ الْكَاذِبِينَ» ، قَالَتْ: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ: وَمَا زَمَانُ الْكَاذِبِينَ؟ قَالَ: «زَمَانٌ يَظْهَرُ فِيهِ الْكَذِبُ فَيَذْهَبُ الَّذِي لَا يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَكْذِبَ، فَيَتَحَدَّثُ بِحَدِيثِهِمْ، فَإِذَا هُوَ قَدْ دَخَلَ مَعَهُمْ فِي كَذِبِهِمْ»

records.matn_ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ زَمَانِ الْكَاذِبِينَ» ، قَالَتْ: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ: وَمَا زَمَانُ الْكَاذِبِينَ؟ قَالَ: «زَمَانٌ يَظْهَرُ فِيهِ الْكَذِبُ فَيَذْهَبُ الَّذِي لَا يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَكْذِبَ، فَيَتَحَدَّثُ بِحَدِيثِهِمْ، فَإِذَا هُوَ قَدْ دَخَلَ مَعَهُمْ فِي كَذِبِهِمْ»
records.isnad_en: Sulayman ibn Bilal reported to me from Kathir ibn Zayd, from the freed slave woman of Muhriz ibn Zuhayr, a man from Aslam and a companion of the Prophet, ﷺ, that she used to hear Muhriz say: '
records.matn_en: O God, I seek refuge in You from the era of liars.' She said I asked him: 'What is the era of liars?' He said: 'An era in which lying becomes widespread, and the one who does not intend to lie speaks with their words, so he becomes involved in their lies.'

narrator_path.name_en: The unnamed freed slave woman of Muhriz ibn Zuhayr
narrator_path.source_form: عَنْ أُمِّ وَلَدِ مُحْرِزِ بْنِ زُهَيْرٍ

narrator_path.name_en: Muhriz ibn Zuhayr (a man from Aslam and companion of the Prophet)

records.boundary_review_note: The unnamed woman reports hearing Muhriz ibn Zuhayr say the supplication and then recounts their exchange. Matn begins with the supplication اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ.

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from Abī al-Aswad, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn Rāfi‘, from Abī Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Faith and disbelief do not gather in the heart of a person, nor do truth and falsehood combine, nor do treachery and trustworthiness come together.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from Abī Qabīl, who said: I heard a man say that he heard ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ās say: 'In Hell, there is a prison, and in Paradise, there is a fortress of pearl. As for the fortress of Paradise, none who has any falsehood in him shall enter it. As for the prison of Hell, none shall enter it except the worst of the wicked. Its floor is fire, its roof is fire, its walls are fire, and fire scorches within it.'

records.boundary_review_note: Abu Qabil says he heard an unnamed man, who said he heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As. The saying is attributed to Abdullah; no Prophetic attribution is made. Matn begins إِنَّ فِي النَّارِ.

records.text_en: Jarīr ibn Hāzim reported to me from Bahz ibn Hakīm, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: 'Woe to the one who tells lies to people to make them laugh. Woe to him, woe to him, woe to him.'

records.text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that a man said to the Messenger of God, ﷺ: 'I tell stories to make people laugh, some of which are false.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'There is no good in falsehood.' The man said: 'O Messenger of God, you jest and laugh.' He replied: 'I only speak the truth.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا، قَالَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: " إِنِّي أُحَدِّثُ الْحَدِيثَ أُضْحِكُ بِهِ الْقَوْمَ بَعْضُهُ بَاطِلٌ، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «لَا خَيْرَ فِي الْبَاطِلِ» . فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّكَ مُمَازِحٌ وَضَاحِكٌ، فَقَالَ: «إِنِّي لَا أَقُولُ إِلَّا حَقًّا»

The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'There is no good in falsehood.' The man said: 'O Messenger of God, you jest and laugh.' He replied: 'I only speak the truth.'
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا، قَالَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: "
records.matn_ar: إِنِّي أُحَدِّثُ الْحَدِيثَ أُضْحِكُ بِهِ الْقَوْمَ بَعْضُهُ بَاطِلٌ، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «لَا خَيْرَ فِي الْبَاطِلِ» . فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّكَ مُمَازِحٌ وَضَاحِكٌ، فَقَالَ: «إِنِّي لَا أَقُولُ إِلَّا حَقًّا»

records.matn_en: I tell stories to make people laugh, some of which are false.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'There is no good in falsehood.' The man said: 'O Messenger of God, you jest and laugh.' He replied: 'I only speak the truth.'
records.boundary_review_note: The unnamed man who asks about joking is part of the matn narrative, not an upstream transmitter. Matn begins إِنِّي أُحَدِّثُ الْحَدِيثَ.

records.text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'God will not look at the old fornicator, the poor who is arrogant, or the lying leader.'

records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، قَالَ: «لَا يَنْظُرُ اللَّهُ إِلَى الشَّيْخِ الزَّانِي، وَلَا إِلَى الْعَائِلِ الْمَزْهُوِّ، وَلَا إِلَى الْإِمَامِ الْكَذَّابِ»

records.display_text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: ‘God will not look [with approval] at an old man who commits fornication, a poor man who is arrogant, or a lying ruler.’
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، قَالَ: «
records.matn_ar: لَا يَنْظُرُ اللَّهُ إِلَى الشَّيْخِ الزَّانِي، وَلَا إِلَى الْعَائِلِ الْمَزْهُوِّ، وَلَا إِلَى الْإِمَامِ الْكَذَّابِ»

records.matn_en: God will not look at the old fornicator, the poor who is arrogant, or the lying leader.'
records.boundary_review_note: Zayd ibn Aslam is the final named authority before the Prophetic attribution. Matn begins لَا يَنْظُرُ اللَّهُ.

records.text_en: Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said 'I never saw anyone more content with truth when it was brought to him than ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ أَنَّهُ، قَالَ: «مَا رَأَيْتُ أَحَدًا قَطُّ أَرْضَى بِالصِّدْقِ إِذَا أُوتِيَ مِنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ أَنَّهُ، قَالَ: «مَا رَأَيْتُ أَحَدًا قَطُّ أَرْضَى بِالصِّدْقِ إِذَا أُوتِيَ مِنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ»
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ أَنَّهُ، قَالَ: «مَا رَأَيْتُ أَحَدًا قَطُّ أَرْضَى بِالصِّدْقِ إِذَا أُوتِيَ مِنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ»
records.raw_text_en: Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said 'I never saw anyone more content with truth when it was brought to him than ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb.'
records.display_text_en: Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said 'I never saw anyone more content with truth when it was brought to him than ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb.'
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ أَنَّهُ، قَالَ: «
records.matn_ar: مَا رَأَيْتُ أَحَدًا قَطُّ أَرْضَى بِالصِّدْقِ إِذَا أُوتِيَ مِنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ»
records.isnad_en: Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said '
records.matn_en: I never saw anyone more content with truth when it was brought to him than ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb.'
records.boundary_review_note: Aslam attributes this observation to his experience of Umar ibn al-Khattab. Matn begins مَا رَأَيْتُ أَحَدًا.

records.text_en: ‘Amr ibn al-Hārith reported to me that Sahl ibn ‘Aqīl told him that the Prophet Ismā‘īl had promised a man to meet him at a certain place. The man came but forgot, so Ismā‘īl waited for him and spent the night there until the man came the next day. He asked: 'Have you not left this place?' Ismā‘īl replied: 'No.' The man said 'I would not have left until you came. That is why he was called the one true to his promise.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، أَنَّ سَهْلَ بْنَ عَقِيلٍ حَدَّثَهُ، " أَنَّ إِسْمَاعِيلَ النَّبِيَّ وَعَدَ رَجُلًا مَكَانًا أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُ فَجَاءَ وَنَسِيَ الرَّجُلُ، فَظَلَّ بِهِ إِسْمَاعِيلُ وَبَاتَ حَتَّى جَاءَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الْغَدِ، فَقَالَ: مَا بَرِحْتَ مِنْ هَاهُنَا؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: «لَمْ أَكُنْ لِأَبْرَحَ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَ فَبِذَلِكَ كَانَ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، أَنَّ سَهْلَ بْنَ عَقِيلٍ حَدَّثَهُ، " أَنَّ إِسْمَاعِيلَ النَّبِيَّ وَعَدَ رَجُلًا مَكَانًا أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُ فَجَاءَ وَنَسِيَ الرَّجُلُ، فَظَلَّ بِهِ إِسْمَاعِيلُ وَبَاتَ حَتَّى جَاءَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الْغَدِ، فَقَالَ: مَا بَرِحْتَ مِنْ هَاهُنَا؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: «لَمْ أَكُنْ لِأَبْرَحَ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَ فَبِذَلِكَ كَانَ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ»
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، أَنَّ سَهْلَ بْنَ عَقِيلٍ حَدَّثَهُ، " أَنَّ إِسْمَاعِيلَ النَّبِيَّ وَعَدَ رَجُلًا مَكَانًا أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُ فَجَاءَ وَنَسِيَ الرَّجُلُ، فَظَلَّ بِهِ إِسْمَاعِيلُ وَبَاتَ حَتَّى جَاءَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الْغَدِ، فَقَالَ: مَا بَرِحْتَ مِنْ هَاهُنَا؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: «لَمْ أَكُنْ لِأَبْرَحَ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَ فَبِذَلِكَ كَانَ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ»
records.raw_text_en: ‘Amr ibn al-Hārith reported to me that Sahl ibn ‘Aqīl told him that the Prophet Ismā‘īl had promised a man to meet him at a certain place. The man came but forgot, so Ismā‘īl waited for him and spent the night there until the man came the next day. He asked: 'Have you not left this place?' Ismā‘īl replied: 'No.' The man said 'I would not have left until you came. That is why he was called the one true to his promise.'
records.display_text_en: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith reported to me that Sahl ibn ʿAqīl told him: The Prophet Ismāʿīl had promised a man to meet him at a certain place. The man came but forgot, so Ismāʿīl stayed there, spending the night, until the man returned the next day. He asked, ‘Have you been here all this time?’ The man replied, ‘Yes.’ Ismāʿīl said, ‘I would not leave until you came.’ That is why he was true to his promise.
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، أَنَّ سَهْلَ بْنَ عَقِيلٍ حَدَّثَهُ، "
records.matn_ar: أَنَّ إِسْمَاعِيلَ النَّبِيَّ وَعَدَ رَجُلًا مَكَانًا أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُ فَجَاءَ وَنَسِيَ الرَّجُلُ، فَظَلَّ بِهِ إِسْمَاعِيلُ وَبَاتَ حَتَّى جَاءَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الْغَدِ، فَقَالَ: مَا بَرِحْتَ مِنْ هَاهُنَا؟ قَالَ: لَا، قَالَ: «لَمْ أَكُنْ لِأَبْرَحَ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَ فَبِذَلِكَ كَانَ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ»
records.isnad_en: ‘Amr ibn al-Hārith reported to me that Sahl ibn ‘Aqīl told him
records.matn_en: that the Prophet Ismā‘īl had promised a man to meet him at a certain place. The man came but forgot, so Ismā‘īl waited for him and spent the night there until the man came the next day. He asked: 'Have you not left this place?' Ismā‘īl replied: 'No.' The man said 'I would not have left until you came. That is why he was called the one true to his promise.'
records.boundary_review_note: This is a narrative transmitted by Sahl ibn Aqil about the Prophet Ismail keeping a promise; it is not presented as a Prophetic hadith. Matn begins أَنَّ إِسْمَاعِيلَ النَّبِيَّ.

records.text_en: Jarīr ibn Hāzim reported to me from Mujālid ibn Sa‘īd, from Qays ibn Abī Hāzim, who said: I heard Abū Bakr al-Siddīq addressing the people, saying: 'O people, beware of lying, for lying is incompatible with faith.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، عَنْ مُجَالِدِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقَ، وَهُوَ يَخْطُبُ النَّاسَ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: «أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ، فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ مُجَانِبُ الْإِيمَانِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، عَنْ مُجَالِدِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقَ، وَهُوَ يَخْطُبُ النَّاسَ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: «أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ، فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ مُجَانِبُ الْإِيمَانِ»
records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، عَنْ مُجَالِدِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقَ، وَهُوَ يَخْطُبُ النَّاسَ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ: «أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ، فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ مُجَانِبُ الْإِيمَانِ»
records.raw_text_en: Jarīr ibn Hāzim reported to me from Mujālid ibn Sa‘īd, from Qays ibn Abī Hāzim, who said: I heard Abū Bakr al-Siddīq addressing the people, saying: 'O people, beware of lying, for lying is incompatible with faith.'
records.display_text_en: Jarīr ibn Hāzim reported to me from Mujālid ibn Sa‘īd, from Qays ibn Abī Hāzim, who said: I heard Abū Bakr al-Siddīq addressing the people, saying: 'O people, beware of lying, for lying is incompatible with faith.'

records.matn_ar: أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ، فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ مُجَانِبُ الْإِيمَانِ»
records.isnad_en: Jarīr ibn Hāzim reported to me from Mujālid ibn Sa‘īd, from Qays ibn Abī Hāzim, who said: I heard Abū Bakr al-Siddīq addressing the people, saying: '
records.matn_en: O people, beware of lying, for lying is incompatible with faith.'
records.boundary_review_note: Qays ibn Abi Hazim explicitly says he heard Abu Bakr address the people. Matn begins أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ.

records.text_en: Ibrāhīm ibn Nashīt reported to me from Qays ibn Rāfi‘, from ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn Jubayr, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ās, who said 'A servant does not attain complete faith until he eats only from lawful earnings, completes his ablution in difficult circumstances, and abandons lying even in jest.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ نَشِيطٍ، عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ رَافِعٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، قَالَ: «لَا يُؤْمِنُ الْعَبْدُ كُلَّ الْإِيمَانِ حَتَّى لَا يَأْكُلَ إِلَّا كَسْبًا، وَيُتِمَّ الْوُضُوءَ فِي الْمَكَارِهِ، وَيَضَعَ الْكَذِبَ وَلَوْ فِي الْمُزَاحَةِ»

records.boundary_review_note: The saying is attributed to Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As and is not explicitly raised to the Prophet. Matn begins لَا يُؤْمِنُ الْعَبْدُ.

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from al-Hārith ibn Yazīd, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ās, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'There are four traits that, if you possess them, you need not care about what you miss in this world: safeguarding a trust, truthful speech, good character, and purity in sustenance.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from Ibn Hubayrah, from Abī ‘Abd al-Rahmān, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘Ās, who said 'There are three traits that, if found in someone other than you, you should not hesitate to testify that he is a hypocrite: if he lies when he speaks, breaks his promise, and betrays when trusted. But if he speaks the truth, fulfills his trust, and keeps his promise, do not hesitate to testify that he is a believer.'

records.boundary_review_note: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As is the source of the admonition. The paired positive traits later in the same quotation remain part of the matn. Matn begins ثَلَاثٌ إِذَا كُنَّ.

records.text_en: Yahyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from Ibn ‘Ajlān that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, would recognize a lie from some of his companions and would remain distant and displeased with him until he knew that he had repented from it.

records.text_en: Shabīb ibn Sa‘īd reported to me from Shu‘bah ibn al-Hajjāj, from Mansūr and Sulaymān, from Abī Wā’il, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn Mas‘ūd, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'A servant continues to speak the truth and strive for truth until he is recorded as truthful. And a servant continues to lie and strive in lying until he is recorded as a liar.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي شَبِيبُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ شُعْبَةَ بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ، عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ، وَسُلَيْمَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي وَائِلٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، قَالَ: «لَا يَزَالُ الْعَبْدُ يَصْدُقُ وَيَتَحَرَّى الصِّدْقَ حَتَّى يُكتَبَ صَدِيقًا، وَلَا يَزَالُ الْعَبْدُ يَكْذِبُ وَيَتَحَرَّى الْكَذِبَ حَتَّى يُكْتَبَ كَاذِبًا»

records.text_en: Shabīb reported to me from Shu‘bah, from someone who told him, from Samurah ibn Jundub, that the Prophet, ﷺ, said 'Whoever narrates a hadith from me thinking it is a lie is one of the two liars.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي شَبِيبٌ، عَنْ شُعْبَةَ، عَنْ مَنْ، حَدَّثَهُ، عَنْ سَمُرَةَ بْنِ جُنْدُبٍ، أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ، عليه السلام ، قَالَ: «مَنْ رَوَى عَنِّي حَدِيثًا يَرَى أَنَّهُ كَذِبٌ فَهُوَ أَحَدُ الْكَاذِبَيْنِ»

records.boundary_review_note: An unnamed transmitter told Shubah, followed by Samurah ibn Jundub. The unnamed link remains unresolved. Matn begins مَنْ رَوَى عَنِّي حَدِيثًا.

records.text_en: Shabīb reported to me from Rawh ibn al-Qāsim, from ‘Āsim ibn Bahdalah, from al-Musayyib ibn Rāfi‘, from Ibn Mas‘ūd, who said 'Satan meets a man in the form of a human and tells him lies, so the man narrates them. It is said: Who told you this? He replies: A man I do not know.'
records.text_ar: وَأَخْبَرَنِي شَبِيبٌ، عَنْ رَوْحِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ ابْنِ بَهْدَلَةَ، عَنِ الْمُسَيِّبِ بْنِ رَافِعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ " إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَلْقَى الرَّجُلَ فِي صُورَةِ الْإِنْسَانِ فَيُخْبِرُهُ بِالْكَذِبِ فَيُحَدِّثُ بِهِ، فَيُقَالُ: مَنْ حَدَّثَكَ؟ فَيَقُولُ: رَجُلٌ لَا أَعْرِفُهُ "

records.text_en: Yahyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from al-Muthannā ibn al-Sabbāh, from ‘Amr ibn Shu‘ayb, that Mu‘ādh ibn Jabal said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, was traveling when a man said: 'O Messenger of God, so-and-so does not eat until he is fed, and does not travel until he is prepared for.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'You have backbitten your brother.' They said: 'We only said what is true about him.' He replied: 'It is enough that you speak about your brother what is true about him.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ الْمُثَنَّى بْنِ الصَّبَّاحِ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ، أَنَّ مُعَاذَ بْنَ جَبَلٍ، قَالَ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام مُسَافِرًا، فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَا يَأْكُلُ فُلَانٌ حَتَّى يُطْعَمَ، وَلَا يَرْحَلُ حَتَّى يُرَحَّلَ لَهُ ⦗ص: 649⦘ مَا أَعْجَزَهُ فَقَالَ: «اغْتَبْتُمْ أَخَاكُمْ» ، قَالُوا: قُلْنَا مَا فِيهِ؟ قَالَ: «حَسْبُكُمْ أَنْ تُحَدِّثُوا عَنْ أَخِيكُمْ مَا فِيهِ»

records.text_en: Yahyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from Yahyā ibn Sa‘īd, from ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahmān, that ‘Ā’ishah bint Talhah ibn ‘Ubayd God entered upon ‘Ā’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ, while a Bedouin woman was with her. The Bedouin woman left, dragging her garment. ‘Ā’ishah bint Talhah said 'How long her garment is!' ‘Ā’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'You have backbitten her. Catch up with her and ask her to seek forgiveness for you.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ عَمْرَةَ بِنْتِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَنَّ عَائِشَةَ ابْنَةَ طَلْحَةَ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ، دَخَلَتْ عَلَى عَائِشَةَ زَوْجِ ⦗ص: 650⦘ النَّبِيِّ عليه السلام ، وَعِنْدَهَا أَعْرَابِيَّةٌ، فَخَرَجَتِ الْأَعْرَابِيَّةُ عَلَى ذَيْلِهَا، فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ بِنْتُ طَلْحَةَ: مَا أَطْوَلَ ذَيْلَهَا ، فَقَالَتْ لَهَا عَائِشَةُ، زَوْجُ النَّبِيِّ ، عليه السلام: «اغْتَبْتِيهَا، أَدْرِكِيهَا تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكِ»

records.text_en: Yahyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from Ismā‘īl ibn ‘Uqbah al-Madanī that he heard Ibn Shihāb say: Ibn Mas‘ūd climbed a tree to pick fruit for the Messenger of God, ﷺ. Some of the Prophet’s companions said 'How thin your legs are, O Ibn Umm ‘Abd!' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'By the One in Whose hand is my soul, they are heavier in the scale than Mount Uhud. And you have backbitten him.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ الْمَدَنِيِّ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ ابْنَ شِهَابٍ، يَقُولُ: إِنَّ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ طَلَعَ شَجَرَةً يَجْنِيهَا لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، فَقَالَ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ عليه السلام: مَا أَدَقَّ سَاقَيْكَ يَا ابْنَ أُمِّ عَبْدٍ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لَهُمَا فِي الْمِيزَانِ أَثْقَلُ مِنْ أُحُدٍ ، وَقَدِ اغْتَبْتَهُ»

records.text_en: Hishām ibn Sa‘d and ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, during his final illness, was visited by his wives. Safiyyah bint Huyayy said 'By God, O Prophet of God, I wish that what afflicts you were afflicting me.' The other wives of the Prophet, ﷺ, exchanged glances at her. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, noticed and said: 'Rinse your mouths.' They asked: 'From what, O Messenger of God?' He replied: 'From exchanging glances at your companion. By God, she is truthful.'

records.text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah and Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that two men passed by the Messenger of God, ﷺ, while he was sitting in the Hijr, and another man was standing and praying. They exchanged glances at him. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, heard their words while they were circumambulating. When they returned to him, he handed them a stick and said 'Use it to clean your teeth.' They said: 'O Prophet of God, we did not eat anything.' He replied: 'Yes, you did.'

records.display_text_en: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd reported to me from Khālid ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī Hilāl, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, to whom it was conveyed that: “While the Prophet was traveling, a Bedouin came to him and began asking him questions, and the Prophet turned toward him. records.text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah reported to me from al-‘Alā’ ibn ‘Abd al-Rahmān, from his father, from Abī Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Do you know what the bankrupt is?' They said: 'O Messenger of God, the bankrupt among us is one who has no dirham or property.' He said: 'The bankrupt from my nation is one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayers, fasting, and charity, but he has insulted this one, slandered that one, struck another, and consumed the wealth of yet another. Then he will be made to sit, and this one will be given from his good deeds, and that one from his good deeds. If his good deeds are exhausted before he has repaid what he owes of sins, some of their sins will be taken and cast upon him, then he will be cast into the Fire.'

records.display_text_en: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim reported to me from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmārah, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd God, from ʿĀʾishah bint Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd God, from ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet, who said: “A short woman came in to see us. When she left, I gestured with my hand [to indicate her height] and said, ‘How short she is!’ The Messenger of God said, ‘You have backbitten her. Get up and ask her to release you from that.’ She said: Another woman came to see us, trailing her garment. When she left, I said, ‘Messenger of God, how long her train is!’ He said, ‘You have backbitten her. Get up and ask her to release you from that.’”

Translation reviewed against Arabic. The Arabic is translated directly; the source English was not aligned to this report.

records.text_en: On Sitting with Storytellers
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، وَهِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام فِي وَجَعِهِ الَّذِي تُوُفِّيَ مِنْهُ اجْتَمَعَ إِلَيْهِ نِسَاؤُهُ، فَقَالَتْ صَفِيَّةُ بِنْتُ حُيَيٍّ: أَمَا وَاللَّهِ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ لَوَدِدْتُ أَنَّ الَّذِي بِكَ بِي، فَتَغَامَزْنَهَا أَزْوَاجُ النَّبِيِّ عليه السلام ، فَأَبْصَرَهُنَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام فَقَالَ: «مَضْمِضْنَ» ، قُلْنَ: مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ؟ قَالَ: «مِنْ تَغَامُزِكُنَّ بِصَاحِبَتِكُنَّ، وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّهَا صَادِقَةٌ»

records.raw_text_en: On Sitting with Storytellers
records.display_text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah and Hishām ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that, during the illness from which the Messenger of God died, his wives gathered around him. Safiyyah bint Huyayy said, ‘By God, O Prophet of God, I wish that what afflicts you were afflicting me.’ The other wives exchanged glances at her. The Messenger of God noticed them and said, ‘Rinse your mouths.’ They asked, ‘From what, O Messenger of God?’ He replied, ‘From your exchanging glances at your companion. By God, she is truthful.’
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي حَفْصُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ، وَهِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام فِي وَجَعِهِ الَّذِي تُوُفِّيَ مِنْهُ

records.isnad_en: Hishām ibn Sa‘d and ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that the Messenger of God, ﷺ,
records.matn_en: during his final illness, was visited by his wives. Safiyyah bint Huyayy said 'By God, O Prophet of God, I wish that what afflicts you were afflicting me.' The other wives of the Prophet, ﷺ, exchanged glances at her. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, noticed and said: 'Rinse your mouths.' They asked: 'From what, O Messenger of God?' He replied: 'From exchanging glances at your companion. By God, she is truthful.'

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb said Yahyā ibn ‘Abd Allāh ibn Sālim reported to me from ‘Abd al-Rahmān that Ibn al-Musayyib 'did not sit with the storyteller, nor did he prostrate with him when he prostrated.'

records.display_text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah and Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that two men passed by the Messenger of God, ﷺ, while he was sitting in the Hijr, and another man was standing and praying. They said: 'O Prophet of God, we did not eat anything.' He replied: 'Yes, you did.'

records.text_en: I heard Mālik say: 'Ibn al-Musayyib and others did not sit with the storyteller nor turn to him.'

records.raw_text_en: I heard Mālik say: 'Ibn al-Musayyib and others did not sit with the storyteller nor turn to him.'
records.display_text_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah reported to me from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: ‘Do you know who the bankrupt is?’ They replied, ‘The bankrupt among us is one who has no dirham.’ He said, ‘The bankrupt of my community is one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting, and alms, but has insulted one person, slandered another, struck another, and consumed another’s wealth. He will then sit, and this one will be given some of his good deeds, and that one some of his good deeds. If his good deeds run out before he has settled the wrongs he owes, some of their sins will be taken and cast upon him; then he will be cast into the Fire.’

records.isnad_en: Hafs ibn Maysarah reported to me from al-‘Alā’ ibn ‘Abd al-Rahmān, from his father, from Abī Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said '
records.matn_en: Do you know what the bankrupt is?' They said: 'O Messenger of God, the bankrupt among us is one who has no dirham or property.' He said: 'The bankrupt from my nation is one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayers, fasting, and charity, but he has insulted this one, slandered that one, struck another, and consumed the wealth of yet another. Then he will be made to sit, and this one will be given from his good deeds, and that one from his good deeds. If his good deeds are exhausted before he has repaid what he owes of sins, some of their sins will be taken and cast upon him, then he will be cast into the Fire.'

narrator_path.name_en: His father, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yaqub

records.boundary_review_note: Abu Hurayrah transmits the question and explanation of the bankrupt person from the Messenger. Matn begins أَتَدْرُونَ.

records.text_en: Mu‘āwiyah ibn Sālih reported to me from Azhar ibn Sa‘īd who said: I heard Dhū al-Kalā‘ say: Ka‘b used to tell stories during the governorship of Mu‘āwiyah. ‘Awf ibn Mālik said to me: 'O Abū Shuraḥbīl, do you see your cousin telling stories by the order of the governor?' I said: 'I do not know.' He said: 'I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: "Storytellers are of three types: a ruler, one who is commanded, or a deceiver."'
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ: أَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَنَّ ابْنَ الْمُسَيِّبِ، «لَمْ يَكُنْ يَجْلِسُ مَعَ الْقَاصِّ ، وَلَا يَسْجُدُ مَعَهُ إِذَا سَجَدَ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ: أَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَنَّ ابْنَ الْمُسَيِّبِ، «لَمْ يَكُنْ يَجْلِسُ مَعَ الْقَاصِّ ، وَلَا يَسْجُدُ مَعَهُ إِذَا سَجَدَ»

records.display_text_en: I heard Mālik relate that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Qāsim was especially devoted to his father. One night his father noticed that he was absent; then he came to him, and his father asked, “Where were you?” He replied, “I was with a storyteller.” His father said, “That is good, God willing, my son, but do not do it another time.”

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from Bakr ibn Sawādah that ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib went out one day and saw a man narrating to the people, saying: 'Know me, so know me.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنَا مُعَاوِيَةُ، عَنْ سُلَيْمِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ الْكَلَاعِيِّ، عَنْ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ نُفَيْرٍ، أَنَّ أُمَّ الدَّرْدَاءِ، بَعَثَتْهُ إِلَى نَوْفٍ الْبِكَالِيِّ، وَإِلَى رَجُلٍ آخَرَ يَقُصَّانِ، فَقَالَتْ: " قُلْ لَهُمَا: «لِتَكُنْ مَوْعِظَتُكُمَا النَّاسَ لِأَنْفُسِكُمَا»

records.text_en: Mālik ibn Anas reported to me that Sa‘īd ibn al-Musayyib, al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, and Khārijah ibn Zayd ibn Thābit used to sit in circles talking, while the storyteller of the group narrated, and they did not sit with him.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي بَشِيرُ بْنُ أَبِي عَمْرٍو الْخَوْلَانِيُّ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، قَالَ فِي قَوْمٍ اجْتَمَعُوا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ ، وَرَجُلٌ يَذْكُرُ وَحْدَهُ، «فَلَهُ مِنَ الْفَضْلِ عَلَيْهِمْ كَفَضْلِ الْقَمَرِ عَلَى النُّجُومِ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي بَشِيرُ بْنُ أَبِي عَمْرٍو الْخَوْلَانِيُّ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، قَالَ فِي قَوْمٍ اجْتَمَعُوا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ ، وَرَجُلٌ يَذْكُرُ وَحْدَهُ، «فَلَهُ مِنَ الْفَضْلِ عَلَيْهِمْ كَفَضْلِ الْقَمَرِ عَلَى النُّجُومِ»

records.display_text_en: Bashīr ibn Abī ʿAmr al-Khawlānī reported to me from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said of a group gathered to remember God and one man remembering Him alone: ‘His merit over them is like the moon’s merit over the stars.’
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي بَشِيرُ بْنُ أَبِي عَمْرٍو الْخَوْلَانِيُّ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، قَالَ فِي قَوْمٍ اجْتَمَعُوا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ ، وَرَجُلٌ يَذْكُرُ وَحْدَهُ، «
records.matn_ar: فَلَهُ مِنَ الْفَضْلِ عَلَيْهِمْ كَفَضْلِ الْقَمَرِ عَلَى النُّجُومِ»
records.isnad_en: Bashīr ibn Abī ‘Amr al-Khawlānī reported to me from ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib who said:
records.matn_en: about a group gathered to remember God, while one man remembered Him alone: 'He has a virtue over them like the virtue of the moon over the stars.'

records.text_en: Mālik said 'Abd Allāh ibn ‘Umar used to say to some of those who narrated: 'You have driven me out of my house.' Mālik said: 'Abd Allāh ibn ‘Umar lived sixty years after the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and Ibn Mas‘ūd and other companions of the Prophet, ﷺ, did not narrate stories, as far as I know.'

records.display_text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from Abī Qabīl that ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, ﷺ, said: Whoever does not know the abrogated verses of the Qur’ān should not narrate to the people.

records.matn_ar: مَنْ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ مَنْسُوخَ الْقُرْآنِ فَلَا يَقُصَّ عَلَى النَّاسِ»
records.isnad_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from Abī Qabīl that ‘Alī ibn Abī Tālib, ﷺ, said:
records.matn_en: Whoever does not know the abrogated verses of the Qur’ān should not narrate to the people.

records.text_en: Mālik ibn Anas reported to me that Tamīm al-Dārī said to ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: 'Let me call, recite, narrate, and remind the people.' ‘Umar said: 'No.' He repeated his request, and ‘Umar said: 'You want to say: I am Tamīm al-Dārī, so know me.' Then ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Affān later struck him for narrating in the mosque, finding him narrating after the Maghrib prayer.

records.text_en: Abū al-Muthannā Sulaymān ibn Yazīd al-Ka‘bī reported to me from Ibrāhīm ibn ‘Abd Allāh ibn Abī Farwah who said 'I saw the guards of ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Azīz following the storytellers in the mosque.' He said: 'There was a man who narrated after the Maghrib prayer.'

records.text_en: I heard Sufyān ibn ‘Uyaynah narrate from ‘Amr ibn Dīnār that Tamīm al-Dārī asked permission from ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to narrate, and he said 'If you wish, I will permit you, but it is slaughter,' and he gestured with his hand to his throat.
records.text_ar: قَالَ مَالِكٌ: كَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمَرَ يَقُولُ لِبَعْضِ مَنْ كَانَ يَقُصُّ: «أَخْرَجَنِي مِنْ بَيْتِي» قَالَ مَالِكٌ: إِنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ أَقَامَ بَعْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام سِتِّينَ سَنَةً، وَقَدْ كَانَ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ وَغَيْرُهُ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ ، عليه السلام ، وَمَا أَعْلَمُ أَحَدًا مِنْهُمْ قَصَّ

records.text_en: I heard Sufyān narrate from Ibn ‘Ajlān, from Bukayr ibn ‘Abd Allāh, who said ‘Awf ibn Mālik al-Ashja‘ī entered the mosque of Ḥimṣ with Dhū al-Kalā‘ from Ḥimyar. ‘Awf said to him: 'This is your cousin narrating.' Dhū al-Kalā‘ said: 'What prevents them when he is the scholar of this nation?' ‘Awf said: 'I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: "No one narrates in our mosque except a ruler, one who is commanded, or a boaster."'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِكُ بْنُ أَنَسٍ، أَنَّ تَمِيمًا الدَّارِيَّ، قَالَ لِعُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ: دَعْنِي أَدْعُوا وَأَقْرَأُ وَأَقُصُّ وَأُذَكِّرُ النَّاسَ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: لَا. فَأَعَادَ عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: أَنْتَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَقُولَ: أَنَا تَمِيمٌ الدَّارِيُّ فَاعْرِفُونِي، قَالَ: ثُمَّ ضَرَبَهُ عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عَفَّانَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى الْقَصَصِ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ، وَجَدَهُ يَقُصُّ بَعْدَ الْمَغْرِبِ

records.text_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from ‘Ayyāsh ibn ‘Abbās al-Qitbānī that Salmān al-Fārisī sat one day with some people from Quraysh and the Anṣār. When he wanted to leave, they asked him to supplicate for them, so he did. The next day, he sat with them again, and they asked him to supplicate for them, but he refused. They said 'May God rectify you, you supplicated for us yesterday, so why not today?' He said: 'I wish I had remained neutral in yesterday’s gathering, neither for me nor against me. records.display_text_en: Ibn Lahiʿah reported to me from ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās al-Qitbānī that Salmān al-Fārisī once sat with some people from Quraysh and the Anṣār. When he was about to leave, they asked him to pray for them, and he did. The next day he sat with them again, and they asked him to pray for them, but he refused. They said, ‘May God set you right; you prayed for us yesterday, so why not today?’ He replied, ‘I wish yesterday’s gathering had been neutral for me, bringing me neither gain nor blame. Satan came to me and said: “The men of Quraysh and the Anṣār will come to you asking you to pray for them.”’

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ سَلْمَانَ الْفَارِسِيَّ، قَعَدَ يَوْمًا مَعَ نَاسٍ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ، وَالْأَنْصَارِ، فَلَمَّا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَقُومَ سَأَلُوهُ أَنْ يَدْعُوَا لَهُمْ، فَدَعَا لَهُمْ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ مِنَ الْغَدِ قَعَدَ إِلَيْهِمْ فَسَأَلُوهُ أَنْ يَدْعُوَا لَهُمْ، فَأَبَى، فَقَالُوا لَهُ: أَصْلَحَكَ اللَّهُ قَدْ دَعَوْتَ لَنَا أَمْسِ، فَمَا بَالُكَ الْيَوْمَ، قَالَ: " لَوَدِدْتُ أَنِّي بِمَجْلِسِ أَمْسِ كَفَافًا لَا عَلَيَّ وَلَا لِيَ، أَتَانِي الشَّيْطَانُ، فَقَالَ رِجَالُ قُرَيْشٍ، وَالْأَنْصَارِ: يَأْتُوكَ فِي دُعَائِكَ "
records.isnad_en: Ibn Lahī‘ah reported to me from ‘Ayyāsh ibn ‘Abbās al-Qitbānī
records.matn_en: that Salmān al-Fārisī sat one day with some people from Quraysh and the Anṣār. When he wanted to leave, they asked him to supplicate for them, so he did. The next day, he sat with them again, and they asked him to supplicate for them, but he refused. They said 'May God rectify you, you supplicated for us yesterday, so why not today?' He said: 'I wish I had remained neutral in yesterday’s gathering, neither for me nor against me. Satan came to me and said: Men of Quraysh and the Anṣār come to you for your supplication.'
records.boundary_review_note: Ibn Lahiah reports through Ayyash ibn Abbas al-Qitbani an anecdote about Salman and requests for supplication. Matn begins أَنَّ سَلْمَانَ.

records.text_en: Abū Hāni’ al-Khawlānī reported to me from Abī ‘Abd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘Āṣ, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'God decreed the destinies of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ بِلَالٍ، عَنْ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَتْ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «يَا عَائِشَةُ بَيْتٌ لَا تَمْرَ فِيهِ جِيَاعٌ أَهْلُهُ»

records.text_en: Yūnus reported to me from Ibn Shihāb that ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr told him from Zaynab bint Abī Salamah, from Umm Ḥabībah bint Abī Sufyān, that she said to the Messenger of God, ﷺ: 'Do you want my sister, the daughter of Abī Sufyān?' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'What would I do?' She said: 'Marry her.' He said: 'Your sister?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you like that?' She said: 'Yes, and I am not one to keep you to myself. The most deserving of those who share with me in goodness is my sister.' He said: 'She is not lawful for me.' She said: 'By God, I was told that you are proposing to the daughter of Abī Salamah.' He said: 'The daughter of Umm Salamah?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'By God, even if she were not my stepdaughter under my care, she would not be lawful for me. She is the daughter of my brother through nursing. Thuwaybah nursed me and her. Do not offer me your daughters or sisters.'

records.text_en: Muḥammad ibn Khallād al-Iskandarānī reported to me from al-Layth, from Hishām, from his father, from Zaynab, from Umm Ḥabībah, similarly. Ya‘qūb ibn ‘Abd al-Raḥmān reported to me from Hishām ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from Zaynab, from Umm Ḥabībah, except that in the narration of al-Layth and Ya‘qūb, she said: 'I heard that you are marrying Durrah, the daughter of Abī Salamah.'

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Abbās supplicated: 'O God, this is the month of Ramadan, the month of fasting, the month of standing in prayer, the month of repentance, the month of mercy, forgiveness, salvation from the Fire, and attainment of Paradise. O God, grant it safety for me, grant me safety in it, and grant it safety from me. Assist me in it with Your best assistance, guide me in it to Your obedience, occupy me in it with Your worship, supplication, and recitation of Your Book. Increase for me in it blessings, grant me in it good health, keep my body healthy in it, expand my provision in it, suffice me in it from what concerns me, answer my supplication in it, and fulfill my hope in it. O God, remove from me in it drowsiness, laziness, boredom, slackness, hardness of heart, heedlessness, and deception. Keep me away from illnesses, distractions, worries, sorrows, ailments, sins, and transgressions. Turn away from me evil, indecency, ignorance, play, fatigue, and hardship. You are the One who answers supplications. O God, protect me in it from Satan, his whispering, his spitting, his blowing, his insinuations, his discouragement, his plotting, his deception, his cavalry, his tricks, his infantry, his snares, his helpers, his parties, his followers, and his partners. O God, grant me in it diligence, striving, strength, energy, turning to You, repentance, desire, sincerity of intention, awe, piety, fear of You, hope in You, trust in You, restraint from Your prohibitions, beneficial knowledge, elevated deeds, answered supplications, and do not let anything prevent me from these due to an affliction, illness, worry, or sorrow, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. Grant me in it the best of what You grant to Your righteous servants of forgiveness, mercy, tenderness, well-being, and continuous safety in this world and the Hereafter. O God, make my supplication in it reach You, my deeds in it accepted, and my sins in it forgiven, so that my share in it is the greatest and my portion in it is the largest, for the Night of Decree, so that no one from Your friends and those most pleasing to You is given preference over it. A month, grant me in it the best of what You have granted anyone whom You have allowed to reach it and honored with it. Make me among those freed by You from the Fire, those released by You from Hell, and the fortunate of Your creation through Your forgiveness, mercy, pleasure, well-being, and safety, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. O God, Lord of the dawn and the ten nights, Lord of Jibrīl, Mīkā’īl, Isrāfīl, Ibrāhīm, Ismā‘īl, Isḥāq, Ya‘qūb, Lord of Mūsā, we flee to You from our sins, so shelter us; we are repentant, so accept our repentance; we seek forgiveness, so forgive us; we seek refuge, so grant us refuge; we submit, so do not forsake us; we flee, so grant us security; we desire, so intercede for us... Her children said 'Here we are, O Lord, here we are.' They came while the call was among the Anṣār, saying: 'O assembly of the Anṣār, O assembly of the Anṣār.' Then the call was restricted to Banī al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, saying: 'O Banī al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, O Banī al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, looked while he was on his mule, stretching towards their fighting, and said: 'This is when the battle heats up.' Then the Messenger of God, ﷺ, took pebbles and threw them at the faces of the disbelievers, then said: 'They have been defeated by the Lord of Muḥammad.' I went to look, and the battle was as it was, but the Messenger of God, ﷺ, had thrown pebbles at them. I kept seeing their edge dull and their affair retreating. God revealed: {Certainly has God given you victory on many battlefields, and on the day of Ḥunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for you; then you turned back, fleeing. Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers you did not see and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.} [At-Tawbah: 25-26]. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, took six thousand captives from them that day, women and children, and took camels and sheep in numbers they could not count. He divided the captives and the wealth into fifths. Then the delegation of Hawāzin came to him and said: 'O Messenger of God, you are the most just and most righteous of people and the most merciful to people. You have taken our women and children...' He said to them: 'The best speech is the truest. I have with me those you see of the people... all of it. Look which of the two groups you prefer. If you prefer the women and children, or if you prefer the wealth.' They said: 'Our women and children.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, stood among the Muslims and said: 'O assembly of Muslims, these are your brothers from Hawāzin. I have returned their women and children to them. Whoever wishes to make this voluntary, let him do so, and whoever wishes to have it recorded against us, let him do so.' The Muslims said: 'No, we have made it voluntary, O Messenger of God...' from those who did not make it voluntary, return until your leaders inform us of your decision in this matter. The Muslims made it voluntary, the best responder to the supplications of the distressed, the remover of every evil, the God of the worlds. I call upon You by all Your names, those I know and those I do not know, O Lord, glory be to You. To You belong the loftiest attributes and the most beautiful names, Jibrīl, the God of Ibrāhīm, Ismā‘īl, Isḥāq, and Ya‘qūb, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor. I ask You, O Lord, by You, to grant us from poverty, and do not turn our faces to anyone from Your creation, by the One besides Whom there is no deity, and to make us among... Your protection, and bestow upon them by Your grace, and be generous to them with Your pardon, by the One besides Whom there is no deity, glory be to You, O Lord. You have not forgotten anyone who sought You, nor have You disappointed anyone who asked You, nor have You let down anyone who relied on You, O Lord, glory be to You. Your will is action, Your decree is just, and Your command is executed... whom You protect is fortunate and saved, and whom You forsake is ruined... and they are saddened, so there is no deity... and He gives life and causes death, while He is alive and does not die. Good is in His hand, and He is over all things competent. God has fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone. {Exalted is your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe. And peace upon the messengers. And praise to God, Lord of the worlds.} [As-Saffat: 180-182]. So glory be to our Lord, and His names are sanctified and praised. The people of praise and its ultimate end, its refuge and its originator, the initiator of seriousness, its creator, and its chosen one, glory be to Him and praised. We praise You, {but you do not understand their praise.} [Al-Isra: 44]. Praise be to God who is exalted and overpowering, praise be to God who possesses and decrees, praise be to God who gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent. Glory be to Him, glory be to Him, from every other who is clothed with pride. Forgive my sins, my stumbling, my oppression, and my excesses upon myself. Provide for me from Your bounty and mercy, for they are in Your hand, and no one else possesses them. Forgive what has passed from me, protect me in what remains of my life, and conceal the faults of my parents and those of the believers from me... and the Hereafter, for all of that is in Your hand, and You are vast in forgiveness. Do not disappoint me, O Lord, nor turn my hands against my throat when I call upon You, and answer all that I have asked of You by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. O God, grant me the completion of its fasting and the attainment of hope in all that pleases You in it, with patience, faith, certainty, and expectation. Then accept that from me with continuous multiplication. May God’s blessings be upon Muḥammad, the one who answers. records.raw_text_en: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Abbās supplicated: 'O God, this is the month of Ramadan, the month of fasting, the month of standing in prayer, the month of repentance, the month of mercy, forgiveness, salvation from the Fire, and attainment of Paradise. O God, grant it safety for me, grant me safety in it, and grant it safety from me. Assist me in it with Your best assistance, guide me in it to Your obedience, occupy me in it with Your worship, supplication, and recitation of Your Book. Increase for me in it blessings, grant me in it good health, keep my body healthy in it, expand my provision in it, suffice me in it from what concerns me, answer my supplication in it, and fulfill my hope in it. O God, remove from me in it drowsiness, laziness, boredom, slackness, hardness of heart, heedlessness, and deception. Keep me away from illnesses, distractions, worries, sorrows, ailments, sins, and transgressions. Turn away from me evil, indecency, ignorance, play, fatigue, and hardship. You are the One who answers supplications. O God, protect me in it from Satan, his whispering, his spitting, his blowing, his insinuations, his discouragement, his plotting, his deception, his cavalry, his tricks, his infantry, his snares, his helpers, his parties, his followers, and his partners. O God, grant me in it diligence, striving, strength, energy, turning to You, repentance, desire, sincerity of intention, awe, piety, fear of You, hope in You, trust in You, restraint from Your prohibitions, beneficial knowledge, elevated deeds, answered supplications, and do not let anything prevent me from these due to an affliction, illness, worry, or sorrow, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. Grant me in it the best of what You grant to Your righteous servants of forgiveness, mercy, tenderness, well-being, and continuous safety in this world and the Hereafter. O God, make my supplication in it reach You, my deeds in it accepted, and my sins in it forgiven, so that my share in it is the greatest and my portion in it is the largest, for the Night of Decree, so that no one from Your friends and those most pleasing to You is given preference over it. A month, grant me in it the best of what You have granted anyone whom You have allowed to reach it and honored with it. Make me among those freed by You from the Fire, those released by You from Hell, and the fortunate of Your creation through Your forgiveness, mercy, pleasure, well-being, and safety, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. O God, Lord of the dawn and the ten nights, Lord of Jibrīl, Mīkā’īl, Isrāfīl, Ibrāhīm, Ismā‘īl, Isḥāq, Ya‘qūb, Lord of Mūsā, we flee to You from our sins, so shelter us; we are repentant, so accept our repentance; we seek forgiveness, so forgive us; we seek refuge, so grant us refuge; we submit, so do not forsake us; we flee, so grant us security; we desire, so intercede for us... Her children said 'Here we are, O Lord, here we are.' They came while the call was among the Anṣār, saying: 'O assembly of the Anṣār, O assembly of the Anṣār.' Then the call was restricted to Banī al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, saying: 'O Banī al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, O Banī al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, looked while he was on his mule, stretching towards their fighting, and said: 'This is when the battle heats up.' Then the Messenger of God, ﷺ, took pebbles and threw them at the faces of the disbelievers, then said: 'They have been defeated by the Lord of Muḥammad.' I went to look, and the battle was as it was, but the Messenger of God, ﷺ, had thrown pebbles at them. I kept seeing their edge dull and their affair retreating. God revealed: {Certainly has God given you victory on many battlefields, and on the day of Ḥunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for you; then you turned back, fleeing. Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers you did not see and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.} [At-Tawbah: 25-26]. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, took six thousand captives from them that day, women and children, and took camels and sheep in numbers they could not count. He divided the captives and the wealth into fifths. Then the delegation of Hawāzin came to him and said: 'O Messenger of God, you are the most just and most righteous of people and the most merciful to people. You have taken our women and children...' He said to them: 'The best speech is the truest. I have with me those you see of the people... all of it. Look which of the two groups you prefer. If you prefer the women and children, or if you prefer the wealth.' They said: 'Our women and children.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, stood among the Muslims and said: 'O assembly of Muslims, these are your brothers from Hawāzin. I have returned their women and children to them. Whoever wishes to make this voluntary, let him do so, and whoever wishes to have it recorded against us, let him do so.' The Muslims said: 'No, we have made it voluntary, O Messenger of God...' from those who did not make it voluntary, return until your leaders inform us of your decision in this matter. The Muslims made it voluntary, the best responder to the supplications of the distressed, the remover of every evil, the God of the worlds. I call upon You by all Your names, those I know and those I do not know, O Lord, glory be to You. To You belong the loftiest attributes and the most beautiful names, Jibrīl, the God of Ibrāhīm, Ismā‘īl, Isḥāq, and Ya‘qūb, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor. I ask You, O Lord, by You, to grant us from poverty, and do not turn our faces to anyone from Your creation, by the One besides Whom there is no deity, and to make us among... Your protection, and bestow upon them by Your grace, and be generous to them with Your pardon, by the One besides Whom there is no deity, glory be to You, O Lord. You have not forgotten anyone who sought You, nor have You disappointed anyone who asked You, nor have You let down anyone who relied on You, O Lord, glory be to You. Your will is action, Your decree is just, and Your command is executed... whom You protect is fortunate and saved, and whom You forsake is ruined... and they are saddened, so there is no deity... and He gives life and causes death, while He is alive and does not die. Good is in His hand, and He is over all things competent. God has fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone. {Exalted is your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe. And peace upon the messengers. And praise to God, Lord of the worlds.} [As-Saffat: 180-182]. So glory be to our Lord, and His names are sanctified and praised. The people of praise and its ultimate end, its refuge and its originator, the initiator of seriousness, its creator, and its chosen one, glory be to Him and praised. We praise You, {but you do not understand their praise.} [Al-Isra: 44]. Praise be to God who is exalted and overpowering, praise be to God who possesses and decrees, praise be to God who gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent. Glory be to Him, glory be to Him, from every other who is clothed with pride. Forgive my sins, my stumbling, my oppression, and my excesses upon myself. Provide for me from Your bounty and mercy, for they are in Your hand, and no one else possesses them. Forgive what has passed from me, protect me in what remains of my life, and conceal the faults of my parents and those of the believers from me... and the Hereafter, for all of that is in Your hand, and You are vast in forgiveness. Do not disappoint me, O Lord, nor turn my hands against my throat when I call upon You, and answer all that I have asked of You by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. O God, grant me the completion of its fasting and the attainment of hope in all that pleases You in it, with patience, faith, certainty, and expectation. Then accept that from me with continuous multiplication. May God’s blessings be upon Muḥammad, the one who answers. O God, You are my Lord and I am Your servant, by the right of the servant who asks his Lord, and no servant has asked the likes of You... the seekers, the end of the need of those who desire, O hope of the distressed, O refuge of those who seek help, O God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, O neighbor of those who seek refuge, hidden from every eye, hidden from every... and much praise be to God. May God’s blessings be upon our Prophet Muḥammad, the servant of God and His Messenger, peace and blessings of God. There is no power except with God, the Most High, the Most Great. My Lord suffices me among the servants, my Creator suffices me among the created, He who does not bestow from those who bestow suffices me, the Most Great suffices me. O God, assist me with Your protection, and settle me in Paradise by Your mercy, O Generous, O Lord, glory be to You. No one can repay Your favors, nor can anyone enumerate Your prohibitions. O God, I have turned to You with Your goodness, and I have confessed my sins. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have committed. O... Your religion until I meet You with it, the One besides Whom there is no deity, O Generous. O God, whatever my desire has fallen short of, and my obedience has been incapable of, and the goodness of my Hereafter and my world, and safety from every evil, so grant it to me and bestow it upon me soon. Let me recite Your Book well whenever You teach me, make it beloved to me, beautify it in my eyes, illuminate it in my heart, and expand my chest with it... You prohibit in it from Your trials until You bring me, by Your favor, to the ranks of those whom You have perfected in it... by it, O Most Merciful of the merciful. Make it for me, O Lord, a guide, a light, guidance, mercy, and an argument for me, and do not make it an argument against me. Teach me from it what I do not know, and grant me its recitation during the hours of the night and day in the manner that pleases You... I call upon You by Your name, which You have mentioned in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen. I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge in all my affairs, and I seek Your power by Your ability in all my affairs. Choose for me the best choice in everything I enter into, and in everything I leave, and in everything I have mentioned seeking Your refuge in it. I ask You from Your bounty in that which You know is good for me, O Knower of the unseen. In it is the good in the immediate... for its light are the heavens and the earth, O God, Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Do not deprive me of the reward of what I ask You... and from the fearful, and the end of the desire of the worshippers, the reliever of the distressed, the comforter of the grieving... and upon him be peace, and the mercy of God. What God wills, there is no power except with God the Most Great. I bear witness that God is over all things competent, and that God encompasses all things in knowledge.
records.display_text_en: Abū Hāni’ al-Khawlānī reported to me from Abī ‘Abd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘Āṣ, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'God decreed the destinies of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth.'

records.text_en: ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī reported to me from Shu‘bah ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abī Sinān, from Abī Wā’il, who said: I heard Ibn Mas‘ūd say: 'I wish that God would forgive me for one of my sins or a mistake from my errors, and that no lineage would be known for me.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ 581 - وَأَخْبَرَنِي يُونُسُ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، أَنَّ عُرْوَةَ بْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ، حَدَّثَهُ، عَنْ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ أُمِّ حَبِيبَةَ بِنْتِ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: هَلْ لَكَ فِي أُخْتِي بِنْتِ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ؟ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ، صلى الله عليه وسلم: «فَاعِلٌ مَاذَا؟» ، قَالَتْ: تَنْكِحُهَا، قَالَ: «أُخْتُكِ؟» ، قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: «وَتُحِبِّينَ ذَلِكَ؟» ، قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ وَلَسْتُ مِنْكَ بِمُخْلِيَةٍ، وَأَحَقُّ مَنْ شَرِكَنِي فِي خَيْرٍ إِلَيَّ أُخْتِي. قَالَ: «فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَحِلُّ لِي» ، قَالَتْ: فَوَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أُخْبِرْتُ أَنَّكَ تَخْطُبُ ابْنَةَ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، قَالَ: «بِنْتُ أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ؟» قَالَتْ ⦗ص: 672⦘ : نَعَمْ، قَالَ: «فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْ لَمْ تَكُنْ رَبِيبَتِي فِي حِجْرِي مَا حَلَّتْ لِي ، إِنَّهَا ابْنَةُ أَخِي مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ، أَرْضَعَتْنِي وَإِيَّاهَا ثُوَيْبَةُ، وَلَا تَعْرِضْنَ عَلَيَّ بَنَاتِكُنَّ وَلَا أَخَوَاتِكُنَّ» ⦗ص: 673⦘

records.display_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يُونُسُ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، أَنَّ عُرْوَةَ بْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ، حَدَّثَهُ، عَنْ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ أُمِّ حَبِيبَةَ بِنْتِ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: هَلْ لَكَ فِي أُخْتِي بِنْتِ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ؟ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ، صلى الله عليه وسلم: «فَاعِلٌ مَاذَا؟» ، قَالَتْ: تَنْكِحُهَا، قَالَ: «أُخْتُكِ؟» ، قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: «وَتُحِبِّينَ ذَلِكَ؟» ، قَالَتْ: نَعَمْ وَلَسْتُ مِنْكَ بِمُخْلِيَةٍ، وَأَحَقُّ مَنْ شَرِكَنِي فِي خَيْرٍ إِلَيَّ أُخْتِي. قَالَ: «فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَحِلُّ لِي» ، قَالَتْ: فَوَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أُخْبِرْتُ أَنَّكَ تَخْطُبُ ابْنَةَ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، قَالَ: «بِنْتُ أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ؟» قَالَتْ : نَعَمْ، قَالَ: «فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْ لَمْ تَكُنْ رَبِيبَتِي فِي حِجْرِي مَا حَلَّتْ لِي ، إِنَّهَا ابْنَةُ أَخِي مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ، أَرْضَعَتْنِي وَإِيَّاهَا ثُوَيْبَةُ، وَلَا تَعْرِضْنَ عَلَيَّ بَنَاتِكُنَّ وَلَا أَخَوَاتِكُنَّ»
records.raw_text_en: ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī reported to me from Shu‘bah ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abī Sinān, from Abī Wā’il, who said: I heard Ibn Mas‘ūd say: 'I wish that God would forgive me for one of my sins or a mistake from my errors, and that no lineage would be known for me.'
records.display_text_en: Yūnus reported to me from Ibn Shihāb that ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr told him from Zaynab bint Abī Salamah, from Umm Ḥabībah bint Abī Sufyān, that she said to the Messenger of God, ﷺ: 'Do you want my sister, the daughter of Abī Sufyān?' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'What would I do?' She said: 'Marry her.' He said: 'Your sister?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you like that?' She said: 'Yes, and I am not one to keep you to myself. The most deserving of those who share with me in goodness is my sister.' He said: 'She is not lawful for me.' She said: 'By God, I was told that you are proposing to the daughter of Abī Salamah.' He said: 'The daughter of Umm Salamah?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'By God, even if she were not my stepdaughter under my care, she would not be lawful for me. She is the daughter of my brother through nursing. Thuwaybah nursed me and her. Do not offer me your daughters or sisters.'
