records.text_en: ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Umar ibn Ḥafṣ ibn ‘Āṣim ibn ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb reported to me from Nāfi‘, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, 'used to wear a ring on his right hand and place its stone on the inside of his palm.' Nāfi‘ said 'Ibn ‘Umar’s ring was made of silver.'

records.text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me from Ibn Shihāb who said Someone I do not suspect told me from ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Abbās that he said: ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb saw a gold ring on my hand during his caliphate. His anger was evident, intending to remove it from my finger. I extended my finger to him, 'so he pulled it off and threw it away.'

matched_source_translation.english_text: ‘Amr ibn al-Ḥārith reported to me from Bakr ibn Sawādah that Abū al-Najīb told him that Abū Sa‘īd al-Khudrī told him that a man came from Najrān to the Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, wearing a gold ring. The Messenger of Allāh, peace and blessings be upon him, turned away from him and said 'You have come to me with a coal of fire in your hand.'

records.text_en: ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī reported to me, and Sufyān al-Thawrī reported to me from al-A‘mash, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from Aslam, who said ‘Abd Allāh ibn Mas‘ūd said: 'If you knew my sins, no two men among you would walk behind me, and you would throw dust on my head. I wish that God would forgive me for one of my sins and that I would be called ‘Abd Allāh ibn Rawthah.'

records.display_text_en: Usāmah ibn Zayd reported to me that he heard Makḥūl al-Dimashqī say: ‘Awf ibn Mālik al-Ashja‘ī entered upon ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb wearing a gold ring. ‘Umar struck his hand and said 'Throw this away.' He threw it away. ‘Umar said: 'I think we have hurt you and destroyed your ring.' The next day, he came wearing an iron ring. ‘Umar said: 'You have replaced the adornment of the people of the Fire.' records.matn_ar: إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ صَلُّوا وَنَامُوا، وَأَنْتُمْ لَمْ تَزَالُوا فِي صَلَاةٍ مُنْذُ انْتَظَرْتُمُوهَا، كَأَنِّي أَنْظُرُ إِلَى وَبِيصِ خَاتَمِهِ فِي الظُّلْمَةِ لَيْلَتَئِذٍ، وَبَعْضُهُمْ يَزِيدُ عَلَى بَعْضٍ»
records.isnad_en: ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Umar, Anas ibn ‘Iyāḍ, and Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl who said: I heard Anas ibn Mālik being asked if the Prophet, ﷺ, had a ring. He said Yes, he delayed the ‘Ishā’ prayer until half the night. Then he turned to us after praying and said: '

records.boundary_review_note: Three named transmitters are listed before Humayd al-Tawil, who says he heard Anas ibn Malik answer a question about the Prophet's ring. Matn begins with the address to the waiting people.

records.display_text_en: Others reported to me from Anas ibn Mālik that when the Prophet, ﷺ, wanted to write to Kisrā, Qayṣar, and the kings, he was told they would accept letters only if sealed. So he had a silver ring made. The Messenger of God forbade gold rings and instructed that silver rings be used. Anas said: He led us in the ʿIshāʾ prayer, and I was in the second or third row. The Messenger of God turned to us and said, ‘I have had a ring made,’ and raised his finger, ‘so do not … make [an inscription] on it.’ Anas explained: ‘That is, do not engrave it.’ Its inscription was ‘Muḥammad, the Messenger of God.’

records.text_ar: قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، أَنَّ مُحَمَّدَ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ، حَدَّثَهُ، " أَنَّ مُعَاذَ بْنَ جَبَلٍ لَمَّا قَدِمَ مِنَ الْيَمَنِ حِينَ بَعَثَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَدِمَ وَفِي يَدِهِ خَاتَمٌ مِنْ وَرِقٍ نَقْشُهُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ⦗ص: 697⦘ : «يَا مُعَاذُ ، مَا هَذَا الْخَاتَمُ؟» ، فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنِّي كُنْتُ أَكْتُبُ كُتُبًا إِلَى النَّاسِ فَأَفْرُقُ أَنْ يُزَادَ فِيهَا وَيُنقَصَ مِنْهَا، وَاتَّخَذْتُ خَاتَمًا أَخْتِمُ بِهِ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «مَا نَقْشُهُ؟» ، فَقَالَ مُعَاذٌ: مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، فَقَالَ: «آمَنَ كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مِنْ مُعَاذٍ حَتَّى خَاتَمُهُ» ثُمَّ أَخَذَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، فَتَخَتَّمَهُ

records.raw_text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me from Ibn Shihāb, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said 'The ring of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, was made of silver, and its stone was Ethiopian.'
records.display_text_en: Usāmah ibn Zayd reported to me that Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Affān told him that Mu‘ādh ibn Jabal, when he returned from Yemen after the Messenger of God, ﷺ, sent him, arrived with a silver ring engraved with "Muḥammad, the Messenger of God." The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to him: 'O Mu‘ādh, what is this ring?' He said: 'O Messenger of God, I used to write letters to the people and feared that something might be added or removed, so I made a ring to seal with.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'What is its engraving?' Mu‘ādh said: 'Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, ﷺ.' He said: 'Everything about Mu‘ādh is trustworthy, even his ring.' Then the Messenger of God, ﷺ, took it and wore it.

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb said Hishām ibn Sa‘d reported to me from Sa‘īd al-Maqburī, from his father, from Abī Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'God has removed from you the arrogance of the Jāhiliyyah and its boasting about ancestors. A believer is pious, and a wicked person is miserable. You are the children of Ādam, and Ādam was from dust. Let men cease boasting about people, for they are merely coals from the coals of Hell, or they will be more insignificant to God than the dung beetles that push filth with their noses.'

records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ: أَخْبَرَنِي مَالِكُ بْنُ أَنَسٍ، وَابْنُ أَبِي ذِئْبٍ، وَيُونُسُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، وَابْنُ سَمْعَانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ السُّلَمِيِّ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، أُمُورًا كُنَّا نَصْنَعُهَا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: كُنَّا نَأْتِي الْكُهَّانَ، قَالَ: «فَلَا تَأْتُوا الْكُهَّانَ» ، قَالَ: كُنَّا نَتَطَيَّرُ. قَالَ: «ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ يَجِدُهُ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي نَفْسِهِ فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكُمْ»

records.display_text_en: Yūnus reported to me from Ibn Shihāb, who said: It reached us that Abū Hurayrah said the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: ‘There is no contagion, no ill omen, and no hāmah (the pre-Islamic omen bird).’

records.display_text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me from Ibn Shihāb that Abū Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Raḥmān told him that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'There is no contagion.' He also narrated that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Do not bring the sick near the healthy.' Abū Salamah said: Abū Hurayrah used to narrate both from the Messenger of God, ﷺ. Then Abū Hurayrah later stopped saying 'there is no contagion' and insisted that a keeper of diseased camels should not bring them among healthy camels. Al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Dhubāb, who was the cousin of Abū Hurayrah, said: I used to hear you, O Abū Hurayrah, narrating along with this hadith another hadith. He said: I had stopped it. You used to say: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'There is no contagion.' Abū Hurayrah refused to acknowledge that and said: 'Do not bring the sick near the healthy.' Al-Ḥārith did not see anything wrong with that until Abū Hurayrah became angry. Abū Hurayrah then spoke in Abyssinian and said to al-Ḥārith: 'Do you know what I said?' He said: 'No.' Abū Hurayrah said: 'I refuse.' Abū Salamah said: By my life, Abū Hurayrah used to narrate to us that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'There is no contagion.' I do not know whether Abū Hurayrah forgot or one of the two sayings abrogated the other.

records.display_text_en: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd reported to me from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who heard Ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī say: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: ‘There are no omens, no contagion, no hāmah (omen bird), and no ghouls.’ A man said, ‘O Messenger of God, a mangy camel came among healthy camels and they all became mangy.’ The Messenger of God asked, ‘Who made the first one mangy?’ The man replied, ‘God made it mangy.’ The Messenger of God said, ‘God made this one mangy; this is an affliction and a decree.’

records.raw_text_en: Ibn Abī Dhi’b reported to me from ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Mihrān, from ‘Umayr, the freed slave of Ibn ‘Abbās, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'There is no contagion, no haunting, and no ghoul.'
records.display_text_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād reported to me from his father, who said: Men known for integrity and contentment, among the sons of the Companions and the foremost people, told me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: ‘There is no contagion, no hāmah, and no Ṣafar. Keep away from a person afflicted with leprosy as one keeps away from a lion.’

records.text_en: Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthmān reported to me from his mother Fāṭimah bint Ḥusayn, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Abbās, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Do not stare at them,' meaning the lepers.

records.display_text_en: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh reported to me from his father, who said: Khārijah ibn Zayd ibn Thābit told me that a man afflicted with leprosy used to visit ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. When food was brought while the man was with him, ʿUmar would say, ‘So-and-so, eat from what is in front of you. By God, if someone else were afflicted with what you have—or had the illness you have—he would not sit within a spear’s length of me.’ Ḥarmalah said: He was Muʿayqib, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb’s treasurer in charge of the public funds.

records.display_text_en: I heard Mālik ibn Anas say: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr told me that Ibn Abī Mulaykah informed him: While ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was circumambulating the Kaʿbah, he saw a woman afflicted with leprosy and said to her, ‘Do not harm the people.’ She remained at home. After ʿUmar died, people came to her and said, ‘The one who forbade you to go out has died, so go out.’ She replied, ‘By God, I would not obey him while he was alive only to disobey him after his death!’
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ مَالِكَ بْنَ أَنَسٍ، يَقُولُ: حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، أَنَّ ابْنَ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ، أَخْبَرَهُ، قَالَ:
records.matn_ar: بَيْنَمَا عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ يَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ نَظَرَ إِلَى امْرَأَةٍ مَجْذُومَةٍ، فَقَالَ لَهَا عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ: «لَا تُؤْذِي النَّاسَ» فَجَلَسَتْ فِي بَيْتِهَا، فَلَمَّا تُوُفِّيَ عُمَرُ جَاءَهَا النَّاسُ، فَقَالُوا لَهَا: إِنَّ الَّذِي نَهَاكِ عَنِ الْخُرُوجِ قَدْ مَاتَ فَاخْرُجِي، قَالَتْ: وَاللَّهِ لَا أُطِيعُهُ حَيًّا وَأَعْصِيهِ مَيِّتًا

records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِكُ بْنُ أَنَسٍ، وَيُوسُفُ بْنُ طَهْمَانَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ ⦗ص: 732⦘ أَبِي أُمَامَةَ بْنِ سَهْلِ بْنِ حُنَيْفٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَاهُ، يَقُولُ: اغْتَسَلَ أَبِي سَهْلُ بْنُ حُنَيْفٍ بِالْخَرَّارِ فَنَزَعَ جُبَّةً كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ ، وَعَامِرُ بْنُ رَبِيعَةَ يَنْظُرُ ، وَكَانَ سَهْلٌ رَجُلًا أَبْيَضَ حَسَنَ الْجِلْدِ ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عَامِرُ بْنُ رَبِيعَةَ: مَا رَأَيْتُ كَالْيَوْمِ قَطُّ، وَلَا جِلْدَ عَذْرَاءَ، فَوُعِكَ سَهْلٌ مَكَانَهُ وَاشْتَدَّ وَجَعُهُ، فَأُتِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فَأُخْبِرَ أَنَّ سَهْلًا وَجِعَ ، وَأَنَّهُ غَيْرُ رَائِحٍ مَعَكَ، فَأَتَاهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، فَأَخْبَرَهُ بِالَّذِي كَانَ مِنْ شَأْنِ عَامِرٍ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «عَلَامَ يَقْتُلُ أَحَدُكُمْ أَخَاهُ أَلَا بَرَّكْتَ، إِنَّ الْعَيْنَ حَقٌّ، تَوَضَّأْ لَهُ» ، فَتَوَضَّأَ فَرَاحَ سَهْلُ بْنُ حُنَيْفٍ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ، صلى الله عليه وسلم ، لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ وَأَحَدُهُمَا يَزِيدُ عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ، وَقَالَ يُوسُفُ بْنُ طَهْمَانَ فِي الْحَدِيثِ: إِنَّ سَهْلًا قَامَ يَغْتَسِلُ يَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ حِينَ هَزَمَ اللَّهُ الْعَدُوَّ، وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ: سَأَلْتُ ابْنَ شِهَابٍ كَيْفَ غَسَلَ عَامِرٌ لِسَهْلٍ حِينَ أَصَابَهُ بِالْعَيْنِ؟، فَقَالَ: غَسَلَ وَجْهَهُ وَيَدَيْهِ وَمِرْفَقَيْهِ وَرُكْبَتَيْهِ وَأَطْرَافَ رِجْلَيْهِ وَدَاخِلَةَ إِزَارِهِ ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ صَبَّ عَلَى سَهْلِ بْنِ حُنَيْفٍ فَرَاحَ لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ

records.raw_text_en: Wāqid ibn Salamah reported to me from Yazīd al-Raqāshī, from Anas ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'There is no contagion, no haunting, and the most truthful omen is a good omen. The evil eye is real.'
records.display_text_en: Mālik ibn Anas and Yūsuf ibn Tahmān reported to me from Muḥammad ibn Abī Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf that he heard his father say: My father, Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, bathed at al-Kharrār and removed a cloak he was wearing while ‘Āmir ibn Rabī‘ah was watching. Sahl was a fair-skinned man with beautiful skin. ‘Āmir ibn Rabī‘ah said to him: 'I have never seen the like of what I see today, not even the skin of a virgin.' Sahl fell ill on the spot, and his pain intensified. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, was informed that Sahl was ill and could not go with him. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, came to him and was told what had happened with ‘Āmir. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Why would one of you kill his brother? Why did you not say: May God bless you? The evil eye is real. Perform ablution for him.' ‘Āmir performed ablution for him, and Sahl ibn Ḥunayf went with the Messenger of God, ﷺ, in the evening, feeling no harm. One narrator adds more than the other. Yūsuf ibn Tahmān said in the hadith: Sahl was bathing on the day of Ḥunayn when God defeated the enemy. Mālik said: I asked Ibn Shihāb how ‘Āmir washed for Sahl when he was afflicted by the evil eye. He said: He washed his face, hands, elbows, knees, the tips of his feet, and the inside of his lower garment. Then he poured the water over Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, and he went feeling no harm.

records.boundary_review_note: Malik and Yusuf ibn Tahman are parallel sources. Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah reports from his father about Sahl ibn Hunayf and Amir ibn Rabiah; the report concerns the evil eye.

records.raw_text_en: Mālik ibn Anas and Yūsuf ibn Tahmān reported to me from Muḥammad ibn Abī Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf that he heard his father say: My father, Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, bathed at al-Kharrār and removed a cloak he was wearing while ‘Āmir ibn Rabī‘ah was watching. Sahl was a fair-skinned man with beautiful skin. ‘Āmir ibn Rabī‘ah said to him: 'I have never seen the like of what I see today, not even the skin of a virgin.' Sahl fell ill on the spot, and his pain intensified. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, was informed that Sahl was ill and could not go with him. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, came to him and was told what had happened with ‘Āmir. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Why would one of you kill his brother? Why did you not say: May God bless you? The evil eye is real. Perform ablution for him.' ‘Āmir performed ablution for him, and Sahl ibn Ḥunayf went with the Messenger of God, ﷺ, in the evening, feeling no harm. One narrator adds more than the other. Yūsuf ibn Tahmān said in the hadith: Sahl was bathing on the day of Ḥunayn when God defeated the enemy. Mālik said: I asked Ibn Shihāb how ‘Āmir washed for Sahl when he was afflicted by the evil eye. He said: He washed his face, hands, elbows, knees, the tips of his feet, and the inside of his lower garment. Then he poured the water over Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, and he went feeling no harm.
records.display_text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd, Mālik ibn Anas, and Ibn Samʿān reported to me from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, who told him that ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah passed by Sahl ibn Ḥunayf while he was bathing at al-Kharrār and said, ‘By God, I have never seen anything like today—not even the skin of a secluded woman.’ Sahl collapsed. The Messenger of God was called, and they said to him, ‘O Messenger of God, will you attend to Sahl ibn Ḥunayf? By God, he cannot raise his head.’ The Messenger of God asked, ‘Do you suspect anyone?’ They said, ‘Yes. ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah passed by him while he was bathing and said, “By God, I have never seen anything like today—not even the skin of a secluded woman.”’ The Messenger of God summoned ʿĀmir and reproached him, saying, ‘Why would one of you kill his brother? Why did you not invoke a blessing? Wash for him.’ ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah washed his face, hands, elbows, knees, the tips of his feet, and the inside of his lower garment in a vessel, then poured the water over him. That evening Sahl went out with the people, unharmed.

The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Leave it as blameworthy.' Ibn Sam‘ān reported to me... from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, similarly.
records.display_text_en: Abū [name omitted] Nawfal reported to me from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād, that a woman from the Anṣār came to the Messenger of God and said, “Messenger of God, we bought a house and moved into it. We were many, but our number dwindled; we had much wealth, but became impoverished; and we were on good terms, but then became estranged.” The Messenger of God said, “Why did you not leave it as an ill-omened place?” She asked, “What should we do with it, Messenger of God?” He replied, “Sell it or give it away.”

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥabīb, the freedman of ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said 'The people complained to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, during the year of Khaybar about what had befallen them, saying: If only we could move away from here.'

records.text_en: Ibn Samʿān reported to me that Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed him that he had heard that during the year of Khaybar, the Messenger of God, ﷺ, camped near Mirṭah. His path to the fortress of Banī al-Qarān was through the interior of Mirṭah. It was said to him: 'O Messenger of God, it is a plague-ridden place.' So he took another path, which was longer, and that was his route for forty nights until God granted him victory. He did not traverse the interior of Mirṭah out of aversion to what was said about it.

records.text_en: I heard Mālik say: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd reported to me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to al-Qaḥḥah al-Ṭalḥah: 'Who will milk this?' A man stood up, and the Prophet, ﷺ, asked him: 'What is your name?' He replied: 'Murrah.' The Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Sit down.' Then he said: 'Who will milk this?' Another man stood up, and the Prophet, ﷺ, asked him: 'What is your name?' He replied: 'Ḥarb.' The Prophet, ﷺ, said: 'Sit down.' Then he said: 'Who will milk this?' Another man stood up, and the Prophet, ﷺ, asked him: 'What is your name?' He replied: 'Yaʿīsh.' The Prophet said: 'Milk it.' So he milked it. Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah, who reported from Mūsā ibn ʿUlayy, from his father, from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, similarly. Ibn Lahīʿah reported from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, similarly.

records.display_text_en: I heard Mālik say: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd reported to me that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said about Talḥah’s milch-camel, ‘Who will milk this?’ A man stood up, and the Prophet asked him, ‘What is your name?’ He replied, ‘Murrah (Bitterness).’ The Prophet said, ‘Sit down.’ He then asked, ‘Who will milk this?’ Another man stood up. The Prophet asked his name, and he replied, ‘Yaʿīsh (He will live).’ The Prophet said, ‘Milk it.’ So he milked it.

records.text_en: Ibn Samʿān reported to me from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith al-Taymī that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Who will milk for us?' A man from Banī Sulaym stood up and said: 'I will, O Messenger of God.' The Prophet asked: 'Who is this speaker?' He replied: 'I am al-Musāwir.' The Prophet said: 'Sit down.' Then the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Who will milk for us?' Another man from Banī Sulaym stood up and said: 'I will, O Messenger of God.' The Prophet asked: 'Who is the speaker?' He replied: 'I am Khidāsh.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, laughed and said: 'Sit down.' Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: 'O Messenger of God, should I speak or remain silent?' The Prophet said: 'Rather, remain silent, and I will inform you of what you intended.' He said: 'Then inform me, O Messenger of God.' The Prophet said: 'You thought, O ʿUmar, that it was an evil omen.' He said: 'There is no omen except God’s omen, and no good except His good, but I prefer a good omen.'

records.raw_text_en: Ibn Samʿān reported to me from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith al-Taymī that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Who will milk for us?' A man from Banī Sulaym stood up and said: 'I will, O Messenger of God.' The Prophet asked: 'Who is this speaker?' He replied: 'I am al-Musāwir.' The Prophet said: 'Sit down.' Then the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Who will milk for us?' Another man from Banī Sulaym stood up and said: 'I will, O Messenger of God.' The Prophet asked: 'Who is the speaker?' He replied: 'I am Khidāsh.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, laughed and said: 'Sit down.' Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: 'O Messenger of God, should I speak or remain silent?' The Prophet said: 'Rather, remain silent, and I will inform you of what you intended.' He said: 'Then inform me, O Messenger of God.' The Prophet said: 'You thought, O ʿUmar, that it was an evil omen.' He said: 'There is no omen except God’s omen, and no good except His good, but I prefer a good omen.'

records.boundary_review_note: The report recounts the Prophet asking for someone to milk an animal and exchanging words with two men and Umar. Matn begins مَنْ يَحْلُبُ لَنَا.

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās, from Abī al-Ḥuṣayn, from Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd al-Anṣārī, a companion of the Prophet, ﷺ, who said 'Whoever is deterred by an evil omen has committed an act of polytheism.' Al-Layth ibn Saʿd reported to me from ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās, from Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī, from Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd, similarly. Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from ʿUbayd God ibn Hubayrah, from Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Maʿāfirī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, similarly.

records.text_en: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith reported to me that al-Julāḥ informed him that Aws informed him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ met Kaʿb with two books. He said to him: 'O Kaʿb, what about the knowledge of the stars?' Kaʿb replied: 'There is no good in it.' ʿAbd Allāh asked: 'Why?' Kaʿb said: 'You see in it what you dislike,' meaning omens. Kaʿb said: 'Even if it passes?' And he said: 'O God, there is no omen except Your omen, no good except Your good, and no lord besides You.' Then he fell silent. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said: 'There is no power nor strength except with You.' Kaʿb said: 'ʿAbd Allāh has spoken the truth. By the One in Whose hand is my soul, it is the essence of reliance and the treasure of the servant in Paradise. Whoever says it at that time and then proceeds, nothing will harm him.' ʿAbd Allāh said: 'What if he does not proceed but stays?' Kaʿb replied: 'He has tasted polytheism.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، أَنَّ الْجُلَاحَ، حَدَّثَهُ، أَنَّ أَوْسًا حَدَّثَهُ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ، الْتَقَى هُوَ وَكَعْبٌ، بِالْكِتَابَيْنِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ: يَا كَعْبُ ، عِلْمُ النُّجُومِ؟ قَالَ لَهُ كَعْبٌ: لَا خَيْرَ فِيهِ، قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: لِمَ؟ قَالَ: تَرَى فِيهِ مَا تَكْرَهُ ، يُرِيدُ الطِّيَرَةَ، قَالَ كَعْبٌ: وَإِنْ مَضَى، وَقَالَ: «اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّهُ لَا طَيْرَ إِلَّا طَيْرُكَ، وَلَا خَيْرَ إِلَّا خَيْرُكَ، وَلَا رَبَّ غَيْرُكَ» ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ سَكَتَ، فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرٍو: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِكَ، قَالَ كَعْبٌ: جَاءَ بِهَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ ، وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ إِنَّهَا لِرَأْسُ التَّوَكُّلِ وَكَنْزُ الْعَبْدِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ، وَلَا يَقُولُهَا عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ يَمْضِي إِلَّا لَمْ يَضُرَّهُ شَيْءٌ، قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: أَفَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ لَمْ يَمْضِ فَقَعَدَ؟ قَالَ: طَعِمَ الْإِشْرَاكَ

records.boundary_review_note: The report recounts Abdullah ibn Amr meeting Kab and discussing astrology and omens. Matn begins الْتَقَى هُوَ وَكَعْبٌ.

records.text_en: Usāmah ibn Zayd reported to me: I heard Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim say: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār asked ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: 'Do you take omens?' He replied: 'Yes.' Kaʿb asked: 'What do you say when you take an omen?' He said 'I say: O God, there is no omen except Your omen, no good except Your good, no lord besides You, and no power except with You.' Kaʿb said: 'You are the most knowledgeable of the Arabs, and it is indeed as such in the Torah.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ نَافِعَ بْنَ جُبَيْرِ بْنِ مُطْعِمٍ، يَقُولُ: سَأَلَ كَعْبُ الْأَحْبَارِ، عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَمْرٍو، فَقَالَ: هَلْ تَطَيَّرُ؟، فَقَالَ: «نَعَمْ» ، قَالَ: فَكَيْفَ تَقُولُ إِذَا تَطَيَّرْتَ؟ ، قَالَ: أَقُولُ: «اللَّهُمَّ لَا طَيْرَ إِلَّا طَيْرُكَ، وَلَا خَيْرَ إِلَّا خَيْرُكَ، وَلَا رَبَّ غَيْرُكَ، وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِكَ» فَقَالَ كَعْبٌ: أَنْتَ أَفْقَهُ الْعَرَبِ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَذَلِكَ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ

Kaʿb asked: 'What do you say when you take an omen?' He said 'I say: O God, there is no omen except Your omen, no good except Your good, no lord besides You, and no power except with You.' Kaʿb said: 'You are the most knowledgeable of the Arabs, and it is indeed as such in the Torah.'

records.text_en: Ibn Samʿān reported to me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ informed him from the companions of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said 'The Messenger of God, ﷺ, forbade amulets and charms.' It was said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: 'We know what amulets are, but what are charms?' He replied: 'What some women use to endear themselves to their husbands, like soothsaying and the like.'

narrator_path.name_en: The companions of Abdullah ibn Masud (unnamed group)
narrator_path.source_form: عَنْ أَصْحَابِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ

records.boundary_review_note: The route passes through unnamed companions of Abdullah ibn Masud; they remain a group rather than individually identified narrators. Matn begins نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ.

records.text_en: Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ reported to me from Khālid ibn ʿUbayd, from Mishraḥ ibn Hāʿān, who said: I heard ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī say: 'I heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: Whoever hangs an amulet, may God not complete it for him, and whoever hangs a cowrie shell, may God not grant him peace.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي حَيْوَةُ بْنُ شُرَيْحٍ، عَنْ خَالِدِ بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ، عَنْ مِشْرَحِ بْنِ هَاعَانَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ عُقْبَةَ بْنَ عَامِرٍ الْجُهَنِيَّ، يَقُولُ: " سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ، صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ ، يَقُولُ: «مَنْ عَلَّقَ تَمِيمَةً فَلَا أَتَمَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ، وَمَنْ عَلَّقَ وَدَعَةً فَلَا وَدَعَ اللَّهُ لَهُ»

narrator_path.name_en: An unnamed man from Banu Ghifar

records.boundary_review_note: An unnamed man from Banu Ghifar says his mother took him to the Messenger, who removed his amulet. Matn begins دَخَلَتْ أُمِّي.

records.text_en: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd reported to me that Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd informed him: It reached us that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd entered the house of one of his family members while he was wearing an iron bead necklace. He cut it off and said 'The family of Ibn Masʿūd is free from polytheism.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي اللَّيْثُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، أَنْ يَحْيَى بْنَ سَعِيدٍ حَدَّثَهُ، قَالَ: بَلَغَنَا أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ مَسْعُودٍ دَخَلَ عَلَى بَعْضِ أَهْلِهِ وَعَلَيْهِ خَرَزَةٌ مُعَلَّقَةٌ، فَقَطَعَهَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: «إِنَّ أَهْلَ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ لَأَغْنِيَاءُ عَنِ الشِّرْكِ»

records.text_en: Ibrāhīm ibn Nashīṭ and al-Layth reported to me from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb that he heard Abī al-Khayr say: I heard ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir say regarding amulets: 'Wherever it is placed on a person, that place becomes an act of polytheism.'

records.text_en: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from Ibn Zaḥr, from Bakr ibn Sawādah, from a man of Ṣudāʾ, who said We came to the Prophet, ﷺ, twelve men and pledged allegiance, but he left one man without taking his pledge. We said: 'Pledge allegiance to him, O Prophet of God.' He said: 'I will not take his pledge until he removes what he is wearing, for whoever among us wears such a thing is a polytheist as long as he wears it.' We looked and saw that on his upper arm was a strap containing something from the bark of a tree or a piece of a tree.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، عَنِ ابْنِ زَحْرٍ، عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ سَوَادَةَ، عَنْ رَجُلٍ مِنْ صُدًا، قَالَ: أَتَيْنَا النَّبِيَّ ، صلى الله عليه وسلم ، اثْنَا عَشَرَ رَجُلًا فَبَايَعْنَا وَتَرَكَ مِنَّا رَجُلًا لَمْ يُبَايِعْهُ، فَقُلْنَا: بَايِعْهُ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: «لَنْ أُبَايِعَهُ حَتَّى يَنْزِعَ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ؛ إِنَّهُ مَنْ كَانَ مِنَّا عَلَيْهِ مِثْلَ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ كَانَ مُشْرِكًا، مَا كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ» قَالَ: فَنَظَرْنَا فَإِذَا فِي عَضُدِهِ سَيْرٌ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ مِنْ لِحَا شَجَرَةٍ، أَوْ شَيْءٌ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib used to say: 'Hanging amulets is a branch of the practices of the Age of Ignorance.'

records.text_en: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith reported to me that Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed him that his mother told him that she sent her brother Makhramah to ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ. He was being treated for an ulcer that affects children. When ʿĀʾishah saw him and finished with him, she noticed two iron anklets on his legs. ʿĀʾishah said 'Do you think these two anklets will ward off anything that God has decreed for him? If I had seen them, he would not have been treated near me, or even touched near me. By my life, two silver anklets are purer than these.'

records.text_en: Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid wrote to me, saying: ʿAlqamah ibn Abī ʿAlqamah reported to me from his mother, from ʿĀʾishah, that she used to be brought children when they were born so that she could invoke God’s blessing upon them. A child was brought to her, and as she was about to take him, she found something under his pillow and threw it away. She said 'The Messenger of God, ﷺ, disapproved of omens and forbade them.'

records.text_en: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr reported to me from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAbdah bint Abī Ḥumaydah, who said I entered with my brother Bukayr upon Umm al-Muʾminīn ʿĀʾishah to seek her blessing for him. A woman entered with her child, who had a black mark drawn between his eyes or on his forehead. ʿĀʾishah said: 'I will not bless him until this mark is erased.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، عَنْ عَبْدَةَ بِنْتِ أَبِي حُمَيْدَةَ، قَالَتْ: دَخَلْتُ بِأَخِي بُكَيْرٍ عَلَى أُمِّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَائِشَةَ، لِتُبَارِكَ عَلَيْهِ، وَدَخَلَتِ امْرَأَةٌ عَلَيْهَا بِصَبِيٍّ لَهَا قَدْ خَطَّتْ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ، أَوْ فِي جَبْهَتِهِ خَطًّا أَسْوَدَ، فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ: «لَا أُبَارِكُ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يُمْحَى هَذَا الْخَطُّ»

records.matn_en: I entered with my brother Bukayr upon Umm al-Muʾminīn ʿĀʾishah to seek her blessing for him. A woman entered with her child, who had a black mark drawn between his eyes or on his forehead. ʿĀʾishah said: 'I will not bless him until this mark is erased.'
records.boundary_review_note: Abdah bint Abi Humaydah narrates entering with her brother Bukayr to seek Aishah's blessing; the woman with the child is a participant in her account. Matn begins دَخَلْتُ بِأَخِي.

records.text_en: Mālik ibn Anas wrote to me regarding the iron ring worn by a pregnant woman, saying: It reached me that ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet, used to dislike that.

records.text_en: Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb reported to me from Abī ʿĪsā al-Khurāsānī that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, passed by a man who had an iron ring or an iron signet ring on his hand. He asked: 'What is this?' The man replied: 'For weakness.' The Prophet said 'It will only increase your weakness.' Another person reported to me from al-Ḥasan, from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, similarly, and the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to him: 'If you die while believing it benefits you, you will not see the face of Muḥammad.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ 672 - وَأَخْبَرَنِي سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ أَبِي عِيسَى الْخُرَاسَانِيِّ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، مَرَّ بِرَجُلٍ وَفِي يَدِهِ حَلَقَةٌ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ أَوْ خَاتَمٌ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ، فَقَالَ: «هَذِهِ؟» ، فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ: مِنَ الْوَاهِنَةِ، فَقَالَ: «وَلَا تَزِيدُكَ إِلَّا وَهْنًا» ⦗ص: 757⦘

records.text_en: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim reported to me that he heard al-Ḥasan say: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Whoever hangs something will be left to it.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah and ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith reported to me from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, that ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ, said 'An amulet is not what is hung after the affliction has occurred.'

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb that he said 'I saw a bead that belonged to ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith al-Zubaydī, a companion of the Prophet, ﷺ, used for facial paralysis. It was placed in the sun, then wiped on the face of the person with facial paralysis.'

records.text_en: ʿUqbah ibn Nāfiʿ reported to me that Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd used to dislike a drink that prevents pregnancy, or what prevents pregnancy from a drink, fearing it might kill what is in the womb.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عُقْبَةُ بْنُ نَافِعٍ، قَالَ: «كَانَ يَحْيَى بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، يَكْرَهُ الشَّرَابَ يَمْنَعُ الْحَبَلَ، وَمَا يَمْنَعُ الْحَبَلُ مِنَ الشَّرَابِ، فَإِنَّهُ يُخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلَ مَا فِي الرَّحِمِ»

records.boundary_review_note: Uqbah ibn Nafi reports Yahya ibn Said's view of a drink used to prevent pregnancy. Matn begins كَانَ يَحْيَى.

records.text_en: It reached me from Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān that he said 'Whoever makes a woman wear a bead so that she may conceive or so that she may not conceive, he said: This is from the evil and displeasing opinion of the one who acts upon it.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَبَلَغَنِي عَنْ رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ: أَنَّهُ قَالَ: " مَنْ أَلْبَسَ امْرَأَةً خَرَزَةً كَيْمَا تَحْبَلُ أَوْ كَيْمَا لَا تَحْبَلُ، قَالَ: هَذَا مِنْ رَأْيِ السُّوءِ الْمَسْخُوطِ لِمَنْ عَمِلَ بِهِ "

records.text_en: ʿUqbah ibn Nāfiʿ reported to me from Rabīʿah that he said 'There is no harm in treating with the milk of a black sheep, or black cows, or the milk of a woman in the first pregnancy.' He saw no harm in all of that.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عُقْبَةُ بْنُ نَافِعٍ، عَنْ رَبِيعَةَ، قَالَ: «لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يُعَالَجَ لَبَنُ الشَّاةِ السَّوْدَاءِ، أَوِ الْبُقُورِ السَّوْدَاءِ، أَوْ لَبَنُ الْمَرْأَةِ فِي أَوَّلِ بَطْنٍ» لَا يَرَى بِذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ بَأْسًا

records.matn_en: There is no harm in treating with the milk of a black sheep, or black cows, or the milk of a woman in the first pregnancy.' He saw no harm in all of that.
records.boundary_review_note: Rabiah gives the ruling. Matn begins لَا بَأْسَ أَنْ يُعَالَجَ.

records.text_en: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr reported to me from Ibn Jurayj, who said I asked ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ about incantations, and he disliked that except for pouring. He said: They tie knots with it. I do not know what they do. He said: Whatever you do with it, there is no harm in it.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ عَطَاءَ بْنَ أَبِي رَبَاحٍ، عَنِ النُّشْرَةِ ، وَكَرِهَ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا صَبًّا، قَالَ: يَعْقِدُونَ بِهَا، قَالَ: وَلَا أَدْرِي مَا يَصْنَعُونَ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّمَا شَيْءٍ تَصْنَعُهُ فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ

records.display_text_en: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr reported to me from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ about nushrah, a treatment used to undo magic. He disapproved of it except by pouring. He said, ‘They tie knots with it. I do not know what they do.’ He added, ‘Whatever you do, there is no harm in it.’

records.matn_ar: وَكَرِهَ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا صَبًّا، قَالَ: يَعْقِدُونَ بِهَا، قَالَ: وَلَا أَدْرِي مَا يَصْنَعُونَ، قَالَ: فَأَيُّمَا شَيْءٍ تَصْنَعُهُ فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ

records.matn_en: and he disliked that except for pouring. He said: They tie knots with it. I do not know what they do. He said: Whatever you do with it, there is no harm in it.
records.boundary_review_note: Ibn Jurayj asks Ata about nushrah; Ata's response and ensuing explanation begin وَكَرِهَ ذَلِكَ.

records.text_en: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me that he heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say: 'There is no harm in the incantation that is gathered from magic or perfume and with which a person washes, as long as it does not contain polytheism.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ يَحْيَى بْنَ سَعِيدٍ، يَقُولُ: «لَيْسَ بِالنُّشْرَةِ الَّتِي يُجْمَعُ فِيهَا مِنَ السِّحْرِ أَوِ الطِّيبِ وَيَغْتَسِلُ بِهَا الْإِنْسَانُ بَأْسٌ»
records.raw_text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ يَحْيَى بْنَ سَعِيدٍ، يَقُولُ: «لَيْسَ بِالنُّشْرَةِ الَّتِي يُجْمَعُ فِيهَا مِنَ السِّحْرِ أَوِ الطِّيبِ وَيَغْتَسِلُ بِهَا الْإِنْسَانُ بَأْسٌ»

records.raw_text_en: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me that he heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say: 'There is no harm in the incantation that is gathered from magic or perfume and with which a person washes, as long as it does not contain polytheism.'
records.display_text_en: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me that he heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say: ‘There is no harm in nushrah made by gathering [ingredients] from magic or perfume and washing with it.’
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ أَيُّوبَ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ يَحْيَى بْنَ سَعِيدٍ، يَقُولُ: «
records.matn_ar: لَيْسَ بِالنُّشْرَةِ الَّتِي يُجْمَعُ فِيهَا مِنَ السِّحْرِ أَوِ الطِّيبِ وَيَغْتَسِلُ بِهَا الْإِنْسَانُ بَأْسٌ»
records.isnad_en: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me that he heard Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd say: '
records.matn_en: There is no harm in the incantation that is gathered from magic or perfume and with which a person washes, as long as it does not contain polytheism.'
records.boundary_review_note: Yahya ibn Said states this ruling. Matn begins لَيْسَ بِالنُّشْرَةِ.

records.text_en: Hishām ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that some people said to the Messenger of God, ﷺ: 'We used to visit soothsayers in the Age of Ignorance.' He said: 'There is no good in soothsayers, so do not visit them.' They said: 'What about those who cast pebbles?' He said: 'Do not visit them.' They said: 'What about drawing lines, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'One of the prophets was taught to draw lines. Whoever matches that drawing has succeeded, otherwise, he has not.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي هِشَامُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، أَنَّ نَاسًا قَالُوا لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: إِنَّا كُنَّا نَأْتِي الْكَهَنَةَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، قَالَ: «لَا خَيْرَ فِي الْكَهَنَةِ فَلَا تَأْتُوهُمْ» ، فَقَالُوا: أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِينَ يَضْرِبُونَ بِالْحَصَا، فَقَالَ: «لَا تَأْتُوهُمْ» ، قَالُوا: أَفَرَأَيْتَ الْخَطَّ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، فَقَالَ: «إِنَّ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ عُلِّمَ الْخَطَّ فَمَنْ أَصَابَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ الْخَطِّ فَقَدْ أَصَابَ وَإِلَّا فَلَا»

records.display_text_en: Hishām ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that some people said to the Messenger of God, ﷺ: ‘In the pre-Islamic period, we used to visit soothsayers.’ He replied, ‘There is no good in soothsayers, so do not visit them.’ They asked, ‘What about those who cast pebbles?’ He said, ‘Do not visit them.’ They asked, ‘What about drawing lines, O Messenger of God?’ He said, ‘One of the prophets was taught this art of line-drawing. Whoever draws a line like his has got it right; otherwise, he has not.’

records.isnad_en: Hishām ibn Saʿd reported to me from Zayd ibn Aslam that some people said to the Messenger of God, ﷺ: 'We used to visit soothsayers in the Age of Ignorance.' He said: '
records.matn_en: There is no good in soothsayers, so do not visit them.' They said: 'What about those who cast pebbles?' He said: 'Do not visit them.' They said: 'What about drawing lines, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'One of the prophets was taught to draw lines. Whoever matches that drawing has succeeded, otherwise, he has not.'
records.boundary_review_note: The people ask the Messenger about their pre-Islamic visits to soothsayers; his answer begins لَا خَيْرَ فِي الْكَهَنَةِ. Subsequent dialogue remains matn.

records.text_en: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrate from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said 'Whoever visits a fortune-teller and asks him, his prayer will not be accepted for forty nights.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قَالَ: «مَنْ أَتَى عَرَّافًا يَسْأَلُهُ لَمْ تُقْبَلْ مِنْهُ صَلَاةٌ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً»

records.boundary_review_note: The matn begins with the Prophet's statement مَنْ أَتَى عَرَّافًا.

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd, from Kathīr ibn ʿAmr, from Nāfiʿ, from Abī Hurayrah, who said 'Whoever goes to a soothsayer and believes what he says, God will be angry with him for forty nights.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ كَثِيرِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «مَنْ ذَهَبَ إِلَى كَاهِنٍ فَصَدَّقَهُ بِمَا يَقُولُ غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً»

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd, from Wadāʿah, that he entered upon Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd, a companion of the Prophet, ﷺ, who brought him food. Faḍālah said 'Do you know what this is? A certain female slave of his had gone to a soothsayer to ask him about something, so I ordered her to fast for forty days as expiation for that. Today is the completion of that.'

Faḍālah said 'Do you know what this is? A certain female slave of his had gone to a soothsayer to ask him about something, so I ordered her to fast for forty days as expiation for that. Today is the completion of that.'
records.display_text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd, from Wadāʿah, who said: I entered upon Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd, a Companion of the Prophet, ﷺ. He brought me food and asked, ‘Do you know what this is? A certain enslaved woman who had borne him a child went to a soothsayer to ask about something. I ordered her to fast for forty days as expiation. Today completes that period.’
records.isnad_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ وَدَاعَةَ:
records.matn_ar: أَنَّهُ دَخَلَ عَلَى فَضَالَةَ بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ، صَاحِبِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فَقَرَّبَ إِلَيْهِ طَعَامًا، فَقَالَ فَضَالَةُ: «تَدْرِي مَا هَذَا؟ ، إِنَّ فُلَانَةَ أُمَّ وَلَدٍ لَهُ كَانَتْ ذَهَبَتْ إِلَى كَاهِنٍ تَسْأَلُهُ عَنْ شَيْءٍ ، فَأَمَرْتُهَا أَنْ تَصُومَ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا كَفَّارَةً لِذَلِكَ، فَالْيَوْمُ تَمَامُ ذَلِكَ»
records.isnad_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd, from Wadāʿah,
records.matn_en: that he entered upon Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd, a companion of the Prophet, ﷺ, who brought him food. Faḍālah said 'Do you know what this is? A certain female slave of his had gone to a soothsayer to ask him about something, so I ordered her to fast for forty days as expiation for that. Today is the completion of that.'
records.boundary_review_note: Wadaah narrates his visit to Fadalah; Fadalah's dialogue is matn. Matn begins أَنَّهُ دَخَلَ عَلَى فَضَالَةَ.

records.text_en: Mūsā ibn ʿUlayy reported to me from Ḥabbān ibn Abī Jablah, who said I do not know if he attributed it to the Prophet or not: 'Whoever visits a fortune-teller or a soothsayer and believes what he says is like one who disbelieves in what was revealed to Muḥammad, ﷺ.' Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim reported to me that he heard Abī Isḥāq al-Hamdānī say from Hubayrah ibn Yarīm, from Ibn Masʿūd, similarly, and he said: 'Or a sorcerer.'

records.isnad_en: Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb reported to me from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said '
records.matn_en: A people who look at the stars and write abjad (alphabetical divination) have no share in the Hereafter.'
records.boundary_review_note: Ibn Abbas's statement begins قَوْمٌ يَنْظُرُونَ.

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ, that she heard the Messenger of God, ﷺ, say: 'The angels descend in the clouds, which are the sky, and mention the matter decreed in the heavens. The devil eavesdrops and hears it, then conveys it to the soothsayers, who lie along with it a hundred lies from themselves.'

records.text_en: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr reported to me from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Shihāb, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, who said Some people asked the Messenger of God, ﷺ, about soothsayers. The Messenger of God said to them: 'They are nothing.' They said: 'O Messenger of God, sometimes they tell something that is true.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'That is a word of truth that the jinn preserve and whisper into the ear of their ally like the clinking of glass. They mix in it more than a hundred lies.'
records.text_ar: وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ سَأَلَ نَاسٌ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام عَنِ الْكُهَّانِ، فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: «لَيْسُوا بِشَيْءٍ» ، قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّهُمْ يُحَدِّثُونَ أَحْيَانًا بِالشَّيْءِ يَكُونُ حَقًّا، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «تِلْكَ الْكَلِمَةُ مِنَ الْحَقِّ، يَحْفَظُهَا الْجِنُّ، فَيُقِرُّهَا فِي أُذُنِ وَلِيِّهِ قَرَّ الزُّجَاجَةِ، فَيَخْلِطُونَ فِيهَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ مِائَةِ كِذْبَةٍ»

records.text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me from Ibn Shihāb, who said ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn informed me from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Some men from the companions of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, from the Anṣār, informed me that while they were sitting with the Messenger of God, ﷺ, a shooting star blazed. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to them: 'What did you used to say in the Age of Ignorance when something like this was shot?' They said: 'God and His Messenger know best. We used to say: A great man was born tonight, or a great man died.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'It is not shot for the death of anyone or the life of anyone. Rather, when God decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify Him, then the inhabitants of the heavens glorify Him until the glorification reaches the inhabitants of the lowest heaven. Then those near the bearers of the Throne say: What did your Lord say? They inform them of the glorification of the inhabitants of the heavens until the news reaches this lowest heaven. The jinn then snatch the hearing and convey it to their allies. What they bring forth as it is, is true, but they embellish it and add to it. God, the Exalted in praise, says: {Until, when fear is banished from their hearts, they say: What did your Lord say? They say: The truth.} [Saba: 23]' Ḥarmalah said: Bishr reported to me that al-Awzāʿī reported from al-Zuhrī similarly.
records.text_ar: قَالَ 693 - وَأَخْبَرَنِي يُونُسُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، قَالَ: وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ حُسَيْنٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي رِجَالٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ أَنَّهُمْ بَيْنَمَا هُمْ جُلُوسٌ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، رُمِيَ بِنَجْمٍ فَاسْتَنَارَ، فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «مَا كُنْتُمْ تَقُولُونَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ إِذَا رُمِيَ بِمِثْلِ هَذَا؟» ، قَالُوا: اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ، كُنَّا نَقُولُ: وُلِدَ اللَّيْلَةَ عَظِيمٌ وَمَاتَ عَظِيمٌ، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: " فَإِنَّهَا لَا يُرْمَى لِمَوْتِ أَحَدٍ وَلَا لَحَيَاةِ أَحَدٍ، وَلَكِنْ رُبَّمَا إِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا سَبَّحَ حَمَلَةُ الْعَرْشِ، ثُمَّ يُسَبِّحُ أَهْلُ السَّمَاءِ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ التَّسْبِيحُ أَهْلَ السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَ حَمَلَةَ الْعَرْشِ: مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ؟ فَيُخْبِرُونَهُمْ بِتَسْبِيحِ أَهْلِ السَّمَوَاتِ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْخَبَرُ هَذِهِ السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا ، فَيَخْطَفُ الْجِنُّ السَّمْعَ ، فَيَذْهَبُونَ بِهِ إِلَى أَوْلِيَائِهِمْ ، فَمَا جَاءُوا بِهِ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ فَهُوَ حَقٌّ، وَلَكِنَّهُمْ يَرْقُونَ فِيهِ وَيَزِيدُونَ، قَالَ اللَّهُ جَلَّ ثَنَاؤُهُ: {حَتَّى إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ قَالُوا مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ قَالُوا الْحَقَّ} [سبأ: 23] ⦗ص: 773⦘ "

records.raw_text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me from Ibn Shihāb, who said ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn informed me from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Some men from the companions of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, from the Anṣār, informed me that while they were sitting with the Messenger of God, ﷺ, a shooting star blazed. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to them: 'What did you used to say in the Age of Ignorance when something like this was shot?' They said: 'God and His Messenger know best. We used to say: A great man was born tonight, or a great man died.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'It is not shot for the death of anyone or the life of anyone. Rather, when God decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify Him, then the inhabitants of the heavens glorify Him until the glorification reaches the inhabitants of the lowest heaven. Then those near the bearers of the Throne say: What did your Lord say? They inform them of the glorification of the inhabitants of the heavens until the news reaches this lowest heaven. The jinn then snatch the hearing and convey it to their allies. What they bring forth as it is, is true, but they embellish it and add to it. God, the Exalted in praise, says: {Until, when fear is banished from their hearts, they say: What did your Lord say? They say: The truth.} [Saba: 23]' Ḥarmalah said: Bishr reported to me that al-Awzāʿī reported from al-Zuhrī similarly.

records.text_en: Yazīd ibn ʿIyāḍ reported to me from ʿAmr ibn Abī Jaʿfar, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Labībah, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, except that he said 'Then the devils eavesdrop on it and bring it to the soothsayers, adding and subtracting. The soothsayers err and hit the mark. Then God, the Mighty and Exalted, protected the sky with these stars that they sit by, and soothsaying was cut off, and there is no soothsaying.'

records.text_en: It reached me from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd that he said regarding a slave who runs away and stays without magic until the paths become obscure to him and he is prevented from relieving himself and urinating, and this becomes severe for him, so he returns to his family: 'I have seen the best of those we have met strongly dislike that and forbid it.' Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Hurmuz, the freedman of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, that... ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr. He saw the goats mounting... What is here? I did not know the beasts here were large. It was said: Yes, but they have been bewitched, so they mingle with the livestock without agitating them. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said: Small branches...'

records.text_en: Ibn Wahb said Yūnus ibn Yazīd, ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, and Ibn Samʿān reported to me that Ibn Shihāb informed them that Abū Khuzāmah, one of Banī al-Ḥārith ibn Saʿd ibn Huzaym, reported to him that his father reported to him that he said to the Messenger of God, ﷺ: 'O Messenger of God, what do you think of medicine we use, incantations we recite, and precautions we take? Do they avert anything from God’s decree?' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'They are from God’s decree.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ: أَخْبَرَنِي يُونُسُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، وَعَمْرُو بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، وَابْنُ سَمْعَانَ، أَنَّ ابْنَ شِهَابٍ أَخْبَرَهُمْ أَنَّ أَبَا خُزَامَةَ أَحَدَ بَنِي الْحَارِثِ بْنِ سَعْدِ بْنِ هَزِيمٍ حَدَّثَهُ، أَنَّ أَبَاهُ حَدَّثَهُ أَنَّهُ، قَالَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ، أَرَأَيْتَ دَوَاءً نَتَدَاوَى بِهِ ، وَرُقًى نَسْتَرْقِيهَا ، وَتُقًى نَتَّقِيهَا، هَلْ تَرُدُّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ قَدَرِ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ؟، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إِنَّهُ مِنْ قَدَرِ اللَّهِ»

records.boundary_review_note: Three parallel transmitters report through Ibn Shihab. Abu Khuzamah's unnamed father asks the Messenger; matn begins يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ.

records.text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me from Ibn Shihāb, who said It reached us from men of knowledge that they used to say: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, forbade incantations when he arrived in Medina, as incantations at that time contained much polytheistic speech. The people refrained from them when the Messenger of God, ﷺ, forbade them. Then, when a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, was stung by a thorn or struck, the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Is there anyone who can recite an incantation?' They said: 'O Messenger of God, the family of Ḥazm used to recite an incantation for snake bites, but when you forbade incantations, they abandoned it.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Call ʿUmārah ibn Ḥazm for me.' He had no children and had witnessed Badr. He was called, and the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Show me your incantation.' He showed it to him, and he saw no harm in it, so he permitted him to recite it.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يُونُسُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، قَالَ: بَلَغَنَا عَنِ الرِّجَالِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ، أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَقُولُونَ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَهَى عَنِ الرُّقَى حِينَ قَدِمَ الْمَدِينَةَ، وَكَانَتِ الرُّقَى فِي ذَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ فِيهَا كَثِيرٌ مِنْ كَلَامِ الشِّرْكِ، فَانْتَهَى النَّاسُ عَنْهَا حِينَ نَهَاهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، فَيَنْهَاهُمْ كَذَلِكَ إِذَا لُدِغَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ، عليه السلام ، بِنَشْبَةِ حَرْبَةٍ، أَوْ بِضَرْبٍ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «هَلْ مِنْ رَاقٍ» ، قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَدْ كَانَ آلُ حَزْمٍ يَرْقُونَ بِرُقْيَةٍ مِنَ الْحَيَّةِ، فَلَمَّا نَهَيْتَ عَنِ الرُّقَى تَرَكُوهَا، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ادْعُوا لِي عُمَارَةَ بْنَ حَزْمٍ» ، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلَدٌ، وَقَدْ شَهِدَ بَدْرًا، فَدُعِيَ لَهُ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «اعْرِضْ عَلَيَّ رُقْيَتَكَ» ، فَعَرَضَهَا عَلَيْهِ فَلَمْ يَرَ بِهَا بَأْسًا، فَأَذِنَ أَنْ يَرْقِيَهَا

records.raw_text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me from Ibn Shihāb, who said It reached us from men of knowledge that they used to say: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, forbade incantations when he arrived in Medina, as incantations at that time contained much polytheistic speech. The people refrained from them when the Messenger of God, ﷺ, forbade them. Then, when a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, was stung by a thorn or struck, the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Is there anyone who can recite an incantation?' They said: 'O Messenger of God, the family of Ḥazm used to recite an incantation for snake bites, but when you forbade incantations, they abandoned it.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Call ʿUmārah ibn Ḥazm for me.' He had no children and had witnessed Badr. He was called, and the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Show me your incantation.' He showed it to him, and he saw no harm in it, so he permitted him to recite it.
records.display_text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me from Ibn Shihāb, who said: It reached us from men of knowledge that they used to say the Messenger of God, ﷺ, forbade ruqyas when he arrived in Medina, since the ruqyas then contained much polytheistic speech. So people stopped using them. Later, when one of the Prophet’s Companions was pierced by a spear or struck, the Messenger of God asked, ‘Is there anyone who can recite a ruqya?’ They said, ‘O Messenger of God, the family of Ḥazm used to recite a ruqya for snakebite, but when you forbade ruqyas, they stopped.’ He said, ‘Call ʿUmārah ibn Ḥazm for me.’ He had no children and had fought at Badr. When he was brought, the Messenger of God said, ‘Show me your ruqya.’ He showed it to him, and he saw no harm in it and permitted him to recite it.

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah reported to me from Abī al-Zubayr, from Jābir, that ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm was called to a woman in Medina who had been bitten by a snake to recite an incantation for her, but he refused. The Prophet, ﷺ, was informed of this, so he called him and said 'You forbid incantations?' ʿAmr said: 'You discourage incantations.' The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'Recite it to me.' He recited it to him, and the Prophet said: 'There is no harm in it. They are covenants, so recite it.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي الزُّبَيْرِ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ، أَنَّ عَمْرَو بْنَ حَزْمٍ، دُعِيَ لِامْرَأَةٍ بِالْمَدِينَةِ لَدَغَتْهَا حَيَّةٌ لَيَرْقِيَهَا، فَأَبَى، فَأُخْبِرَ بِذَلِكَ النَّبِيُّ ، عَلَيْهِ ⦗ص: 780⦘ السَّلَامُ ، فَدَعَاهُ، فَقَالَ عَمْرٌو: إِنَّكَ تَزْجُرُ عَنِ الرُّقَى، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: «اقْرَأْهَا عَلَيَّ» ، فَقَرَأَهَا عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: «لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا، إِنَّمَا هِيَ مَوَاثِيقُ، فَارْقِ بِهَا»

records.text_en: Usāmah ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm al-Anṣārī reported to me: 'ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm presented their incantation to the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and he permitted them to recite it.'

records.boundary_review_note: Usamah ibn Zayd reports that Amr ibn Hazm presented the incantation. Matn begins عَرَضَ عَمْرُو.

records.text_en: Ibn Lahīʿah and Ibn Samʿān reported to me from Abī al-Zubayr, from Jābir, who said A man from the Anṣār came and said: 'O Messenger of God, I recite an incantation for scorpion stings.' The Prophet said: 'Whoever is able to benefit his brother, let him do so.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ لَهِيعَةَ، وَابْنُ سَمْعَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي الزُّبَيْرِ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ، قَالَ: جَاءَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْأَنْصَارِ، فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَرْقِي مِنَ الْعَقْرَبِ، فَقَالَ: «مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ أَنْ يَنْفَعَ أَخَاهُ فَلْيَفْعَلْ»

records.text_en: ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, Mālik ibn Anas, and Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me that Nāfiʿ informed them that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar 'was cauterized for facial paralysis and recited an incantation for a scorpion sting.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَحَدَّثَنِي عُمَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ، وَمَالِكُ بْنُ أَنَسٍ، وَيُونُسُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، أَنَّ نَافِعًا، أَخْبَرَهُمْ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ «اكْتَوَى مِنَ اللَّقْوَةِ، وَرُقِيَ مِنَ الْعَقْرَبِ»

narrator_path.name_en: Abd Allah ibn Umar (subject of report)

records.boundary_review_note: Four transmitters report through Nafi from Abd Allah ibn Umar. The reported practice begins اكْتَوَى مِنَ اللَّقْوَةِ.

records.text_en: Others reported to me from Nāfiʿ that Ibn ʿUmar 'recited an incantation for a scorpion sting in Persian.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي غَيْرُهُمْ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، أَنَّ ابْنَ عُمَرَ، «اسْتَرْقَى مِنَ الْعَقْرَبِ بِرُقْيَةٍ فَارِسِيَّةٍ»

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī al-Zinād reported to me from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah, who said The Messenger of God, ﷺ, used to recite this incantation when he recited: 'Remove the harm, Lord of mankind. In Your hand is healing; there is no remover of it except You.' Hishām said: ʿUrwah said: ʿĀʾishah said: I learned this incantation from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, and used to recite it for him.
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ، عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ، يَرْقِي إِذَا رَقَى فَيَقُولُ: «امْسَحِ الْبَاسَ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، بِيَدِكَ الشِّفَاءُ، لَا كَاشِفَ لَهُ إِلَّا أَنْتَ» ، قَالَ هِشَامٌ: قَالَ عُرْوَةُ: قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ: فَتَعَلَّمْتُ هَذِهِ الرُّقْيَةَ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، فَكُنْتُ أَرْقِيهِ بِهَا

records.text_en: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Salmān reported to me from Ibn..., from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḥakam ibn Thawbān, that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, when... the Messenger of God, ﷺ, used to say: 'In the name of God, O God, Lord of mankind, King of mankind, God of mankind... the Healer. records.text_en: Ibn al-Hād reported to me: Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm reported to me from Abī Salamah, from ʿĀʾishah, who also used to say: The Messenger of God, ﷺ, when he was ill, Jibrīl would recite for him: 'In the name of God, may He cure you, from every illness may He heal you, from the evil of an envier when he envies, and from the evil of every eye.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ الْهَادِ: وَحَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، أَيْضًا، كَانَتْ تَقُولُ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ عليه السلام ، إِذَا اشْتَكَى رَقَاهُ جِبْرِيلُ، قَالَ: «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ يُبْرِيكَ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ دَاءٍ يَشْفِيكَ، وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ، وَمِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ ذِي عَيْنٍ»

records.matn_ar: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يَقُولُ: «أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ»
records.isnad_en: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith reported to me from ʿAbd... al-Akbar
records.matn_en: that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, used to say: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from every devil and harmful creature, and from every evil eye.'
records.boundary_review_note: The transmitter's name is incomplete in the source (Abd... al-Akbar); it remains unresolved. Matn begins أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ كَانَ يَقُولُ.

records.text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd reported to me from Ibn Shihāb, who said It reached us that the Messenger of God, ﷺ, said to al-Shifāʾ bint ʿAbd Allāh, the grandmother of Abī Bakr ibn Sulaymān ibn Abī Ḥathmah: 'Will you not teach this one'—meaning his wife Ḥafṣah—'the incantation for ant bites, as you taught her writing?'
records.text_ar: قَالَ 712 - وَأَخْبَرَنِي يُونُسُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، قَالَ: بَلَغَنَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عليه السلام قَالَ للِشِّفَاءِ ابْنَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ، وَهِيَ جَدَّةُ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ ⦗ص: 790⦘ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ أَبِي حَثْمَةَ: «أَلَا تُعَلِّمِينَ هَذِهِ ، يُرِيدُ حَفْصَةَ زَوْجَتَهُ، رُقْيَةَ النَّمْلَةِ كَمَا عَلَّمْتِهَا الْكِتَابَةَ؟» ⦗ص: 791⦘ قَالَ:

records.text_ar: 713 - وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي مَعْشَرٍ، عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ سُلَيْمٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَاءَهُ. . . عَنْ ثَلَاثَةِ أَشْيَاءَ لَا يَعْلَمُهَا إِلَّا نَبِيٌّ، قَالَ: ثُمَّ جَعَلُوا يَتَجَرَّعُونَ لَهُ، يَقُولُونَ لَهُ:. . . أَنْفُهُ. . .، حَسَنٌ عُنُقُهُ، يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُصِيبُوهُ بِالْعَيْنِ، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَى نَبِيِّهِ {قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ} [الناس: 1]

records.display_text_en: Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd reported to me from Abū Maʿshar, from Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym, that the Messenger of God came to him … concerning three things known only to a prophet. They then began whispering to him, saying to him … his nose … his neck is handsome. They wanted to afflict him with the evil eye, so God revealed to His Prophet: “Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind” [Qur’an 114:1].

records.text_en: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ reported to me from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī, who said We used to recite incantations in the Age of Ignorance, so we said: 'O Messenger of God, what do you think of that?' He said: 'Present your incantations to me. There is no harm in incantations as long as there is no polytheism in them.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ صَالِحِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنْ عَوْفِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ الْأَشْجَعِيِّ، قَالَ: كُنَّا نَرْقِي فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَقُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ، كَيْفَ تَرَى فِي ذَلِكَ؟ فَقَالَ: «اعْرِضُوا عَلَيَّ رُقَاكُمْ، لَا بَأْسَ بِالرُّقَى مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ شِرْكٌ»

records.text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd and Ibn Samʿān reported to me that Ibn Shihāb informed them from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ, that the Messenger of God 'when he was ill, would recite the Muʿawwidhāt (the last three chapters of the Qur’an) over himself and blow. She said When his pain intensified, I would recite over him and wipe him with his hand, seeking its blessing.'
records.text_ar: قَالَ وَأَخْبَرَنِي يُونُسُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ، وَابْنُ سَمْعَانَ، أَنَّ ابْنَ شِهَابٍ، أَخْبَرَهُ ⦗ص: 793⦘ ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ " كَانَ إِذَا اشْتَكَى يَقْرَأُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بِالْمُعَوِّذَاتِ وَيَنْفُثُ، قَالَتْ: فَلَمَّا اشْتَدَّ وَجَعُهُ كُنْتُ أَقْرَأُ عَلَيْهِ، وَأَمْسَحُ عَلَيْهِ بِيَدِهِ رَجَاءَ بَرَكَتِهَا "

records.raw_text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd and Ibn Samʿān reported to me that Ibn Shihāb informed them from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet, ﷺ, that the Messenger of God 'when he was ill, would recite the Muʿawwidhāt (the last three chapters of the Qur’an) over himself and blow. She said When his pain intensified, I would recite over him and wipe him with his hand, seeking its blessing.'
records.display_text_en: Yūnus ibn Yazīd and Ibn Samʿān reported to me that Ibn Shihāb informed them from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah, the Prophet’s wife, that the Messenger of God, when ill, would recite the Muʿawwidhāt (protective sūras) over himself and blow. She said: ‘When his pain became severe, I would recite over him and wipe him with his hand, seeking its blessing.’

records.boundary_review_note: Yunus and Ibn Saman are parallel transmitters through Ibn Shihab. Matn begins with Aishah's account of the Prophet's illness and recitation; the quotation mark in the Arabic source is retained.

records.text_en: Makhramah ibn Bukayr... Ṣāliḥ, the freedman of the family of..., reported to me that a group of Bedouins, among whom was a sick man, said to them: Is there anyone among you who can treat him? So they recited upon him with verses of the Qur’an and the Muʿawwidhāt from the sheep. They went to the Prophet, ﷺ, and informed him. The Messenger of God, ﷺ, said: 'They are the reciters, and they are an incantation.' Ibn Samʿān reported to us... from the Messenger of God, ﷺ, similarly, except that he said: 'He recited...'
